### Map dot colours, wave 27: a TRAVEL-PERMIT refusal leaves the system BLUE (2026-11-25)

**Question** (wave-25 leftover): a refusal that is not MinStatus.

**Rig** (`wave27Resources` "M"). gövt 298 Kit Permit Owner, **Require
0x1** (the kit hulls and outfits contribute nothing, so every port of the
govt refuses the player), owns sÿst 1208 Kit Map Permit (-820,-1920; port
spöb 1613, MinStatus -32767), a hyperspace neighbour of Kit Gate N1. The
Kit Lancer at record 0 everywhere. Runs `permit` (Enter Ship beside the
permit port: `l`, then the map) and `permit_map` (the map from N1).

- `l` at the port: **"Landing request denied."** (the stock line, as for a
  MinStatus refusal).
- The map from N1: Kit Map Permit is **#0000ff BLUE** (20 px of the ring;
  #ff6300 would be orange); "Government: Kit Permit Owner", "Legal Status:
  No Record", "Goods Traded: None", "Services: None Available", "Ports: Kit
  Map Permit Port".

So the map's orange / red is the MinStatus (record) refusal only: a port
that turns the player away for a missing permit does not colour the dot.

**NovaJS (main c0129eaa).** `N/spaceport/starmap.ts:91-125`
`refusingSystems` asks the whole landing clearance (`stellarClearanceWith`:
MinStatus, travel permit, ränk 0x0200, bribes, mission destinations), and
`N/spaceport/starmap_draw.ts:186-188` says "GUESS: a refusal for another
reason (a travel permit, ränk 0x0200) follows the same record rule":
**mismatch** for the permit (orange in NovaJS, blue in the original).
**Proposed:** colour a system orange / red only when every port refuses
on the MinStatus / record test (the permit no longer counts); mark the
permit part MEASURED and keep the ränk 0x0200 / bribe parts as GUESSES (an
override that lets the player land should still un-colour it: unmeasured).

Confidence: high (one clean read; the colour is unambiguous).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261125-w27/permit/*/` (`02-l1.png`, `04-map.png`), `permit_map/*/` (`02-map.png`, `03-map_permit.png`).

**Applied (wave-27 fixes, 2026-11-25, `N/spaceport/starmap.ts`
`refusingSystems`, `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts`
`stellarClearanceWith`, `N/nova_plugin/reputation/stellar_clearance.ts`
`planetClearance`).** The map asks the landing clearance with the new
`ignoreTravelPermit`, so a port that refuses only for an unmet gövt
Require leaves the dot blue; a port that ALSO fails MinStatus still
colours it. The landing gate is unchanged ("Landing request denied.").
The GUESS in `N/spaceport/starmap_draw.ts` is now marked measured for the
permit; the ränk 0x0200 / bribe / mission-destination overrides stay
GUESSES. A fresh stock pilot's 35 coloured systems are unchanged (the
stock-data spec passes as it was).

### Plunder self-destruct blast, wave 27: 25.5 + 0.037 x the hulk's mass from 100 t up (nothing from 50 t), to the shield and then the armor in full; repeatable to the pixel; the floor IS the boarder's disable threshold (a 10% hull went to 30%) (2026-11-25)

**Questions** (hub queue and wave-26 leftovers): the blast's mass curve
between 50 and 5,000 t (NovaJS: 0.03 a ton to shield and armor, a 34%
armor floor); whether the floor is exactly the disable threshold.

**Rig** (`wave27Resources` "P"). Wave 26's set-up (`scenarios/w27_plunder_live.json`
= wave 26's with **Cargo clicked first**, the likeliest trip, then Credits,
Energy, Abort): live immobile pointer hulks (AI 4 of gövt 363, 300 armor,
DeathDelay 10) of **100 / 200 / 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 t** (shïp 535 / 534 /
529 / 530 / 531, sÿst 1213 / 1212 / 1209-1211), boarded by shïp 528 Kit
Ring Crawler Tough (100 shield / 3000 armor, no recharge: the shield bar
is about 1.48 px a point) or shïp 532 Kit Ring Crawler Fragile **Ten**
(100 / 300 with shïp **Flags 0x0010**, "disabled at 10% armor instead of
33%") against wave 26's 5,000 t Heavy Quick (sÿst 1202). Bars frame by
frame from each click (`tools/droptime.sh`, `tools/tripsum.sh`); in every
run the boarder sat 5-10 px from the hulk at the trip (`tools/tripframes.sh`).

| run | hulk | boarder | tripped take | after the trip (+0.30-0.37 s) | blast |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pd_100, pd_100b | 100 t | Tough | Cargo; Energy (Cargo and Credits taken first) | shield 148 -> **106** px, both runs | **28.4** |
| pd_200 | 200 t | Tough | Cargo | shield 148 -> **100** px | **32.4** |
| pd_200b | 200 t | Tough | none (Cargo, Credits, Energy all taken) | - | - |
| pd_500, pd_500b | 500 t | Tough | Cargo, Cargo | shield 148 -> **82** px, both runs | **44.6** |
| pd_1000, pd_1000b | 1,000 t | Tough | Credits, Credits (Cargo taken first both times) | shield 148 -> **54** px, both runs | **63.5** |
| pd_2000, pd_2000b | 2,000 t | Tough | Cargo, Cargo | shield **0**, armor 151 -> **146** px, both runs | 100 shield + **about 100 armor** (±20: 20 armor a px) |
| pd_ten | 5,000 t | Fragile **Ten** | Credits | shield **0**, armor 151 -> **45** px (**about 89 of 300, 29.7%**) | 100 shield + **211** armor (±2) |
| wave 26 pd_tough | 30,000 t | Tough | Credits | shield 0, armor about 1,845 | 100 + **about 1,155** (±20) |
| wave 26 pd_live2 | 50 t | Fragile | Credits | **no change** (re-read frame by frame) | **0** |

**Findings.**
1. **Deterministic.** Every repeat landed on the same pixel (500, 1,000,
   2,000 t twice each): no random part.
2. **The amount** fits one straight line from 100 t to 30,000 t: a
   least-squares fit to the five exact points (100-5,000 t) gives
   **blast = 25.5 + 0.0371 x mass** (100 t: 29.2 predicted / 28.4
   measured; 200: 32.9 / 32.4; 500: 44.0 / 44.6; 1,000: 62.6 / 63.5;
   5,000: 210.8 / 210.6; and the coarse points 2,000: 99.6 / about 100,
   30,000: 1,137 / about 1,155), every point within about one point. The same amount hits
   the shield and, once the shield is gone, the armor IN FULL (the
   2,000 t, 5,000 t and 30,000 t armor losses are the whole amount, not the
   part left over by the shield), as NovaJS's own hit rule does.
3. **50 t does nothing** (the line predicts 27, about 40 px of the
   Fragile's shield bar; re-read frame by frame), with the hulk exploding
   about 5 px from the boarder, while 100 t does the full 28. So there is
   a cut-off between 50 and 100 t. GUESS: under 100 t, the Bible's
   smallest Mass band ("1-99: 1 day per jump, small blip"); or a blast
   radius "proportional to its mass" (the Bible's Mass entry) that does not
   reach a boarder 5 px out.
4. **The floor is the boarder's disable threshold**: the Fragile (33%)
   stopped at 33.8% from 5,000 t and 30,000 t (wave 26), the Fragile Ten
   (0x0010, 10%) went on to **29.7%** from the same 5,000 t hulk: the
   whole 211, not floored at a third.
5. Take counts (one draw each, this wave): Cargo 6 trips in 11, Credits
   3 in 5, Energy 1 in 2. With waves 25-26: Cargo 18 in 28 (0.64),
   Credits 9 in 26 (0.35), Energy 3 in 7.

**NovaJS (main c0129eaa).** `N/nova_plugin/ship/ship_explosion.ts:92`
`SHIP_EXPLOSION_DAMAGE_PER_TON = 0.03` (a TUNABLE, "calibrated against the
stock mass range", `:82-91`), `shipExplosionDamage` `:159-170` (that amount
to shield and to armor); `N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:93-104` (a
hit that breaks the shield lands its armor damage in full) and the floor
`nonLethalArmorFloor` `ship_explosion.ts:187-194` (the hull's
`disableArmorFraction`, 0x0010 honoured, + 1%).
- 2: **mismatch** in the amount: 0.03 x mass gives 3 / 6 / 15 / 30 / 60 /
  150 / 900 at 100 / 200 / 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 30,000 t against
  the measured 28 / 32 / 45 / 63 / about 100 / 211 / about 1,155. The shield-then-armor-in-full
  rule **matches**.
- 3: NovaJS gives 50 t 1.5 (its 20 px minimum radius reaches the boarder):
  **small mismatch** (measured none).
- 4: **matches** (the floor follows `disableArmorFraction`; the 1% margin
  sits inside the bar's resolution).
**Proposed:** `shipExplosionDamage` = 25.5 + 0.037 x mass (shield and armor
alike) from 100 t, none below 100 t (GUESS on the cut-off: measured

**Findings.**
1. **The cut-off is a mass rule at 100 t, not a reach.** A 99 t hulk's
   trip did nothing with the boarder overlapping it (about 4 px), a 90 t

   boarder took 148 -> 54 px off the shield, exactly the 1,000 t plunder

   larger coordinate every hit is inside and every miss outside:

   **1,000 t: hits up to 113, misses from 157** (113-157). Both brackets

**Proposed:** make the ship explosion's hurtbox an axis-aligned square

| 2,000 t **big WRECK** | 210 | 149 / 151 | miss | |

**Findings.**
1. **No cap.** The reach keeps growing to 10,000 t: hits at 400 px (5,000
   t) and 760 px (10,000 t), far past NovaJS's old 200 px cap. Each
   bracket holds twice the blast's damage (25.5 + 0.037 x mass):
   **2,000 t: (190, 210)**, 2 x 99.5 = 199; **5,000 t: (400, 440)**, 2 x
   210.5 = 421; **10,000 t: (760, 820)**, 2 x 395.5 = 791. With wave 28's
   100 t (55.3, 60.2) and 1,000 t (113, 157), five masses over two decades
   agree with **half-side = 2 x (25.5 + 0.037 x mass) = 51 + 0.074 x
   mass**; a straight line through the brackets needs a slope between
   0.069 and 0.079 a ton (2,000 and 10,000 t alone), so the factor 2 is
   good to about 5%.
2. **The damage** is the formula's at every distance inside: 2,000 t shield
   0 + 5 px of armor (about 100), 5,000 t 0 + 11 px (about 218; 210.5),
   10,000 t 0 + 20 px (about 397; 395.5). No falloff (as wave 28).
3. **DeathDelay 60 changes nothing but the timing**: the 5,000 t DD-60
   wreck hit at 380 and missed at 470 exactly like the DD-10 one, for the
   same 0 / 140 px. Its blast landed 1.17 s after the Space press against
   0.27 s for DD 10 (50 DeathDelay frames in 0.90 s, about 18 ms a frame).
   The "huge explosion" is the picture only.
4. **Centre to centre, on both sides.** The Big Boarder (the Tough's
   numbers with the stock Fed Carrier's art) was NOT hit by the 2,000 t
   wreck at 230 or 210 px, though its hull reached to about 180 / 152 px
   from the wreck, well inside the 199 px half-side; and a 2,000 t wreck
   with the Fed Carrier's art (shïp 544, by mïsn 1127) did not hit the 24
   px boarder at 230 or 210 px though its own side came within about 192 /
   172 px. Hull sizes play no part, the wreck's or the victim's.
5. Every kill past 230 px was off screen. The target panel read "No Target"
   at once after the beam (a 2,100-armor beam on a 300-armor hulk), on hits
   and misses alike, and the radar showed the hulk on the marker's dot
   before it (12-13 radar px out at 380).

**NovaJS (main 594aa038).** `N/nova_plugin/ship/ship_explosion.ts:144`
`SHIP_EXPLOSION_REACH_PER_DAMAGE = 2`, `shipExplosionReach` `:156-160`
(2 x (25.5 + 0.037 x mass), no cap), `insideShipExplosion` `:167-170`
(max(\|dx\|, \|dy\|) <= reach); `N/nova_plugin/combat/ship_explosion_plugin.ts:96-110`
(the axis-aligned square hurtbox), `N/nova_plugin/combat/blast_plugin.ts:43`
(only victims whose CENTRE is inside). 1: **matches** (every row of the
table, 18 of 18: 199 / 421 / 791 sit inside the three brackets). 2:
**matches** (unchanged formula). 3: **matches** (the damage and reach do not
look at DeathDelay; the fireball graphic `finalFireballRadius` `:216-223`
is display only). 4: **matches** for the victim (the centre test); the wreck's art never
enters NovaJS's square either (centred on the wreck's position): matches. The comments at
`ship_explosion.ts:131-143` ("GUESS on the FORM (two masses only ...)",
"NO CAP: whether the original caps it is unmeasured") are now out of date.
**Proposed:** comments only. Mark the form and the missing cap MEASURED
(five masses, 100-10,000 t, this section), keep the factor 2, and note the
centre-to-centre rule as measured on both sides (this section's big
hulls). Nothing to
change in the code.

Confidence: high for "no cap" and the factor 2 within about 5% (fourteen

250 px, #74 "energized" vs #75 "online" (GUESS: #75 for an already-open

**Findings.**
1. **The selection radius is 498-500 px** (498 selected, wave 29's 500
   not), and **coasting at about 50 px/s does not change it**: inbound the
   selection came between 506 and 494.5 px, outbound 522 px gave nothing

2. **The clearance zone is a SQUARE of half-side between 248 and 250
   px, the same for a 72 px gate**: the 150 px gate cleared at 248 on the
   axis and at the (180, 180) diagonal (255 px away, so not a circle), and

   clearance zone that finds the gate uncleared says "too far" (wave 29's
   second press at 250), and the clearance zone is a fixed 250 (half the
   selection radius?), not frame-based.
3. **A standing request is cleared AUTOMATICALLY**: after the selecting
   press outside the zone, the ship that coasts into the zone is told
   "Cleared for hypergate entry, <ship>." (#91) and the gate opens, with no
   `l` (frame 1237 of `mv_toward1`; the last press was 2.5 s earlier).
4. **#74 / #75 is a draw**, not the gate's state: "online" four times and
   "energized" four times here (300-498 px, two of them coasting), every
   gate closed and no other ship in the system; 300 px said "energized" in
   wave 29 and "online" here. Over waves 28-30: energized 12, online 5. The
   ship's name was added in 7 of 8 here.
5. **An idle gate IS drawn**, as its small grey closed sprite: wave 29's
   `gate_150/02-start.png` shows it 150 px from the ship, and every gate
   shot here shows it before the press (`gate_246`, `mv_toward1` frame
   1225 at about 250 px). Wave 24's "not drawn" was a misreading: there the
   player started ON the gate, and the grey "ship" at the centre of
   `gate_c2/01-space.png` is the closed gate with the Kit Lancer's
   yellow / blue showing between its struts (`sheet_w24_centre.png`).
   **On the radar** every gate, idle (150-594 px, waves 29-30) or open
   (150 / 200 px after the clearance), is a 2 x 2 #808080 dot.

**NovaJS (main 059ce1e2, e04f0f9c applied wave 29).**
`N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts:271` `HYPERGATE_SELECT_RANGE =
500` (skip at `distance >= 500`, `:696-703`): 1 **matches** (498 in, 500
out; distance only, so speed is ignored as on the original). 2:
**mismatch**: the entry window is `stellarLandingRange` (`:757-762`,

where the original clears at 248 and on the 255 px diagonal and enters
there too; NovaJS also has a single zone for both steps, where the
original clears a 72 px gate out to at least 230 px but lets it be

**mismatch**: `attempt` (`:646-654`) and the comment at `:741-745` clear a requested gate only when the
player presses `l` inside the window ("entering the window and pressing
`l` clears the gate"); the original clears a standing request on entry.
4: **mismatch**: `online` (`:764-783`) is set only when another ship holds
a clearance at that gate (GUESS), and `landingRequestMessage`
(`N/display/status_bar_content.ts:459-478`) prints #75 only then; the
original drew #75 in 5 of 17 selections with no other ship.
5: **mismatch** for the sprite: `gateDrawn`
(`N/display/gate_animation_plugin.ts:161-169`, used at `:326`) hides a
closed gate, on the wave-24 misreading quoted in the module comment
(`:35-46`); the radar (`N/display/status_bar_radar.ts:247-264`, a station
is a dot) **matches**.
**Proposed:** (a) split a hypergate's two steps: the CLEARANCE (the
selecting press, and the automatic one of (b)) inside a square of
half-side 249 whatever the art (GUESS in 248-250), the ENTRY (the press
that opens the gate map) inside the art's `landingRange` without the 212
cap for gates (1.7 W: 255 for the stock 150 px gates; GUESS that the cap
is a planet's only); a cleared ship outside the entry window keeps the
"too far" line; (b) when a
ship holds a gate REQUEST (selected outside the window, not yet cleared),
clear it as soon as it is inside the window (the clearance line #91-93 and
the opening), without a press; (c) pick #74 / #75 by a draw like the

"energized"), and drop the `online` = another ship's clearance rule;
(d) draw the idle gate (its closed frame 0) again: delete `gateDrawn`'s

the opening seen), 4 and 5; medium for 2's split into two zones (two

### Capture odds, wave 31: the odds shown are DRAWN per board (the same hulk, the same seven hits read 10-17%); the hulk's damage plays no part; crew 50 averages 12% over 13 boards, crew 40 about 10%, crew 20 about 16% (2026-11-25)

**Question** (brief item 3): wave 30 read 8 / 15 / 7 / 10 / 11% against one
crew-50 hulk with the same boarder (NovaJS 5.6%). What do the odds depend
on: the boarder's crew or strength, a random roll per board, the hulk's
damage when it was disabled?

**Rig.** Wave 30's live immobile hulks (AI 4 of gövt 363, 300 armor, no
shield, 50 t: shïp 546 Kit Hulk Crew 50 in sÿst 1275, and wave 8's Kit Live
Pointer Crew 20 / 40, shïp 831 / 833 in sÿst 2040 / 2042), the only
traffic of their systems; the boarder always the Kit Ring Crawler Tough
(crew 10, no marines) with the Kit Escort Gun turret (30 armor a hit,
reload 20 frames). **Controlled damage:** `scenarios/w31_plunder_crew7.json`
/ `w31_plunder_crew9.json` replace wave 30's 5 s hold with exactly 7 (or
9) single taps 900 ms apart at 150 px: 7 hits leave 90 armor (30%, the
first hit count that disables: the panel read "Disabled" after the taps in
every run), 9 hits 30 armor (10%); then board, read the dialog, Abort.
`tools/odds.sh` crops each dialog (the shot BEFORE the Abort click).

| hulk crew (ratio 10 / crew) | damage | Capture Odds per board |
|---|---|---|
| 50 (0.2) | 7 hits (90 armor) | 11, 17, 13, 10, 14 |
| 50 (0.2) | 9 hits (30 armor) | 14, 11, 15 |
| 50 (0.2) | wave 30, a 5 s hold | 8, 15, 7, 10, 11 |
| 40 (0.25) | 7 hits | 11, 12 (a third run lost the hulk: "target not found") |
| 20 (0.5) | 7 hits | 12, 17, 16 |

(The dialog's Cargo 26-49 t and Energy 30-2,680 of the same hulk vary as
much, and track neither each other nor the odds.)

**Findings.**
1. **The odds are drawn per board**: the same hulk, boarder and seven hits
   read 11, 17, 13, 10 and 14%. Nothing in the rig differed between those
   runs, so the shown odds carry a random part (spread about 7 points).
2. **The hulk's damage does not enter**: seven hits (30% armor) averaged
   13.0%, nine hits (10% armor) 13.3%; wave 8's 7 / 8 / 9 shots against crew
   20 agree (17, 18, 17).
3. **The crew ratio still matters, weakly in this range**: crew 50 (13
   boards) 7-17, mean 12.0; crew 40 (two boards here + wave 8's 7) 7-12,
   mean 10; crew 20 (three here + wave 8's three) 12-18, mean 16.2. Against
   wave 8's crew 1 (75%), 5 (34%), 10 (20%), 15 (18%) the curve is steep
   below a ratio of 1 and nearly flat from 0.5 to 0.2. The boarder's
   strength was not varied (one boarder throughout).

**NovaJS (main 2f13864f).** `captureChance`
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/boarding_component.ts:706-726`) interpolates
`CAPTURE_ODDS_BY_CREW_RATIO` (`:689-698`: [0.25, 0.07], [0.5, 0.175]; 5.6% at 0.2) with
no random part, and its comment (`:678`) reads "The hulk's damage plays no part
... and nothing else enters here either". 1: **mismatch** (a fixed value
per crew ratio where the original draws one per board). 2: **matches**.
3: **mismatch** in level: 5.6% at 0.2 and 7% at 0.25 against means of 12%
and about 10%.
**Proposed:** (a) re-fit the low end on the means: [0.2, 0.12],
[0.25, 0.11] (GUESS: the 0.25 cell's three boards are too few to keep
it below 0.2's), [0.5, 0.165]; extend the table's left end so ratio 0
stays 0 (the 1% floor still applies); (b) if the dialog should show the
spread, draw the shown odds per board as the table value +-5 points
(uniform, GUESS from the 7-17 spread at 0.2, 12-18 at 0.5), from the
board's seeded draw so every peer shows the same number, and roll the
capture against the SHOWN value (the original's success rate against
its shown odds is unmeasured: GUESS). A mean-only model is the simpler
change and keeps the capture rate right on average.

Confidence: medium for 1 and 2 (16 boards here, identical inputs), low
for the exact means (two to thirteen boards a cell).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261125-w31/pc7_*/`,
`pc9_*/`, `c20_*/`, `c40_*/` (the `*-b-NN.png` shot with the dialog,
`*-fired-*.png` "Disabled"), `odds_a.png` .. `odds_f.png`, `w30_crew_odds.png`
(wave 30's five dialogs re-read).

**Applied (wave-31 fixes, 2026-11-25, 2831b75e).** (a) and (b), with one
change to (a). `N/nova_plugin/ship/boarding_component.ts`
`CAPTURE_ODDS_BY_CREW_RATIO` now reads [0, 0], [0.2, 0.12], [0.25, 0.12],
[0.5, 0.165], then wave 8's points as before: 0.25 is held at 0.2's 12%
rather than the proposed 11%, because its three boards cannot show a dip
and a dip would make more crew LOWER the odds (the table's monotonicity
spec). (b) `boardCaptureOdds` draws each board's odds as a whole percent:
the table's mean (rounded) plus an even draw of whole points in [-5, +5]
(GUESS: uniform, symmetric so the mean stays the table's), narrowed so a
board never reads above the 75% cap or below the 1% floor (every crew-1
board here read 75%). The draw is a hash salted with the boarder, the
victim and the board's one seeded money draw (`captureOddsDraw`,
`N/nova_plugin/encounters/boarding_plugin.ts`), frozen as the session

against its shown odds is unmeasured). Schema-only under protocol 8
(wire fingerprint d442dd55b4b6c6ec -> 7fd7a35565bd9f25).

### Landing clearance lapse, wave 32: a port's clearance lapses SILENTLY 24.5-24.6 s after it was given (landed at 24.32 and 24.51 s, fresh clearances at 24.61 s and above); a hypergate's clearance lapses too, at the same time (held at 23.5 s, lapsed at 25.5 s); nothing stands after a lapse, so coming back into the zone does not re-clear (2026-11-25)

**Questions** (brief item 1; wave-31 leftover): the exact lapse time of a
planet / station clearance (13.4-25.1 s so far), what the player sees when
it lapses, whether a GATE clearance lapses too, and whether a ship that
left the zone and comes back is re-cleared automatically.

**Rig.** Wave 31's Kit Land P250 230 (the Kit Lancer at rest on a
decoration 230 px from a 250 px port: inside the 249 clearance square and
the 1.7 W = 425 landing window). `tools/lapse.sh`: `l` clears, then each
next `l` comes about T s after the one before; a press that lands ends the
cascade, a press that does not got a fresh clearance (the old one had
lapsed), which restarts the clock. `tools/oneshot.sh` sends the whole
cascade as ONE keys step (exact intervals; `l` in the spaceport is
harmless). The press intervals are read from the recording's frame-stamped
events and the status line from `tools/sl_changes.mjs`. Gates: Kit Gate
J325 245 (the 325 px art: a cleared press opens the gate map anywhere
inside 552). Away and back: the Kit Ring Crawler Tough at rest 230 px west
of the same port (`tools/awayback.sh`).

| run | from the clearance to the next `l` | the next `l` |
|---|---|---|
| lapse_a | 26.36 s | a fresh clearance ("You are cleared to land. Welcome to Kit Land P250 230.") |
| lapse_a | 24.32 s | **LANDED** |
| lapse_b | 25.92, 25.56, 25.45, 25.17, 24.85, **24.74** s | a fresh clearance every time (six, the #97-99 / #100-101 forms drawn) |
| lapse_c (one keys step) | 24.71, **24.61** s | a fresh clearance each |
| lapse_c | **24.51** s | **LANDED** (the spaceport 0.2 s after the press) |
| gate_lapse40 (gate) | 46.10 s | **a fresh clearance** ("Cleared for hypergate entry, w31-gate-j325-245."), no gate map |
| gate_l235 (gate) | 23.51 s | **the gate map** (still cleared) |
| gate_l255 (gate) | 25.52 s | a fresh clearance ("Cleared for hypergate entry, w31-gate-j325-245.") |
| awayback1 | 68.4 s (out to 359 px for about 45 s, back in to 208 px about 12 s before the press) | a fresh clearance ("w31-walk-p250, you're cleared to land. Welcome to Kit Land P250 230."); NOTHING printed on the way back in |

**Findings.**
1. **A port's clearance lapses 24.5-24.6 s after it was given**: it held
   at 24.32 and 24.51 s and had lapsed at 24.61, 24.71, 24.74 s and every
   longer interval (nine presses). Wave 31's 13.4 s and shorter held,
   its 25.1 and 26.5 s lapsed: all consistent.
2. **The lapse is SILENT**: the status line stayed dark for the whole wait
   in every run (20-63 s), and the nav panel still names the port
   afterwards (the selection is kept); only the next press shows it, with a
   fresh clearance inside the zone (or a fresh request outside it, wave
   31's walk-outs).
3. **A hypergate's clearance lapses too, on the same clock**: a press
   23.5 s after the clearance opened the gate map, one 25.5 s after (and
   one 46.1 s after) got a fresh clearance instead. (Wave 29's gate
   REQUEST that held 41 s was a request, not a clearance.)
4. **Nothing stands after a lapse**: the ship that let its clearance
   lapse 359 px out and came back to 208 px crossed the 249 square with no
   line (wave 31: a standing REQUEST is cleared there), and its press got
   a fresh clearance, not a landing. So the lapse drops the clearance and
   leaves no request behind; only a new press (or a request made after it)
   counts.

**NovaJS (main 1d398457, which applied wave 31's clearance).**
`N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts`: `STELLAR_CLEARANCE_MS = 20_000`
(`:387`, GUESS "20 s inside the bracket") sets `clearedUntil` for a port's
or station's clearance (`:1076`); a gate's clearance has none and "never
lapses (unmeasured for gates)" (`:86-89`). 1: **mismatch** (20 s against
24.5-24.6 s: a press 20-24.5 s after a clearance lands in the original and
is answered with a fresh clearance in NovaJS). 2: **matches** (a lapse is only a time test, `clearanceLapsed` `:141-148`, with no event, and the selection is kept). 3:
**mismatch** (gates never lapse). 4: **matches** (`grantClearance` drops `requested`, `:1070`, so `StellarAutoClearanceSystem` (`:1110`) has nothing to answer on the way back in, as its comment says at `:1096-1097`).
**Proposed:** `STELLAR_CLEARANCE_MS = 24_550` (MEASURED between 24.51 and
24.61 s; GUESS the middle), and give a GATE clearance the same
`clearedUntil` (grantClearance's hypergate branch, `:1072-1074`, sets it too, and
`holdsGateClearance`, `:133-138`, which today requires NO `clearedUntil`, honours the time like `holdsClearance`: the gate then closes
as for any lost clearance, GUESS on the closing animation); comments at `:86-89` and `:378-386` to
cite this section.

Confidence: high for 1 and 4 (nine lapsed presses and two holds read
from frame stamps; one away-and-back run, clear-cut), medium for 3 (three gate presses, one bracket of 2 s).

### Capture odds at crew ratio 1 and above, wave 32: 18-22% at 1, 29-34% at 2 (two crew pairs alike at each), 55-64% at 5, 75% every time at 10; every board within 5 points of its ratio's mean (2026-11-25)

**Question** (brief item 2; wave-31 leftover): the capture odds at crew
ratios (boarder crew / victim crew) of 1 and above, several boards each,
so the upper table and the per-board spread are measured, and whether
the spread is the same at every ratio.

**Rig.** Wave 8's live immobile hulks (AI 4 of gövt 363, 300 armor, the
pointer art) with crew 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 (sÿst/spöb 2039 / 2043 / 2044 /
2040), each the only traffic of its system; the boarder wave 26's Kit
Ring Crawler Tough (crew 10) and two copies with crew 20 / 50
(`wave32Resources`: shïp 548 / 549), the Kit Escort Gun turret, no
marines. `scenarios/w31_plunder_crew7.json` (7 single taps at 150 px, so
every hulk is disabled with 90 armor left), board, read the dialog,
Abort; `tools/odds.sh` crops each dialog (the shot before the Abort).

| boarder crew vs hulk crew | ratio | Capture Odds per board | wave 8 (one board) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 vs 10 | 1 | 18, 22, 18 | 20 |
| 20 vs 20 | 1 | 18, 18, 22 | - |
| 10 vs 5 | 2 | 32, 32, 31 | 34 |
| 20 vs 10 | 2 | 34, 30, 29 | - |
| 50 vs 10 | 5 | 59, 64, 61, 55 | - |
| 10 vs 1 | 10 | 75, 75, 75 | 75 |

(Cargo 25-47 t and Energy 180-2,860 of the same hulks vary as before and
track nothing.)

**Findings.**
1. **The upper table**: ratio 1 averages about 19% (six boards, both
   crew pairs; wave 8's 20%), ratio 2 about 31% (six boards, both crew pairs:
   31.3; wave 8's 34), ratio 5 about 60% (four boards: 59.8), ratio 10 the 75% cap on every board.
2. **The ratio is what counts, not the crews' size or difference**: 20
   vs 20 read the same 18 / 22% as 10 vs 10, and 20 vs 10 (a difference
   of 10) the same 29-34% as 10 vs 5 (a difference of 5).
3. **The spread looks the same at every ratio below the cap**: 7-17 at
   0.2 (crew 50, 13 boards), 12-18 at 0.5 (wave 31), 18-22 at 1, 29-34 at
   2, 55-64 at 5; every one of the 38 boards from 0.2 to 5 lies within 5 points of its
   ratio's mean, and the widest deviations (7 against 12, 55 against 60)
   reach 5 at both ends of the table. At the cap (ratio 10) all three read
   75. The four 18s and two 22s at ratio 1 (no 19-21) hint at a coarse
   draw (GUESS, six boards).

**NovaJS (main 1d398457, which applied wave 31's refit).**
`CAPTURE_ODDS_BY_CREW_RATIO` (`N/nova_plugin/ship/boarding_component.ts:717-727`)
holds [1, 0.20], [2, 0.34], [10, 0.75] and interpolates linearly between
2 and 10 ("between 2 and 10 nothing was measured", `:693`); `boardCaptureOdds`
(`:780-794`) draws each board's odds evenly within +-5 points
(`CAPTURE_ODDS_SPREAD_POINTS`, `:762`), narrowed at the cap. 1: ratio 1
**matches** (20%), ratio 2 **close** (34 against about 32), ratio 5
**mismatch** (the table interpolates 49% where the original reads 59-64),
ratio 10 **matches** (75 on every board: the narrowing). 2: **matches**
(`captureChance` takes the ratio, `:736-758`). 3: **matches** (+-5 points,
narrowed at the cap).
**Proposed:** add a ratio-5 point and lower ratio 2:
`[2, 0.32]` (seven boards with wave 8's: 31.7), `[5, 0.60]` (four
boards); the rest of the table and the +-5 spread stay. The doc comment
at `:693` ("between 2 and 10 nothing was measured") then cites this
section.

Confidence: medium for 1 and 2 (three to six boards a cell, two crew
pairs at ratios 1 and 2); medium for 3 (a uniform +-5 is not
contradicted; its shape is unread).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Findings.**

**NovaJS (main 0478c197).** `N/nova_plugin/spawn/reinforcements.ts`:
`considerCall` (`:538-629`) needs a PLAYER (or his flock) as the
opponent (`caller === undefined` returns at `:562`), and the module
comment says "An NPC's hit never calls it, nor does an NPC's attack on
another NPC" (`:166-168`). 2: **mismatch** (no call without a player).
3: **matches** (no call; for another reason). 4: **matches**
(`REINFORCEMENT_ARRIVAL_DISTANCE = 1_800` from the centre, `:273`; the
measured 1,740 is inside its measured band). The NPC engagement already
honours MaxOdds (`oddsFavorable`, `N/nova_plugin/npc/npc_decision.ts:657`,
`:866`), so wave 32's no-fight **matches** too.
**Proposed:** (a) `ReinforcementCallSystem` calls on an NPC's hit too: when
the hit's responsible ship is an NPC (no player or flock), the call's
caller is that NPC's side, the enemies its side's Strength sum (the
responsible ship and every NPC of its govt hostile to the fleet's govt,

system's own once-a-day for an NPC-caused call, ReinfIntrval kept per
system instead of per pilot for that case), and the fleet's ships take the
attacker as their aggressor; (b) the module comment's "nor does an NPC's
attack on another NPC" becomes "an NPC's attack calls it when the odds
against the fleet's side pass, as a player's (reference ... wave 33)";

target) does not call, as hunt_a1. Multiplayer: no player to stamp, so a
per-system day stamp is needed (a ruling, `needs/maintainer`).

**Findings.**
1. **The +1,000 per plea does not stop**: three channels of twelve and

   27,000 -> 20,200, 31,000 -> 23,200, 11,000 -> 8,200), and every Lower
   Price on a counter withdrew (13 of 13). No sign that the counter depends
   on the ask's place in the climb (counters at asks 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9,
   11, 12).
4. **The 0x0200 warship (hostile by record) haggles exactly as the
   provoked 0x2000 freighter**, and the 0x8000 | 0x0200 warship's flat
   20,000 is only the FIRST ask of each hail (both hails), then +1,000 the
   same way.
5. **The lines are per hail**: each channel kept one withdrawal line
   (STR# 3000 150-154: "What? How dare you! ...", "What a cheapskate! ...",
   "Ha ha ha! ...", "Die, cheapskate!") and one plea line (a mood line or
   "You'll have to pay me first." / "I might if you pay me."), redrawn on
   the next hail.

**NovaJS (main 0478c197, which applied wave 32's haggle).**
`N/nova_plugin/reputation/hail.ts`: `mercyPrice` (`:1055-1061`) adds
`MERCY_ASK_STEP` 1,000 per withdrawn ask, uncapped; `lowerMercyPrice`
(`:1082-1094`) counters with `mercyLowerPriceCounters` (`:1069-1074`, one
in four per ship, pilot, channel and ask) and withdraws on a counter; the
channel is one opening of the comm dialog. 1: **matches**. 3: the 3/4 rule
and the withdrawal on a counter **match**; the odds (one in four) are
**consistent** (19 in 59). 4: **matches** (the 0x8000 flat 20,000 is the
channel's first ask, `shipBribePrice` `:658-664`, and the steps come on
top). 5: one `mercyLoweredText` per channel's seed: **matches** for the
withdrawal; the plea line is the ship's fixed mood line
(`fuelSaleTerms(ship).mood`, `N/display/hail_dialog_plugin.ts:1048`), **mismatch**
with 2. 2: **mismatch**: NovaJS keeps the first ask (and the mood) fixed per
ship and pilot for given cash (`shipBribePrice`, `bribeGrowth`'s seed
`bribe:grow:<ship>:<pilot>`, `:639-650`; the mood `fuelSaleTerms(ship)`, `:451`), where the original re-draws both
on every hail.
**Proposed:** seed the ship's mood and `bribeGrowth` with the CHANNEL too
(`...:<ship>:<pilot>:<channel>`), so each hail draws its own mood line and
first ask (the dialog already names the channel and sends it with the
plea's records, so the quote and the charge still agree); the comment's
"NOT MODELLED" note then cites this section. Optionally keep
`FUEL_COUNTER_IN_FOUR` and cite 19 in 59.

Confidence: high for 1, 3's rounding and 4 (60+ asks read off the popup);
medium for 3's odds (59 presses: one in four and one in three both fit);
high for 2 (ten first asks on ten hails, 3,000 to 20,000
from one ship).

### Capture, wave 33: the roll follows the SHOWN odds (8 captures in 25 rolls where the shown odds expect 10.1; 6 of 7 at 75%); the cap is reached by ratio 7 (75% on every board) and ratio 3 reads 38-45%; marines count: ModVal 10 adds ten crew (ratio 1 -> the ratio-2 band), ModVal -20 adds about 20 points; a Capture Ship click can trip the self-destruct (2 in 27); at the escort cap the dialog reads 0% beside a grey Capture Ship, with no line (2026-11-25)

**Questions** (brief item 3; wave-32 leftovers): whether the capture roll
uses the odds the dialog shows (count captures against the shown
numbers); what marines (oütf ModType 25) do; the odds between ratios 2 and
5 and between 5 and 10; the per-board draw's shape.

**Rig** (`wave33Resources` "C"; `scenarios/w33_capture.json`). Wave 32's:
the boarder (the Kit Ring Crawler Tough and copies) with the Kit Escort
Gun turret against wave 8's live crew-10 hulk (sÿst/spöb 2044; the crew-1
hulk 2039 for ratio 10); 7 single turret taps disable it, the board loop
boards, and the dialog click is now **Capture Ship** (463, 353), not
Abort. Boarders: crew 10 (shïp 528), 30 (shïp 555), 70 (shïp 556); crew 10
with oütf 468 Kit Marines 10 (ModType 25, ModVal 10) or oütf 469 Kit
Marines 20 Pct (ModVal -20). The odds come from the shot before the click
and the outcome from the status line 0.5 and 2.5 s after it
(`tools/capsum.sh` -> `capture_a.png`, `capture_b.png`) and from the
success prompt in the last shot (`tools/capwon.sh`). Five interleaved
rounds of the ratio cells, three of the marine cells.

| boarder vs hulk crew | ratio | shown odds -> outcome, per board |
|---|---|---|
| 70 vs 10 | 7 | 75 SD, 75 C, 75 C, 75 C, 75 F |
| 10 vs 1 | 10 | 75 C, 75 C, 75 C |
| 30 vs 10 | 3 | 42 F, 42 C, 38 F, 45 F, 45 F |
| 10 vs 10 | 1 | 18 F, 24 F, 17 F, 15 F, 25 F |
| 10 + Marines 10 vs 10 | (2) | 34 F, 32 SD, 25 F |
| 10 + Marines 20 Pct vs 10 | (1) | 35 F, 35 F, 45 C |
| 10 vs 1, SIX hired escorts (esc6_1) | 10 | **"Capture Odds: 0%"**, Capture Ship GREYED; the click did nothing, no line |

(C captured: the prompt "Do you want to use this ship as an escort, or
would you rather trade places with its captain and use it as your own
ship?" with Use As My Ship / Use As Escort, over the plunder dialog; F
"Your attempt to capture this ship was unsuccessful." and the dialog
closed; SD "Oops! You tripped this ship's security self-destruct
mechanism.", the hulk destroyed.)

**Findings.**
1. **The capture roll follows the shown odds**: of the 25 clicks that rolled (two
   tripped the self-destruct first, finding 5), 8 captured where the
   shown odds sum to 10.1 (standard deviation about 2.1): 6 of 7 at 75%
   (one 75% FAILED, so the cap is a chance, not a certainty), 2 of 18 at
   15-45% (4.9 expected). Nothing points at another number (the table's
   mean or the bare crew ratio would give nearly the same sums); GUESS
   that the roll is against the shown percent, as NovaJS does.
2. **The cap is reached by ratio 7**: all five crew-70 boards read exactly 75
   (as every ratio-10 board), where a straight line from ratio 5's 60%
   (wave 32) to ratio 10 would read 66. Between 5 and 7 nothing was read.
3. **Ratio 3 reads 38-45%** (42.4 mean over five boards): on the
   straight line from ratio 2's 32% to ratio 5's 60% (41.3 at 3).
4. **Marines count**: Kit Marines 10 (ten more effective crew, the Bible's
   "1 and up") made crew 10 against 10 read 34, 32, 25 (mean 30): ratio
   2's band (wave 32: 29-34), not ratio 1's (15-24 this wave); Kit Marines
   20 Pct (the Bible's "-1 to -100: increase the capture odds by this
   amount") read 35, 35, 45 (mean 38): ratio 1's mean plus about 20 points.
   (The 25 sits 6 points under ratio 2's mean: the spread may be a little
   wider than +-5, or the effective crew is not exactly 20.)
5. **A Capture Ship click can trip the hulk's self-destruct**: 2 of 27
   clicks (one at 75%, one at 32%) answered "Oops! ..." instead of an
   outcome (no capture, the hulk destroyed), as a plunder take does.
   GUESS: a separate draw before the capture roll, about 1 in 10 (Credits'
   take trips about 1 in 4, Cargo 5 in 6).
6. The draw's shape at ratio 1: 18, 24, 17, 15, 25 this wave, with
   wave 32's 18, 22, 18, 18, 18, 22: values from 15 to 25 (not only 18 /
   22), so the steps are not of 4; ratio 1's mean is about 19, as before.
7. **At the escort cap the dialog reads "Capture Odds: 0%" and greys
   Capture Ship**, with no message at all (no STR# 2002 #123 line; a
   pilot with six hired escorts against the crew-1 hulk that reads 75%
   without them): the wave-23 escort-cap leftover. The click on the grey
   button did nothing.

**NovaJS (main 0478c197, which applied wave 32's table).**
`N/nova_plugin/ship/boarding_component.ts`: `CAPTURE_ODDS_BY_CREW_RATIO`
(`:720-731`) [1, 0.20], [2, 0.32], [5, 0.60], [10, 0.75], interpolated
linearly (`captureChance`, `:740-760`), +-5 a board (`boardCaptureOdds`,
`:787-797`); `N/nova_plugin/encounters/boarding_plugin.ts:1545` rolls
`random.next() < boarding.captureOdds / 100`. 1: **matches** (the roll
uses the shown odds). 2: **mismatch** (ratio 7 interpolates 66%; the
original reads the 75% cap). 3: **matches** (41% at ratio 3). 4:
**mismatch**: ModType 25 is parsed (`marines`,
`N/../novadatainterface/src/outfit_data.ts:319-325`, "plumbed but unconsumed") but not used: the
board's odds take the raw shïp Crew (`boarding_plugin.ts:770`,
the "documented seam" at `:1542-1544`). 5: **mismatch** (no self-destruct
draw on a capture). 6: consistent (+-5 around the mean). 7: the button
greys (**matches**, rulings #161 / #250), but `N/display/boarding_plugin.ts`
drops the odds row (`:231-235`, `odds` null when `captureBlocked`) and adds
the STR# 2002 #123 note (`:270-275`) where the original shows "Capture
Odds: 0%" and nothing else: **mismatch** in the readout.
**Proposed:** (a) add `[7, 0.75]` to the table (MEASURED: the cap by ratio
7; GUESS: linear from 5's 0.60); (b) marines: the boarder's effective crew
is shïp Crew + the sum of its outfits' positive ModType-25 values, and the

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| P72 (72) | **125** | **126**, 127, 129, 133, 137, 150 | 122.4 | 126 | 126 |

**Findings.**
1. **The window is trunc(1.75 x W), and a ship exactly on it is too far**:
   each at-rest art lands one pixel inside 1.75 W and refuses ON it (P40
   70, P72 126, S100 175), and the 17 px station, whose 1.75 W is 29.75,
   refuses at 29 and docks at 28: a strict test against the truncated
   value, `max(|dx|, |dy|) < trunc(1.75 W)` (equivalently, for whole-pixel
   offsets, `<= 1.75 W - 1`; the two part only for a ship between 28.75
   and 29 px from a 17 px art). Every earlier reading fits: wave 33's 250
   px planet (432.4 landed, 439.4 too far; 437), wave 31's walk-outs (425.4
   landed), wave 6's at-rest brackets (the 80 px frame "too far at 140":
   exactly trunc(1.75 x 80), so strict; the 88 px frame landed at 146,
   too far at 167: 154), the 315 px station docked from 545.4 (1.7 W =
   535.5 would have refused), and the gates (wave 31's 96 px gate in at
   155, out at 172: 168).
2. **Stations follow the planets' rule**: the 100 x 70 and 17 x 31 stations
   by their WIDTH, like the planets (the 100 x 70 station docks at 174,
   past 1.75 x its height); no station factor.
3. **The ship's size does not count**: the 96 px Kit Ring Crawler Big and
   the 160 px Kit Huge Leader (its disc overlapping the planet's art) were
   both "too far" at 150 px from the 72 px planet (1.7 W + half the ship
   would give 170 and 202). The window is centre to centre.
4. 1.7 W + a constant is out: the 72 px planet refused 126 (1.7 W + 3.6)
   where the 250 px planet landed at 432.4 (1.7 W + 7.4).

**NovaJS (main 6aaad1c4, which applied wave 33's landing GUESS).**
`N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts`: `LAND_RANGE_PER_FRAME_WIDTH = 1.74`
(`:576`), `landingRange` = 1.74 x W (`:609-612`), `inLandingZone`
inclusive `<=` (`:624-626`). 1: every at-rest edge but one **matches**
(P40 69 / 70, P72 125 / 126, S100 174 / 175, the 250 px planet's 432.4 /
439.4, the walk-out's 545.4): 1.74 W sits inside each bracket. The 17 px
station **mismatches**: 29 px is inside 1.74 x 17 = 29.58 (lands in NovaJS)
and too far on the original. No plain factor with an inclusive edge fits
all four arts (the 17 px station needs k < 1.706, the 72 px planet k >=
1.736); the truncation does. In whole pixels NovaJS's last landing pixel,
floor(1.74 W), and the original's, trunc(1.75 W) - 1, part for small arts
with a large fraction (W = 17: 29 vs 28) and for wide arts (W = 250: 435
vs 436; W = 315: 548 vs 550). 2: **matches** (no station factor, the
width). 3: **matches** (centre to centre).
**Proposed:** `landingRange` = `Math.trunc(1.75 * W)` (`LAND_RANGE_PER_FRAME_WIDTH
= 1.75`) and `inLandingZone` strict (`landingDistance(dx, dy) < range`),
the comment citing this section's edges (P40 69 / 70, P72 125 / 126, S17
28 / 29, S100 174 / 175) and dropping the "1.7 W plus the ship's
half-size, or a wider true frame" alternatives (finding 3 and 4). It

wormhole's window is 182 by this rule, 181 by 1.74 W today, under the cap;
nothing between 150 and 230 px was measured).

Confidence: high (twenty at-rest presses on four arts, each edge measured

### Wormholes, wave 34: no clearance and no standing request: every `l` outside the window says "You're too far away to enter this wormhole." (at 230 px, inside the 249 square, too), and a ship that then coasts (or flies with no press) straight over the wormhole is NOT taken through; `l` at 150 px goes through at once; a far `l` about 730 px out selects nothing (2026-11-25)

**Question** (brief item 4; leftover since wave 31): a wormhole and a
standing request: does entering a wormhole's zone clear (or transit)
automatically, as a planet's, a station's and a gate's standing request
is cleared on entry?

**Rig** (`wave34Resources` "W"). Stock Wormhole art and flags (spöb 465:
Flags 0x21, Flags2 0x2200, the 104 px art), HyperLinks to the kit
wormhole in sÿst 1324 Kit Worm Dest. At rest (`gatefar.sh`, three `l`
1.5 s apart, a shot after each): the Kit Ring Lancer on a decoration
with the wormhole at (150, 0), (230, 0) and (300, 0). Coasting
(`moverun.sh`): on Kit Worm 300, turned east by `move.mjs`, then one keys
step `Up@120 wait 300 l wait 15000` (the press about 290 px out, then the
inertial coast at about 45 px/s straight over the wormhole), and the same
with no press. First try, Kit Worm Toward (the wormhole at (1100, 0), the
press 9 s into the coast): the turn left the heading 6 degrees off, so the
ship passed about 280 px wide; it shows only the far press.

| run | presses | lines | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| worm_150 | `l` at 150 px | **"Passing through a wormhole into the Kit Worm Dest system on June 23rd, 1177 NC."** | through on the FIRST press |
| worm_230 | three `l` at 230 px | "You're too far away to enter this wormhole." x 3 | stays (no clearance line, inside the 249 square) |
| worm_300 | three `l` at 300 px | the same x 3 | stays |
| worm_coast_l | `l` about 290 px out, then none | "You're too far away to enter this wormhole." (the press), then nothing | **coasted over the wormhole's centre and on; no transit, no line** |
| worm_coast_nol | none | nothing | **flew over it (about 20-30 px from its centre) and on; no transit** |
| worm_toward | `l` about 730 px out | **nothing** (status line dark, "Nav System Off" kept) | passed 280 px wide |

**Findings.**
1. **A wormhole has no clearance step and no standing request**: inside
   the 249 px square that clears every port, station and gate, `l` says
   "too far" (three presses at 230 px, no cleared line), and a ship whose
   `l` was answered "too far" is NOT taken through when it then coasts over
   the wormhole (over its centre, well inside any window). Only a press
   inside the window transits (150 px: through on the first press, as
   waves 23 and 25).
2. **Flying over a wormhole does nothing** without a press (no line, no
   transit).
3. **A far `l` selects nothing**: about 730 px from the only wormhole (the
   system's only other stellars decorations), the press left "Nav System
   Off" and printed nothing, like a gate beyond its 490-500 px circle (wave
   29); at 290-300 px the press selected it ("too far"). The range in
   between is unmeasured.

**NovaJS (main 6aaad1c4).** `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts`:
`stellarUsesClearance` is false for a wormhole (`:664`), so the selecting
`l` goes straight to the window (`:1067`; "too far" outside, through
inside), and `StellarAutoClearanceSystem` skips it (`:1136`, the
`stellarUsesClearance` test in its step). 1 and 2: **match** (no request,
no clearance, no automatic transit). 3: **mismatch** (small): with nothing
selected, the nearest-port pick limits only hypergates to
`HYPERGATE_SELECT_RANGE` (500, `:358`, the test at `:1045-1047`); a
wormhole is picked from any distance and answered "too far".
**Proposed:** (a) nothing for the standing request (the brief's question:
measured, matches); (b) GUESS: the wormhole joins the hypergate's 500 px
selection circle in the nearest-port pick (a wormhole is a gate kind; the
original selected nothing 730 px out and did select at 300). The 104 px
wormhole's window edge (1.75 W = 182 by the planets' rule, 181 today) is
unmeasured between 150 and 230 px.

Confidence: high for 1 and 2 (five runs, every press and the coast read
frame by frame); medium for 3 (one far press).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261125-w34/worm_150`,
`worm_230`, `worm_300`, `worm_coast_l`, `worm_coast_nol`, `worm_toward`
(`recording.mp4`, `*-l<n>.png`), `lines_worm.png`, `worm_coast_l_lines.png`,
`worm_coast_l_tiles.png` / `worm_coast_nol_tiles.png` (a frame every 1.5 s
from the coast's start), `worm_toward_frames.png`.

**Applied (wave-34 fixes, 2026-11-25, d76630fe).** (a) nothing. (b) As
proposed (GUESS on the radius): with nothing selected, the nearest-port
pick skips a wormhole, like a hypergate, at `distance >= 500`
(`HYPERGATE_SELECT_RANGE`, `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts`); a
wormhole selected by a click or a number key still answers from any
distance. Specced on the synthetic Ossory Rift: picked at 499 px ("too
far"), Halden Refuge picked instead at 501, nothing at 730 with the
station gone; the first-`l` "too far" spec now presses at 300 px. No

### R19 in NPC fights, wave 35: the threshold is about HALF, not 1.0: a lone Strength-10 hunter called against one Strength-6 or Strength-8 prey and never against a Strength-4 one (three runs), one Strength-15 prey called against two hunters (0.75) and not against three (0.5); the friends are summed with the victim (one prey of 11 or 15 against three hunters never called) and NOT shield-weighted (not even with all three at 0% shield); one NPC-caused call per visit: with the first fleet gone, four more minutes of fighting called nothing (2026-11-25, twelfth pass)

NPC, shield-weighted: wave 34's S12many_2 called at 24 against a nominal
30 with one hunter at 20% shield), the threshold between 1.0 and 1.2, and
whether an NPC-caused call is limited per day (a second fight the same
visit, after the first fleet is gone).

so an early call's line is caught with its time; SMALL traffic (avgShips
2, one hunter and one prey about half the time: Kit Reinf Pair 0.4 / 0.6
/ 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.1, Pair Weak 0.8; avgShips 3 for Kit Reinf Friends 15);
the hunters as a FLEET of exactly three placed by the system (sÿst
DudeTypes -319 / -320, Kit Hunter Pack Full / Weak) against one prey; and
for the day, Kit Reinf Day (Full hunters against wave 33's Strength-500
armed preys, ReinfFleet 318: three Strength-1, 60-armor Kit RF Fragile
that the preys destroy) watched with back-to-back censuses
(`tools/huntcen.sh`, one every 20 s for 5 minutes). AI 3 traffic comes and
goes, so only a call in the first seconds (or a composition that held
through a no-call watch) is read; later calls are listed apart.

| run | composition (preys : hunters, from the census) | Strength sums, preys : hunters | ratio | fleet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| friends15_b | 2 S15 : 1 Full | 30 : 10 | 3.0 | **called** 9.1 s |

| late calls, composition uncertain | friends_weak #1 / #2 (Weak hunters first, preys later), friends15_a, pair11_b, pair10_a, pairfull08_a, pairweak08_c, pair06_a, day_a | | | called at 134 / 73 / 67 / 86 / 66 / 128 / 98 / 135 / 65 s |
| day_b (Kit Reinf Day) | 1 S500 : 1 Full at the call, then 2-3 Full hunters against S500 preys to the end | | | ONE call at 16.5 s; the Fragile fleet in censuses 1-2, GONE from census 3 (about 55 s); **no second line** in the 240 s after, the fight going on (prey shields 99 -> 77%) |
| day_a | preys first, a Full hunter later | | | one call at 64.7 s; the fleet in census B (93-109 s), gone by census C (273 s); no second line to 293 s |

**Findings.**
1. **The threshold is about half**: every early fight at a ratio of 0.6
   or more called (0.6, 0.75, 0.8 four times, 1.0, 1.1 twice, 1.2, 1.5,
   1.8, 3.0), every one at 0.5 or less did not (0.5 three times, all
   packs; 0.4 three times; 0.37; wave 34's 8 : 30). A lone Strength-10
   hunter at full shield calls against one Strength-6 prey and never
   against a Strength-4 one. The edge is between 0.4 and 0.6 (between 0.5
   and 0.6 if the packs count): "the attackers' sum over HALF the
   defenders'" fits every reading. Wave 34's "between 1.0 and 1.2" only
   meant that nothing between 0.27 and 1.0 had been tried.
2. **The friends are summed, the victim among them**: one Strength-11 or
   Strength-15 prey against three hunters never called (11 : 30; 15 : 30
   twice as a pack), where the victim alone (11 or 15 against 10) would
   have; one Strength-15 prey against two did (15 : 20); a lone victim's
   Strength-4 prey did not (4 : 10), so a lone victim is not "no friends".
3. **The shield does not weigh the friends**: three Weak hunters, all
   "Shields Down" (hit, fighting), never called against one Strength-15
   prey in two runs (15 : 30 unweighted, 15 : 9 at the Bible's 30%); the
   Weak lone hunter's calls (pairweak08) are the 0.8 calls the Full hunter

### R7 Accept on a raised ask, wave 35: Accept Price on a warship's third plea (22,000 after 20,000 and 21,000) answered "A pleasure to do business with you." and the credits read 100.00M -> 99.97M, so more than the first ask was charged; the plea after an unanswered counter cannot be put (the price popup is modal); in one run the record-hostile warship was not hostile for 2.5 minutes, then asked 4,000 with no bad-mood line (2026-11-25)

(charged as shown?), a plea after an unanswered counter, whether the
per-hail first ask follows the mood line.

Kit Bribe Plain's port, gövt 304 0x0200 warships hostile by record -50,
100M credits) with `tools/r7_35.sh`: **r7_accept** (one hail; Beg For
Mercy, Lower Price until the popup is gone, twice; the third Beg's ask
ACCEPTED (Accept Price, 415, 336); then `l l` and Return to land, take off
and pull the pilot) and **r7_after** (per hail, Beg; if the Lower Price
answer is a COUNTER, click Beg For Mercy's visible left part (300, 361)
with the counter unanswered).

| run | lines and asks in order | after |
|---|---|---|
| r7_accept | "What do you want?" / "Only if you pay me first." 20,000 (Lower Price: COUNTER 15,000; Lower Price: "Die, cheapskate!"), 21,000 (Lower Price: "Die, cheapskate!"), **22,000: Accept Price -> "A pleasure to do business with you."** | credits panel 100.00M before, **99.97M** after; "Landing request denied." (record -50), so no pilot was written |
| r7_after | hails 1-7 (about 2.5 minutes): "What is it?" / "Not a chance." with Greetings / Request Assistance / Close Channel: the warship was NOT hostile (no Beg For Mercy); hail 8: hostile, "You'll have to pay me first." **4,000** (at 100M), Lower Price: "What? How dare you! Prepare to die!" (withdrawn) | no counter reached |

**Findings.**
1. **Accept takes the raised ask**: after two pleas the third ask (22,000)
   was accepted with "A pleasure to do business with you." and the panel
   went from 100.00M to 99.97M. 100M less the first ask (20,000) is
   exactly 99.98M; 99.97M needs more than 20,000, so the raised ask was
   charged (22,000 shows as 99.97M if the panel truncates to 10,000s,
   GUESS; a 21,000 charge would too). The exact amount needs a pilot
   written after it (the port refused the landing at record -50: land on
   another port or pull after a jump).
2. **A plea after an unanswered counter cannot be made**: the price popup
   (Lower Price / Accept Price) is modal over the hail dialog; the only
   ways off a counter are its two buttons, so the "plea after a counter"
   is always after a Lower Price (a withdrawal) or an Accept. (r7_after
   never reached a counter, below; this is read from the popup's layout in
   every wave-33 counter shot.)
3. **Hostility by record is not certain at Enter Ship**: in r7_after (21:47, just before r7_accept on the same pilot) the
   targeted warship was not hostile for seven hails (about 2.5 minutes:
   "What is it?", "Not a chance.") and was on the eighth, where r7_accept's
   and every wave-33 run's were firing at Enter Ship. Its first hostile
   ask, 4,000 at 100M under the plain "You'll have to pay me first.", is
   one more low first ask without a bad-mood line (wave 33: 9,000 and 3,000
   on the hails run), so a low ask does not need the "bad mood" line.
   See the reliability note.

**NovaJS (main 08092a02).** `N/nova_plugin/encounters/hail_plugin.ts`:
the Beg For Mercy Accept charges `mercyPrice(shipBribePrice(...), haggle)`
(`:742-755`), the channel's raised ask on the table: 1 **matches** (as far
as the panel shows). 2: not checked in NovaJS (whether its plea button stays live under the price popup). 3: nothing to compare.
**Proposed:** nothing (mark the raised-ask charge MEASURED to the panel's

**Question** (wave-23 leftover, "F1c: why the re-flowed five sit 4-9 px off
the lattice"). Wave 23 read the five escorts left after rank 1's release
6 s and 8.5 s later; were they still settling?

**Rig.** Wave 23's: `w22_f1c_6` (six hired discs, red rank 1 .. cyan rank
6) at rest at Kit Port; `tools/f1crel.sh`: a shot, a click on red (found
by `discshot.mjs`), `y`, Release (306, 383), then window shots 3, 6, 12,
20, 30, 45, 60 and 90 s after the release, 4 s of thrust and three cruise
shots. Offsets along / across the leader's heading (`tools/comps.mjs
--travel -0.999,0.053`, the heading of the first shot; + across is red's
side).

| escort | before (rank, slot) | new rank and its five-layout slot (wave 22 `f1c_5`) | 3 s .. 90 s at rest (every shot identical) | cruise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| green | 2 (-23.3, -23.8) | 1 (-23.5, +23.5) | (-21.2, +16.1): **7.8 px short** | (-20.5, +17.0) |
| blue | 3 (-47.6, +47.6) | 2 (-23.5, -23.5) | (-29.6, -16.1): **9.6 short** | (-28.0, -14.7) |
| yellow | 4 (-47.6, -47.6) | 3 (-47.0, 0) | (-45.5, -7.6): **7.7 short** | (-45.7, -5.8) |
| magenta | 6 (-71.8, +23.8) | 4 (-47.5, +47.7) | (-56.0, +40.0): **11.5 short** | (-50.4, +41.8) |
| cyan | 5 (-71.3, -23.3) | 5 (-47.5, -47.5) | (-55.2, -40.1): **10.7 short** | (-53.0, -38.3) |

**Findings.**
1. **Not a settle**: the nine rest shots from 3 s to 90 s are identical
   to the pixel, and the cruise shots keep the same offsets within 2-6
   px. Wave 23's 6 s and 8.5 s readings were the final positions.
2. **Each escort stops SHORT of its new slot on the straight line from
   its old one**: the remaining error points back along each escort's
   path (green's old slot was across -23.8, its new +23.5, it stopped at
   +16.1; magenta came in from (-71.8, +23.8) toward (-47.5, +47.7) and
   stopped with (8.5, 7.7) to go; the others alike), 7.7-11.5 px short.
   So the original's escort stops correcting inside about 8-12 px of its
   slot (a dead band), and an escort that enters the band moving stays
   where it stopped. Pilot-loaded escorts start ON their slots (wave 22:
   0.5 px rms) and launched fighters fly in (wave 22: about 7 px rms off
   the lattice), which this explains too.

**NovaJS (main 482d3674).** `N/nova_plugin/npc/npc_formation.ts:442-465`

### Outfit resale (R9), wave 36: a pre-owned outfit sells for HALF its price; the full refund covers only units ABOVE the count the player had when he came in, not "units bought this visit" (2026-11-25)

**Question** (the hub's catalogue audit; R9): what does selling a
pre-owned outfit refund (NovaJS 50%), and the same-visit refund.

**Rig** (`k_port`). Pilot `w36_k_port`: the Kit Lancer at Kit Port with
TWO Kit Plain Mass installed (oütf 455: Cost 1,000, Mass 10, no flags) and
10,000 credits. In the outfitter: select it, Sell x2, Buy, Sell, Buy x3,
Sell x3; "You Have:" read after each.

| action | count after | credits | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| (start, after a 2-credit recharge) | 2 | 9,998 | |
| Sell (pre-owned) | 1 | 10,498 | **+500** |
| Sell (pre-owned) | 0 | 10,998 | **+500** |
| Buy | 1 | 9,998 | -1,000 |
| Sell (the unit JUST BOUGHT) | 0 | 10,498 | **+500** |
| Buy x3 | 3 | 7,498 | -3,000 |
| Sell | 2 | 8,498 | **+1,000** |
| Sell | 1 | 8,998 | **+500** |
| Sell | 0 | 9,498 | **+500** |

**Findings.**
1. **A pre-owned unit sells for 50% of its price** (500 of 1,000, twice).
2. **The full refund is not per unit bought this visit**: a unit bought
   and sold straight back after the two pre-owned ones were sold refunded
   500, and of three bought this visit only one refunded in full. Every
   reading fits "a sale refunds the full price while the count before it
   is ABOVE the count the player came in with (here 2), half otherwise"
   (the count went 3 -> 2 at full price, 2 -> 1 and 1 -> 0 at half; 1 -> 0
   after selling below the starting count at half). Wave 10's same-visit
   full refunds (from a count of 0) fit it too.

**NovaJS (main 482d3674).** `N/spaceport/outfitter_rules.ts:418`
`OUTFIT_RESALE_FRACTION = 0.5`: 1 **matches**. `sellRefund`
(`:495-506`) refunds in full while a per-outfit `boughtThisVisit` counter
is above zero (`outfitter.ts:900` keeps it), so the same sequence pays
1,000 for the unit bought after the two pre-owned sales and 1,000 for all
three of the last three: 2 **mismatch** (3,000 more than the original
over this sequence). **Proposed:** replace the bought-this-visit counter
with the count on entry: `sellRefund` pays `outfitPrice` when the
installed count before the sale is above the count recorded when the
outfitter opened, `outfitResaleValue` otherwise (GUESS: "entry" is the
outfitter's opening, not the landing; one visit measured). The no-profit
invariant still holds (a unit sold at full price was bought at full price
in the same visit).

Confidence: high (nine sales, every credit read off the panel; one
outfit, one visit).

**Evidence:** `k_port/*/08-sel.png` .. `16-sell6.png`, `r9_sheet.png`,
`r9_sheet2.png`.

**Applied (wave-36 fixes, 2026-11-26, f0cd238f).** As proposed:
`sellRefund` (`N/spaceport/outfitter_rules.ts`) pays `outfitPrice` while the
count before the sale is above the count recorded when the outfitter opened
(`Outfitter.setInput`; GUESS: the opening, not the landing), the 50%
`outfitResaleValue` otherwise. The per-unit receipts stay only as a guard: a
full refund also needs one, so a unit an OnPurchase grants (above the entry
count, never paid for) sells at 50%; with plain buys and sells it never
changes the measured rule. Specced: this section's sequence (+500 +500;
+500; +1,000 +500 +500) through `sellRefund` and through the real
Outfitter. No schema change.

never landed.

| rig (art, flags) | fresh clearance at (s) | landed / docked at (s) | edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kit Lapse P250 Station 230 (250 px PLANET art, flags 0x11) | 24.722 .. 24.475 (six) | **24.417** ("cleared to dock") | 24.42-24.47 |
| Kit Lapse S315 Planet 230 (315 x 200 STATION art, flags 0x43) | 24.721 .. 24.538 (five) | **24.474** ("cleared to land") | 24.47-24.54 |
| Kit Lapse P72 120 (72 px planet, 0x43) | 24.725 .. 24.473 (six) | **24.414** | 24.41-24.47 |
| Kit Lapse S100 150 (100 x 70 station, 0x11) | 24.723 .. 24.357 (all seven) | none | below 24.36 |
| the same, lower (`lapse_s100_low`) | (none) | **24.304** (the first press) | **24.30-24.36** |
| Kit Lapse S100 Heavy (the same station, a Jupiter-art decoration on screen) | 24.720 .. 24.481 (five) | **24.418** | **24.42-24.48** |
| **control**: wave 35's `w31_land_p250_230` (250 px planet, 0x43; wave 35: landed 24.617 / 24.649) | 24.722 .. **24.356** (all seven) | **none** | **below 24.36** |
| Kit Gate J325 245 (gate, Jupiter's 325 px art) | 24.725 .. 24.357 (all seven) | none | below 24.36 |
| the same, lower (`lapse_gate_low`) | 24.301, 24.237 | **24.182** (the gate map) | **24.18-24.24** |

**Findings.**
1. **The station flag does not pick the clock**: the planet art WITH the

   24.41 and 24.47 s, all near wave 35's "station" 24.40-24.44 and none
   near its "planet" 24.62-24.65. The flag sets only the wording ("cleared
   to dock" / "to land").
2. **The same rig changed between sessions**: wave 35's 250 px planet rig,
   run unchanged as the control, lapsed at every interval down to 24.356 s
   tonight, where on wave 35's evening it landed at 24.617 and 24.649 s.
   So wave 35's two clocks were two RUNS, not two kinds of stellar.
3. **The life jitters per clearance**: on the 100 x 70 station, nine
   presses at a constant 24.40 s gave five fresh clearances and then a

   lapsed at 24.357 and 24.413, and (with a Jupiter-art decoration on

   planet rig held past 24.6 s; tonight it lapsed by 24.36).

   24.18-24.24, S100 24.30-24.36, P72 24.41-24.47, P250 Station 24.42-24.47,
   S100 Heavy 24.42-24.48, S315 Planet 24.47-24.54, the constant run about

5. **Gate**: the J325 gate's edge tonight, 24.18-24.24 s, is the lowest
   reading but inside the spread; its clearance lapses on the ports'
   clock (wave 32), and nothing here separates it.

**NovaJS (main 482d3674).** `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts:404`
`PLANET_CLEARANCE_MS = 24_630`, `:417` `STATION_CLEARANCE_MS = 24_420`,

clock. 1 and 2 **mismatch**: the flag rule is refuted (a 0x43 port lapsed at

gates, `STELLAR_CLEARANCE_MS = 24_400` (MEASURED: the centre of the nine
edges of one evening and of the constant-interval run; GUESS: a fixed
value, the original's per-clearance scatter of a few frames not
modelled, since it would need a deterministic draw for an effect under
0.1 s), dropping `stellarClearanceMs`'s station branch, the comments to
cite this section.

Confidence: high for 1 and 2 (seven cascades, each bracketed to one 0.06
s step; the control lapsed seven times in a row where wave 35 landed);
high for the per-clearance scatter (five lapses then a docking at one
constant interval); the 24.4 s centre is medium (one evening's nine

2. **MaxOdds 200 does not mean 2-to-1**: the MaxOdds-200 fleet govt was
   called at 12 : 10 (1.2) in the first seconds of m200_12_b, where the
   Bible's "odds against exceed MaxOdds" would need 2.0. **But the
   MaxOdds DOES move the edge**: three 0.6 fights against the MaxOdds-200
   hunter (one prey and one hunter for 65-145 s, both sides hit) never
   called, where the MaxOdds-100 fleet came at 0.6 in the first 9-15 s
   three times (wave 35's pair06_b, solo06_a / _b). So at MaxOdds 200 the
   edge is between 0.6 and 1.2, at MaxOdds 100 between 0.5 and 0.6: both
   fit "the attackers' sum over HALF of MaxOdds / 100 times the
   friends'" (an edge of 0.5 at 100 and 1.0 at 200).
3. **Exactly half does not call** (two fights: pair05_a, one Strength-5
   prey against one Strength-10 hunter for about 100 s, and pair05_c for
   145 s, both sides hit, no line), with wave 35's 0.6 calls: the edge
   is "more than half", strict.

**NovaJS (main 482d3674).** `N/nova_plugin/spawn/reinforcements.ts`
`considerCall` (`:538-629`) still needs a player or his flock as the
opponent (`:562`), so no NPC fight calls the fleet (waves 33-35's mismatch,
unchanged; the NPC-caused call waits on Forgejo #382); `reinforcementOddsCall` (`:329-338`) is enemies / friends x
100 > MaxOdds. 1: nothing to compare in NovaJS until NPC-caused calls
exist; the proposal below counts every fleet-side NPC (fleet members
included) as a possible caller. 2-3: **mismatch** with the player rule
reused for NPCs. **Proposed** (wave 35's, refined): an NPC-caused call
when an NPC of the fleet's side is attacked by NPCs and the attackers'
plain Strength sum is MORE than MaxOdds / 200 times the fleet side's plain sum (MEASURED: at MaxOdds 100 between 0.5 and 0.6, at 200 between 0.6 and 1.2; GUESS: exactly half of the fleet govt's MaxOdds, strict, i.e. `enemies x 200 > maxOdds x friends`) (the
victim counted; fleet members, placed or not, call like any ship);
the player's call keeps `reinforcementOddsCall` (wave 20).

Confidence: high for 1 (three calls, two of them clean in the first
seconds); high for "not 2-to-1" (one clean call at 1.2); medium for the
strict half (two clean fights at 0.5); high for "MaxOdds scales it" (three clean non-calls at 0.6 against three clean calls); the exact edge at 200 (1.0) is a GUESS.

### A paid ship bribe (A8), wave 37: the bribed warship turns non-hostile at once and a MOBILE one LEAVES the system within about 13-23 s (three of three); one that cannot leave stayed non-hostile for the 4.5 minutes watched; only that ship is bought off; after a landing the system's new warships are hostile again (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue A8): how long does a paid SHIP bribe last (the
visit, a day, until provoked)? NovaJS: two minutes.

**Rig.** Wave 22's Kit Bribe Plain (gövt 304: 0x0200 warships take
bribes, CrimeTol 10; sÿst 1169, AI 3 Kit Bribe Warships, avgShips 3) with
pilot `w37_a8` (the Kit Lancer at its port, record -50 there: the
warships hostile; the Kit Tickler); and, added during the wave, sÿst 1384
Kit Bribe Anchored (`wave37Resources` "A8": the same warship with Speed /
Accel 0, shïp 589, avgShips 2; its port spöb 1937 takes the player at any
record) with pilot `w37_a8b`. `tools/a8.sh`: Tab to a warship, hail (y):
"Status: Hostile", Beg For Mercy; the price; **Accept Price**; Close
Channel; then a re-hail of the SAME ship (no Tab) every 12-15 s; a census
hail of the others (Tab, y).

| run | the ask | after Accept | re-hails of the bribed ship | the others |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a8_a (mobile) | "Lucky you - I'm in a good mood today." 1,000 | "Thank you very much."; the dialog loses its Status line, Beg For Mercy becomes Request Assistance, the target brackets turn yellow; 1.00M -> 999,000 | it flew off the screen at once and the first re-hail, 23 s after the channel closed, said **"Unable to send hail - target ship is entering hyperspace."** | three census hails: all "Status: Hostile" with Beg For Mercy, one firing at the player |
| a8_c (mobile) | 3,000 ("Only if you pay me first.") | "A pleasure to do business with you." | **entering hyperspace** at the first re-hail, about 13 s after | |
| a8_d (mobile) | 1,000 (good mood) | "Thank you very much." | **entering hyperspace** at the first re-hail, about 13 s after | |
| a8_b (anchored) | "I'm in a mean mood today, so it's going to cost you extra." 4,000 | "Thank you very much."; 996,000 | **14 re-hails over 4.5 minutes: every one non-hostile** ("What is it?", Request Assistance, no Status line) | after a landing at the port and the take-off a day later (June 24th) both warships sat at NEW places and both read "Status: Hostile", one firing |
| a8_e (anchored) | 1,000 (good mood) | "Good doing business with you."; 999,000 | two re-hails non-hostile (Request Assistance); then ONE Kit Tickler burst (1 damage, the ship 100% -> 99%): its brackets turned red at once and the hail read **"Status: Hostile"** with Beg For Mercy, and again 10 s later | the other warship: Hostile |

**Findings.**
1. **Accept makes the bribed ship non-hostile at once** (no Status line,
   Request Assistance in place of Beg For Mercy, yellow brackets) and it
   stops attacking.
2. **A bribed ship that can leave, leaves**: all three mobile AI 3
   warships flew away and were entering hyperspace 13-23 s after the
   bribe (A8's "reprieve" is in practice "it goes away").
3. **A bribed ship that cannot leave stayed bought** for all 4.5 minutes
   watched (well past NovaJS's two minutes); no lapse was seen.
4. **The bribe buys off only that ship**: the system's other warships of
   the same govt stayed hostile (a8_a's census) and kept firing.
5. A landing and take-off a day later met NEW warships (the system's
   traffic is rebuilt on take-off), hostile again: the bribe does not
   carry to them; whether the same ship would have stayed bought across
   the day cannot be asked this way.
6. **A provocation ends it at once**: one 1-damage hit on the bought ship
   made it hostile again (a8_e).

**NovaJS (main 01292b54).** `N/nova_plugin/encounters/hail_plugin.ts:278-283`
(`BRIBE_PACIFY_MS` = 120,000) and `:755-778` (Accept: `pacifiedUntil =
now + 2 min`, drop the attack): 1 matches; 2 **missing** (a bribed ship
stays and goes back to hunting after two minutes); 3 **mismatch** (a
lapse at 2 minutes); 4 matches (per ship); 5 matches in effect (new
ships). **Proposed:** on Accept, set the bribed NPC's goal to LEAVE the
system (the AI's normal jump-out, as a ship that has finished its visit),
and drop the 2-minute lapse (keep it pacified until it leaves, or for
the visit when it cannot leave); a hit from the player ends it at once (NovaJS's
`N/nova_plugin/npc/npc_targeting.ts:240` already clears `pacifiedUntil` on
provocation: 6 matches).

Confidence: high for 1, 2 (three of three), 4 and 6; medium for 3 (one
anchored ship, 4.5 minutes).

`*-accepted.png`, `*-h*.png`, `*-hcen*.png`, `recording.mp4`),

**Applied (wave-37 fixes, 2026-11-26, dacd264b).** As proposed: on Accept
a ship that can leave (`bribedShipLeaves` in
`N/nova_plugin/encounters/hail_plugin.ts`: effective Speed and Accel above

### A disabled player (A10), wave 37: no recovery unaided: nearly five minutes disabled with nobody in the system, the armor bar never moved, not even on a hull with ArmorRech 300; "Ship disabled." on the status line (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue A10, partly seen in wave 16): does a disabled
PLAYER ever recover unaided?

**Rig** (`wave37Resources` "A10"). shïp 576 Kit Self Disable (a Kit
Lancer-like player hull: shield 0, armor 2500, ArmorRech 0) and 577 Kit
Self Disable Rech (the same with ArmorRech 300, 9 armor points a second),
each with the Kit Big Blast (oütf 610: 2000 damage, a 300 px blast at the
muzzle; B1: the player's own blast hurts the player). Pilots `w37_a10` /
`w37_a10r` (and `w37_a10c`, the control) at Kit Port in quiet Kit Range (no traffic, nobody else in the
system). `tools/a10.sh`: ONE Space tap, a 1 s thrust, then a shot every
15 s for 4 minutes, another thrust and `l` twice; the armor bar's lit
length read off every shot (`tools/bars.mjs`, 151 px when full).

| run | after the tap | 15 s .. 290 s later (16 shots) | thrust / `l` at the end |
|---|---|---|---|
| a10_a (ArmorRech 0) | "Ship disabled.", armor bar 151 -> 31 px (20%: 500 of 2500) | 31 px every time | the ship did not move; `l` selected Kit Port with no status line |
| a10_r (ArmorRech 300) | the same | **31 px every time** (a running recharge adds about 135 points, 8 px, every 15 s, and would have crossed the one-third line in about 37 s) | the same |
| a10_c (control: ArmorRech 300, NOT disabled; five taps of the 50-damage Kit Blast Bomb, wëap 370) | armor bar 151 -> 140 px | 143, 145, 147, 149, 151 px at 4 s intervals, then full: about 9 points a second | (not disabled) |

Control taps (launch; `bayf`: then `f`), or Space held 1.5 s;

| run | the kill | sÿst 1378 record | combat rating | credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r6_esc | `f`: "New escort orders assigned: All ships attacking target."; the escort's first bolt destroyed the victim within 0.5 s (explosion at 47.9 s); the player never fired | **-1100** | **0 -> 40** | 1,000,000 -> 999,990 (the escort's wage, R12) |

original's kill points, so an imported pilot's tier and a NovaJS-earned

the rounding: every Strength seen so far is a multiple of 5); the tier
table (`N/nova_plugin/reputation/reputation.ts:184-195`) stays.

Confidence: high for 1 (the same numbers three ways, one kill each, a

### Escort wages (R12), wave 37: 1% of the hull's Cost a day (crew, Strength and mass play no part; the stock Terrapin draws 1,500), charged when the player LEAVES the spaceport; an escort the player cannot pay DEFECTS with "Due to lack of pay, one of your escorts has defected." (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue R12): the escort daily wage: how much, when it is
charged, and what happens when the player can't pay.

**Rig** (`wave37Resources` "R12"). Kit Wage hulls: the Kit Escort with
mass 100, crew 20, Strength 100 and Cost 100,000, each changing ONE field:
shïp 581 Cost 10,000, 582 (the base), 583 Cost 150,000, 584 Cost
1,000,000, 585 crew 80, 586 Strength 400, 587 mass 400, 588 Cost 1,000.
Pilots at Kit Port (quiet Kit Range), all escorts hired: `w37_r12a`
(581-586, 200,000 credits), `w37_r12b` (587, 588, the stock Terrapin shïp
136, 582; 200,000), `w37_r12c` (582 and 581, 500 credits). `tools/r12.sh`:
the HUD credits in space, then twice: land (`l l`), Leave, the credits
after the take-off. (The Tab hails meant to read each escort's "Pay:" line
got nothing: Tab does not target the player's hired escorts.)

| run | escorts' 1% of Cost | credits: start / after day 1 / after day 2 | a day |
|---|---|---|---|
| r12_a | 100 + 1,000 + 1,500 + 10,000 + 1,000 (crew 80) + 1,000 (Strength 400) = 14,600 | 200,000 / 185,400 / 170,800 | **14,600** |
| r12_b | 1,000 (mass 400) + 10 + 1,500 (Terrapin, Cost 150,000) + 1,000 = 3,510 | 200,000 / 196,490 / 192,980 | **3,510** |
| r12_c | 1,000 + 100, with 500 credits | 500 / 400 | 100, and **"Due to lack of pay, one of your escorts has defected."** |

In every run the spaceport showed the credits UNCHANGED after the landing
(r12_a: 200,000 in the landed shot); the wage came off at the Leave press
(r12_c's message came up in the spaceport, over the buttons, at Leave, with
an Okay button), so the day's wage is charged with the date advance on
departure ("Launching from Kit Port on June 24th").

**Findings.**
1. **The daily wage is 1% of the hull's Cost**, exactly, for Costs from
   1,000 to 1,000,000; crew (20 / 80), Strength (100 / 400) and mass (100
   / 400) change nothing. The stock **Terrapin draws 1,500** (Cost
   150,000).
2. **It is charged when the player leaves a spaceport** (with the day's
   date advance), not on landing.
3. **An escort the player cannot pay defects**: with 500 credits against
   1,000 + 100, the 1,000-a-day escort left ("Due to lack of pay, one of
   your escorts has defected.", one Okay) and the 100-a-day one was paid
   (500 -> 400) and stayed (the pulled pilot holds only shïp 581, still

   credits cannot cover defects; which one goes first when both are

**NovaJS (main 01292b54).** `N/spaceport/escort_fees.ts:122` and
`:179-181`: the wage is 10% of the hire fee, i.e. 1% of the price: 1
**matches**. Its comment (`:66-80`) records the Terrapin's "Pay: 1,100
credits per day" from `hail/hail_escort.png` as a disagreement; the
original charges a Terrapin 1,500 a day here, so that capture's 1,100 came

plug-in), and the caveat can go. 2: `N/spaceport/mission_session.ts:698-712`
advances the date (and settles the books) at the LANDING: **mismatch**
in timing (the original's spaceport still shows the pre-wage credits; the
charge comes at Leave). 3: `N/spaceport/daily_budget.ts:82-89`
(`settleDailyBudget`) clamps the balance at 0 and keeps every escort
("we have no dismissal flow yet"): **mismatch**.
**Proposed:** keep the 1% rule and drop the 1,100 caveat; settle the
day's wages at departure; when a hired escort's wage cannot be paid,
dismiss that escort with "Due to lack of pay, one of your escorts has
defected." (one dialog per escort, GUESS) and pay the others in roster
order while the credits last.

Confidence: high for 1 (two runs, ten hulls, exact sums twice a run);
high for 2 (three runs); medium for 3 (one run, one defection).

**Applied (wave-37 fixes, 2026-11-26, 65a0064f).** As proposed: the

### Outfit resale "entry" (R9) and the Trade Center (K6), wave 37: the count on entry is taken when the OUTFITTER OPENS (not at the landing); one commodity tier, or one jünk sold there, turns the Trade Center on (2026-11-26)

|---|---|---|---|

| Sell | 2 | 9,500 | **+500** |
| Buy | 3 | 8,500 | -1,000 |
