### Jump phases and fuel (U8), wave 38: from rest `j` to arrival is 4.8 s (turn, a short hold, about 3.5 s of acceleration); departure and arrival are ONE frame (a white flash), the 100 fuel comes off on it; the ship arrives at top speed about 1,350 px out heading for the centre; nothing the player does stops a jump once pressed, and his weapons are locked (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue U8): the hyperspace sequence's timings (from `j`
to the jump effect, to the arrival) and when the fuel is deducted (before,
during, after; an aborted jump).

**Rig** (`wave38Resources` "U8"). sÿst 1387 Kit Jump A (port at the centre,
a decoration stellar 2000 px east, outside the 1000 px no-jump zone)
linked to 1388 Kit Jump B (40 map units east, port at the centre). shïp
590 Kit Jump Lancer (the inertialess Kit Lancer, Speed 800, with Fuel 300:
a jump is a third of the fuel bar, 50 px) and 591 Kit Jump Self Disable
(armor 2500, no recharge, Fuel 300, the Kit Big Blast). Pilots start on
the decoration (`w38_u8`, `w38_u8d`) or the port (`w38_u8p`). `tools/steps.sh`:
`\` (select), `j`; the recording read per frame (`tools/frameseries.mjs`:
the fuel bar, the status line, a centre box; `tools/leftedge.mjs`: the
decoration's edge; `tools/starshift.mjs`: the star field's shift;
`tools/shipstrip.sh`: the ship's sprite), the press frame from
`recording.events.json` (`tools/jumpsum.sh`).

| run | start | `j` press -> arrival | phases (frames at 30 fps) |
|---|---|---|---|
| u8_a j1 | at rest, about 135 degrees off | **144 frames (4.80 s)** | turn 376-396 (0.67 s), still 396-409 (0.43 s), acceleration 409-513 (3.47 s; 18-24 px a frame by 430, the decoration off screen by 437, more than 30 px a frame after), arrival 513 |
| u8_a j2, j3 | coasting at top speed straight away from the destination | **172 frames (5.73 s)** each | braking about 0.9 s (star shift 12 -> 0 px a frame), a 180-degree turn about 0.9 s, acceleration about 3.6 s |
| u8_d1, u8_d2, u8_x1-3, a9_j1, a9_j2 | at rest | 143-146 frames (4.77-4.87 s) | as j1 |
| u8_a j4 | fuel 0 | no jump | **"Insufficient energy for hyperspace jump."** at once (4.4 s on the line) |
| u8_p | on the centre port | no jump | **"Can't initiate hyperspace jump - not yet far enough away from system center."** at once (6.7 s) |

**The arrival frame** (every jump): the screen goes full WHITE for one
frame (caught at 30 fps in u8_x3 and a9_j1 / a9_j2), and on the next the ship is in the
new system: "Arriving in the Kit Jump B system on June 24th, 1177 NC." (in a
system with no stellar: "Entering the Kit Pirate Jump Exit system on June
25th, 1177 NC. No stellar objects present."), "Nav System Off", the date one
day on, and **the fuel bar one jump shorter on that same frame** (148 -> 98
px; 148 -> 143 on a 3,000-fuel hull). There is no separate hyperspace
interval: the system changes on the frame the acceleration ends.

**After the arrival**: the ship coasts at its top speed (the B port crossed
the screen at 340-351 px/s; Speed 800 is about 350 px/s, wave 1's 0.44
px/s per unit) straight at the system's centre from the origin's side, and
passed over the centre port 3.9 s after the arrival in all three jumps (116-118
frames): it arrives about **1,350 px** out (1,000 + about one second at top
speed).

**Abort attempts** (all at rest, all jumped on time): a second `j` 1.65 s
after the first (u8_x1); Down held 2.5 s from +1.65 s (u8_x2); `l` at
+1.66 s (u8_x3); **the Kit Big Blast** (Space) at +0.47 s and +2.65 s
(u8_d1 / u8_d2): **no blast at all** (the armor bar stayed full; the same
tap took it to 20% in wave 37): **the player's weapons are locked once the
jump starts**. A disable in mid-jump (the xeno pirate of A9 firing on a
Kit Fragile Trader on a port 2000 px out, `j` timed against wave 38's
41.6 s to the disable, `tools/a9j.sh`): pressed 39.2 / 37.7 s after
the Leave (a9_j1 / a9_j2) the ship got away one hit above the line (armor
52 / 55 px; "Entering the Kit Pirate Jump Exit system ... No stellar objects
present.", the fuel bar 148 -> 143 px, a 3,000-fuel hull, on the arrival
frame). Pressed 40.45 / 41.1 s after (a9_j3 / a9_j4), the disabling hit
landed **1.13 s / 0.57 s into the sequence** (while turning): **"Ship
disabled - hyperspace field collapsed."**, no jump, **the fuel bar
unchanged** (148 px for the next minute), the destination still selected
("Hyperspace / Kit Pirate Jump Exit"); the pirate then plundered him (A9).

**Findings.**
1. From rest, `j` -> arrival takes **4.8 s**: a turn at the hull's rate,
   about 0.4 s still, then about 3.5 s of acceleration (from facing the
   destination to the arrival: 3.7-3.9 s). From cruise the ship first
   brakes (about 0.9 s) and then turns.
2. **Departure and arrival are the same frame** (one white frame between),

4. **A started jump cannot be stopped by the player**: `j`, Down and `l`

5. The blocked presses print **"Can't initiate hyperspace jump - not yet

The disable cancel
(`N/nova_plugin/encounters/disabled_plugin.ts:214`, `JumpDisableCancelSystem`)
refunds nothing because nothing was taken yet: **matches**, but prints no

(`N/nova_plugin/combat/weapon_plugin.ts:590-595` reads `firePrimary` with

5: a blocked jump only beeps (`N/display/ui_sound_triggers_plugin.ts:206-221`),

**Proposed:** `JUMP_SPINUP_DELAY_MS` 1000 -> 400 and `JUMP_DEPART_DELAY_MS`
2000 -> 3400 (aligned to arrival 3.8 s; GUESS for the split, the hold read
off one jump); `JUMP_ARRIVAL_MARGIN_S` 3 -> 1 (GUESS: "1,000 + one second"
fits 1,350 at 345 px/s; one hull measured); hold the player's primary and
secondary fire while a JumpComponent is present; print the two refusal

### Tribute (R18), wave 39: the defence fleet is the PILOT'S per-stellar count, which a novaref pilot held at 0 for every kit planet (so wave 38's "dominated at once" was an artifact); with it set, a demand from 12,800 up answers "...our defense fleet..." and launches the first wave, and once the launched ships are destroyed the next demand is accepted; below 12,800 it laughs and launches nothing; Tribute -1 / 0 pays 1,000 x TechLevel; EVERY dominated stellar pays at every day's advance (a jump too); a domination survives leaving the system (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue R18, wave-38 leftovers): what launches the
defence fleet (wave 38: never, in twelve demands), its waves, the
domination's reset on leaving or over days, and where the 5,000 Tribute
came from.

**The cause of wave 38's instant dominations.** The original keeps, in
the pilot file, the number of defence ships each stellar has LEFT
(AltPlayerFileDataStruct `stellarShipCount`, 2048 shorts at 0x0006;
novaparse `pilot_parse.ts:267`). A pilot created in the game fills it
from each spöb's DefCount (Earth 600 = DefCount 7006, Spacedock II 120 =
2206 in every novaref pilot); novaref's pilots descend from a base pilot
made before the kit existed, so every kit stellar read **0**, "fleet
already destroyed". Wave 38's Kit Tribute Six / Thirty and this wave's
first four planets (below) all gave in at once for that reason. Fixed in
tooling: pilot-make takes `"stellarShipCount": {"<spöb id>": n}`
(`packages/novaparse/src/pilot/pilot_write.ts`), and the wave-39 tribute
pilots set the DefCount totals.

**Rig** (`wave39Resources` "R18"; gövt 290 Kit Tribute Govt, owner of
every system here, wave 38's Strength-20 one-bolt red-disc defenders).
sÿst 1400 Kit Tribute Plain (spöb 1955 Plain Six: Tribute 1234, DefCount
6 plain), 1401 Kit Tribute Strong (1956 Strong Six: Tribute -1, TechLevel
4, Strength-1000 defenders, DefCount 1062 = six in waves of two), 1402
Kit Tribute Fed (1957 Fed Four: Tribute 0, TechLevel 3, the STOCK düde 130
Lone Big Federation Ship, DefCount 1042), 1406 Kit Tribute Huge (1961
Huge Six: Strength-30000 defenders, 1062); linked 1406 - 1400 - 1401 -
1402. Pilots `w39_*`: the Kit Lancer (Strength 100) with the Kit Escort
Gun and Kit Beam turrets, 100,000 credits. `tools/tribute.sh` (demand,
shots every 3 s, N rounds of `r` + Space 1.5 s, a second demand),
`domreset.sh`, `waves.sh`; `tools/reds.mjs` counts the red defenders per
frame.

| run | planet (fleet count in the pilot) | rating | reply (STR# 3002, one-based) | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ts12800_a, tp12800_a, tf12800_a, th12800_a | Strong / Plain / Fed / Huge (**0**) | 12,800 | #26 "All right, all right already!  The planet agrees to pay you tribute." | Dominated at once (Strong Six's 6,000 and Huge Six's 180,000 of Strength, the stock Fed düde: no difference) |
| tp6400_l, tp6400_f | Plain Six (6) | 6,400 | #8 "Surrender? To you? Ha ha ha!" | Status: Hostile, nothing launched (60 s watched); the port still took the landing (MinStatus -32767) |
| tpcrim12800_a | Plain Six (6), record -1000 | 12,800 | #15 "Eat vacuum, sucker - our defense fleet is on its way." | Hostile; **all six** launched |
| tp12800_f | Plain Six (6) | 12,800 | #14 "We're sending out our defense fleet. In a few minutes you'll be begging for mercy." | Hostile; **all six** up 1.8 s after the channel closed (the dialog pauses the game); the turrets killed all six; the second demand: #26, **Dominated** |
| ts12800_f | Strong Six (6, waves of 2) | 12,800 | #15 | Hostile; **two** launched; both killed by 91 s; no other ship for the next 57 s; the second demand: #26, **Dominated** |
| th12800_f | Huge Six (6, waves of 2) | 12,800 | #14 | Hostile; two launched |
| tpcrim_a | Plain Six (6), record -1000, no demand | 0 | - | 50 s: nothing launched; landed normally |

**The pay** (`payA_a`, `payB_a`: dominated set in the pilot, two landings
and Leaves at Plain Six; `domr_a`):

| pilot | dominated | credits per day |
|---|---|---|
| payA | Strong Six (Tribute -1, TL 4) and Fed Four (Tribute 0, TL 3), the player at the UNdominated Plain Six | 100,000 -> 107,000 -> 114,000: **4,000 + 3,000** |
| payB | Plain Six (Tribute 1234) | 100,000 -> 101,234 -> 102,468 |
| domr_a | Plain Six, dominated by fighting | Leave 101,234; jump to Kit Tribute Strong **102,468**; jump back **103,702** |

**Leaving** (`domr_a`): dominated by fighting at Plain Six, landed, Leave,
flown out, jumped to Kit Tribute Strong and straight back: the hail reads
**Status: Dominated** with Greetings / Release / Close Channel (Offer
Bribe / Release while the planet had been hostile, right after the
fight). The pulled pilot (after the landing) holds dominated = true and
the planet's fleet count **0**; a pilot with a dominated planet and a
count of 6 written in it reads 0 after one Leave (payB): a dominated
stellar's count is zeroed. The undominated planets' counts never moved
(6 / 4 throughout).

**Findings.**
1. **The demand's three outcomes**: combat rating below 12,800 (wave 38's
   edge) -> a laugh (#6-10) and the planet turns hostile, no launch; from
   12,800 with defence ships LEFT -> one of #11-15 ("...defense fleet..."),
   the planet turns hostile and launches its first wave (the whole fleet
   when DefCount is a plain count; one wave of the DefCount's last digit
   otherwise); from 12,800 with **no ships left** -> #26 / #27 and the
   stellar is dominated.
2. **One destroyed wave ends the fleet**: at Strong Six (six in waves of
   two) only the first wave of two launched; once both were dead the
   pilot's count for the planet read **0** (`waves_a` pull w1, after a
   landing), no second wave ever launched (57 s and a landing later), and
   the next demand was accepted (twice: `ts12800_f`, `waves_a`). So the
   "waves" never followed one another in these runs: GUESS that the
   original zeroes the count when the launched ships are all destroyed
   (the Bible's waves would need a player who leaves mid-fight; not run).
3. Neither the fleet's Strength (120 to 180,000) nor the player's ship
   Strength nor a criminal record changes the outcome; a criminal record
   alone launches nothing (50 s).
4. **Tribute**: the field when it is 1 or more (1,234 exactly); 0 and -1
   both pay **1,000 x TechLevel** (Bible); wave 38's 5,000 was simply the
   kit's Tribute field.
5. **Every dominated stellar pays every day**, wherever the player is: the
   payment comes with each date advance (a Leave, and each hyperspace
   jump: two jumps paid twice).
6. **A domination survives leaving** (a jump out and back, landings, days)
   and a dominated stellar's defence count is zeroed.
7. **The record**: every demand that is not laughed at costs **-600** in
   the planet's system (the fleet answer and the acceptance alike; spread
   0.65 per jump as usual), and the defenders' kills cost **nothing** and
   add **nothing** to the combat rating: `waves_a` read -600 after the
   fleet answer and two kills, -1,200 after the acceptance with no further
   kill; `domr_a` -1,200 after one fleet answer, six kills and the
   acceptance; the rating stayed 12,800 throughout (gövt 290: Kill 100,
   Disab 50, Board 50; GUESS that 600 is fixed, not 6 x KillPenalty).

**Wave 38 corrected.** Its edge (a laugh below 12,800, acceptance from
12,800) stands for a planet whose fleet is gone; with a fleet left, the
12,800 demand gets the fleet instead (wave 38's "accepted outright ...
no defence fleet ever launched" was the pilot's zero count). Its 5,000
was the kit's Tribute field.

**NovaJS (main 2c297e21).** Not implemented: Demand Tribute is drawn grey
(`N/spaceport/hail_layout.ts:237-258`), the domination seam is noted at
`N/nova_plugin/reputation/hail.ts:1740-1742` and
`novadatainterface/src/planet_data.ts:104-106`, and the defence fleet is
parsed (`PlanetDefenseFleet`, `planet_data.ts:42`) but never launched.
**Proposed** (for #353), replacing wave 38's proposal:
- per player, each stellar's defence ships LEFT, initialised from the
  DefCount total and zeroed when the stellar is dominated;
- Demand Tribute live on any inhabited stellar; below rating 12,800: a
  laugh (STR# 3002 6-10) and the stellar hostile to the player for the
  visit; from 12,800 with ships left: STR# 3002 11-15, the stellar
  hostile, its first wave launched (the whole fleet for a plain count,
  the last digit's wave otherwise), the count zeroed once the launched
  ships are destroyed (GUESS, finding 2); from 12,800 with none left:
  STR# 3002 26 / 27 (planet / station) and dominated;
- -600 to the record in the stellar's system per answered demand (fleet
  or acceptance, GUESS: fixed), nothing for the defenders' kills;
- every dominated stellar pays its Tribute (or 1,000 x TechLevel for 0 /
  -1) at EVERY day's advance (a departure, a jump), wherever the player
  is; a domination lasts across systems and days until Release (STR#
  3002 36 / 37).

Confidence: high for findings 1, 4, 5, 6 (exact credits, pulled pilots,
eleven fleet / no-fleet demands); medium for 2 and 7 (two runs each).

### The player's afterburner (U4), wave 39: about 1.5 x the top speed, it thrusts on its own (no Up needed), and the coast back down takes about 2.5 s at roughly half the hull's acceleration (2026-11-26)

**Rig.** Kit Probe A (Speed 300, Accel 300, inertial) with the stock
Afterburner (oütf 197), regular play, Kit Range. One keys step: Up 8 s
(top speed), z 5 s (Up held), z up, Up 8 s more, Up up; 4 s; z alone 3 s;
4 s; later Up 3 s, z 2 s, both released. Speed from the star field's
shift, 1 s vector means (`tools/starshift.mjs`; the stars move with the
camera at the ship's speed: wave 38's Speed 800 read 345-360 px/s).

| phase | px a frame (1 s means) |
|---|---|
| top speed, Up only | 3.9-4.4 (4.05 mean over 27-35 s; 130 px/s, wave 10) |
| z held with Up (18-23 s) | 5.8-6.4 (**6.1**) |
| z released, Up held | 6.2 -> 5.5 -> 4.5 -> 3.7: back to top speed about **2.5 s** after the release |
| z alone after Up released (35-38 s) | 4.1 -> **6.1-6.2**: the burner thrusts by itself |
| its release | 6.2 -> 5.9 -> 4.6 -> 4.1 in about 2.5 s, and the ship coasts on at top speed |
| z 2 s from cruise, then both released (48-50 s) | 4.5 -> 6.9 -> 5.8 -> 4.6 -> 3.7 |

**Findings.**
1. The afterburner raises the top speed by about **1.5 x** (6.1 / 4.05;
   one hull, so 1.5 x vs "+ a constant" is not separated).
2. It **thrusts by itself**: z alone accelerates the ship.
3. **The coast-down**: about 2.5 s from the boosted 6.1 back to 4.0, i.e.
   about 25 px/s², roughly **half** the hull's own acceleration (the ramp
   from rest: 0 -> 4.5 in about 2.5 s, about 54 px/s², wave 10's 59).

**NovaJS (main 2c297e21):** `AFTERBURNER_FACTOR` 2
(`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:21`): **mismatch** (1.5);
it thrusts while held (`:105-114`): **matches**; the overspeed bleeds at
`OVERSPEED_DECAY_FACTOR` 1 x the hull's acceleration (`:50`): **about
twice the original's rate**. **Proposed:** AFTERBURNER_FACTOR 1.5 and
OVERSPEED_DECAY_FACTOR 0.5 (GUESS from one hull; a second hull would
separate a factor from an added constant). The star shift steps in whole
pixels at 30 fps, so each 1 s mean is good to about ±0.3 px. Confidence:
medium.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w39/u4_a/`
(`recording.mp4`), `u4.shift.txt`.

### Jump phases on a slow hull (U8), wave 39: the sequence takes the SAME time on a Turn-10 / Accel-100 hull as on the Kit Jump Lancer (4.73 s from rest, 5.53 / 5.77 s from cruise), the slow hull turning at its own rate almost to the end and accelerating only in the last half second (2026-11-26)

**Rig.** shïp 595 Kit Jump Slow (inertial, Speed 200, Accel 100, Turn 10
= 29 deg/s, Fuel 300) on wave 38's Kit Jump A Start (2000 px east of Kit
Jump A's centre, linked to Kit Jump B). Pilot `w39_u8s`: `\`, j (from
rest), wait 30 s; `\`, j (arrived at top speed: from cruise); again.
`tools/jumpsum.sh` (the white arrival frame and the fuel bar) and
`tools/changes.mjs` (frames where the ship's 80 px crop changes: a
rotation step every 10.3 frames at 29 deg/s).

| jump | press -> flash | the ship's crop |
|---|---|---|
| j1, from rest | 378 -> 520: **142 frames, 4.73 s** | rotation steps every 10-11 frames from 387 to 501 (about 3.8 s, about 110 deg), the moon under it moving only from 509; departure at 520 |
| j2, from cruise | 1485 -> 1651: **166 frames, 5.53 s** | rotation steps every 10 frames from 1493 to 1641; departure at 1651 |
| j3, from cruise | 2536 -> 2709: **173 frames, 5.77 s** | rotation steps from 2545 to 2702; departure at 2709 |

Wave 38's Kit Jump Lancer (Turn 60, Accel 2000): 4.80 s from rest (a
0.67 s turn, a 0.43 s hold, 3.47 s of acceleration), 5.73 s from cruise.
The fuel came off on the flash frame each time (148 -> 98 -> 48 -> 0 px).

**Findings.**
1. The sequence's length does **not** depend on the hull: about 4.7-4.8 s
   from rest and 5.5-5.8 s from cruise for a 6x slower-turning, 20x
   slower-accelerating hull.
2. The slow hull spends nearly all of it **turning at its own rate**
   (still stepping 0.3 s before the flash) and accelerates only for the
   last half second: the departure comes at a fixed time, not at the end
   of a fixed acceleration phase.
3. GUESS: the original runs a fixed clock (about 4.7 s from rest, about
   0.8-1 s more from cruise for the brake) and the ship turns / burns
   inside it; it departs on time whether or not it has finished turning
   (j1 had about 110 of the needed turn done; the arrival heading is set
   by the arrival rule anyway).

**NovaJS (main 2c297e21; 5bf2f895): mismatch for slow hulls.** The player
turns at the hull's rate, then waits `JUMP_SPINUP_DELAY_MS` 400 and burns
`JUMP_DEPART_DELAY_MS` 3400 (`N/nova_plugin/travel/jump_plugin.ts:52,
57`): 4.8 s only for a hull that turns in about 1 s; this hull would take
about 4-6 s of turning plus 3.8 s. **Proposed:** depart at a fixed time
from the press (about 4.75 s from rest; braking adds its own time, about
0.8-1 s from cruise), with the turn at the hull's rate and the burn
filling what is left (GUESS on how the burn is cut when the turn runs
long). Confidence: medium (three jumps on one slow hull; the turn's start
angle is not measured).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w39/u8s_a/`
(`recording.mp4`, `j1.txt`..`j3.txt`), `scratchpad u8s_j1.png` copied to
`u8s_a/j1sheet.png`.

### spöb Gravity (U7), wave 40: Gravity is an ACCELERATION toward the stellar (away for a negative one), roughly in proportion to the field (Gravity 1: about 1 px a frame per second; 10: about 15), capped at the ship's own top speed; from Gravity 100 up the ship is at top speed in a frame and held on the well; weak wells make it swing through; no falloff seen out to 2,000 px; an inertialess ship is not moved at all (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue U7): the unit of spöb Gravity and its falloff.

**Rig** (`wave40Resources` "U7"; no traffic). sÿst 1408 Kit Gravity 100 (the
well, spöb 1963, Gravity 100, at the centre; decoration start points 1964 /
1965 at 300 / 1,000 px east), 1409 Kit Gravity 1000 (1966; starts 1967 / 1968
/ 1969 at 300 / 1,000 / 2,000 px), 1410 Kit Gravity Push (1970, Gravity -1000;
start 1971 at 300 px). Pilots `w40_g*`: Kit Probe A (inertial, Speed 300: top
speed about 4.05-4.4 px a frame, waves 10 / 39) on the start point, or the Kit
Lancer (inertialess); added during the wave, sÿst 1422 / 1423 (Gravity 1 / 10,
start at 300 px) and Kit Probes B / C (Speed 600 / 200).
`scenarios/w40_space_early.json` (recording from before Enter Ship), 20 s
untouched. The ship's velocity from the star field's shift
(`tools/starshift.mjs`, 1 s means), its arrival from the well's position on
screen.

| run | well, start | motion |
|---|---|---|
| g100_300_a | Gravity 100, 300 px | toward the well at **4.6 px a frame from the first frame** (no ramp), on it 66 frames later (300 px); then held there (shift within ±1-4 px, a jitter) |
| g100_1000_a | Gravity 100, 1,000 px | **4.4 px a frame** for 228 frames (1,000 px), then held |
| g1000_300_a | Gravity 1000, 300 px | 4.5 px a frame, on the well about 66 frames later, held to the end (20 s) |
| g1000_1000_a | Gravity 1000, 1,000 px | 3.9-4.45 (1 s means), on the well about 7.5 s later |
| g1000_2000_a | Gravity 1000, 2,000 px | 3.8-4.4 for 15 s (about 2,000 px), then held |
| g1000_300L_a | Gravity 1000, 300 px, **Kit Lancer (inertialess)** | **did not move** (the well stayed 300 px off for 20 s) |
| gpush_300_a | Gravity -1000, 300 px | AWAY from the well at **3.7-3.9 px a frame** for the whole 20 s (about 2,300 px), no slowing |
| g1_300_a (added: sÿst 1422) | **Gravity 1**, 300 px | a RAMP: 1 px a frame by 0.1 s, 2 by 1.2 s, 3 by 2.6 s, 4-5 by 3.6 s (about 1 px a frame per second); through the well at about 9 s and swinging back (-2 to -4 px a frame) |
| g10_300_a (sÿst 1423) | **Gravity 10**, 300 px | 5 px a frame within 0.3 s (about 15 px a frame per second), through the well at 2.6 s, then a damped swing (sign flips every 1-1.5 s, amplitude 5 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1) |
| g100_300B_a | Gravity 100, 300 px, **Kit Probe B** (Speed 600) | **8.6 px a frame** (its top speed), on the well in about 1.2 s, held |
| g100_300C_a | Gravity 100, 300 px, **Kit Probe C** (Speed 200) | **2.5-2.9 px a frame** (its top speed), on the well in about 3.5 s, held |

**Findings.**
1. Gravity ACCELERATES an inertial ship toward the stellar, roughly in
   proportion to the field (Gravity 1: about 1 px a frame per second, i.e.
   about 30 px/s²; Gravity 10: about 15 px a frame per second), and the speed
   is capped at the ship's own top speed (Probes A / B / C: 4.4 / 8.6 / 2.7
   px a frame at Gravity 100).
2. From Gravity 100 up the cap is reached within a frame or two, so the ship
   comes in at top speed, and the same pull reverses it within a frame on
   the far side: it sits ON the well (a few-pixel jitter). Weak wells (1,
   10) let it swing through and back, damped.
3. No falloff with distance at Gravity 100 / 1000 (300 to 2,000 px alike);
   the weak wells were run only from 300 px.
4. A negative Gravity pushes the ship away at about the same speed (3.8 px
   a frame) with no falloff seen out to 2,600 px.
5. An inertialess hull is not affected at all (like the Bible's tractor
   beams).

**NovaJS (main 6d529ae0):** spöb Gravity is parsed and never used
(`novadatainterface/src/planet_data.ts:408-413`, tracker #306); no stock
stellar has Gravity (`N/nova_plugin/core/stellar_defense_stock_test.ts:99`),
so it matters only to plug-ins. **Proposed** (when #306 is taken up): each
tick, an inertial ship gains about Gravity x 1 px a frame per second (GUESS =
30 x Gravity px/s²) toward the stellar (away for negative), the speed clamped
at the ship's top speed; inertialess ships exempt. Not measured: falloff for
weak wells, several wells in one system, whether thrust can fight it, the
exact damping (GUESS: the ordinary top-speed clamp is the only brake).
Confidence: medium for the shape (eleven runs, four hulls), low for the
constant.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w40/g*_a/`
(`recording.mp4`); the star-shift series were run with `tools/starshift.mjs`.

302 / 303 / 304 Kit Fade Bolt F1 / F4 / F0 (an unguided bolt, Speed 100,
Count 90, Falloff 1 / 4 / 0). Two shots each, 5 s apart. Per recording
frame (30 fps): the green / orange pixel count, their brightness sum and the
farthest one's distance from the ship (`tools/colorcount.mjs`,
`tools/beams.sh`).

| weapon | shot 1 | shot 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Plain Beam (Count 30) | frames 265-280: **16 frames**, 1,560 px, length 301 throughout | 419-434: 16 |
| Decay Beam (Count 30, Decay 5, Falloff 4) | 248-264 full (1,492 px, length 300), 265-270 **thinning** to 1,201 px (-20%) at length **300**: **23 frames** | 402-418 full, 419-424 thinning: 23 |
| Fade Bolt F0 | 238 to ~329: **about 90 frames**, full brightness to the end | 392 to ~485 |
| Fade Bolt F1 | 258 to 338: full (sum ~3,300) to ~322, then down to 0 by ~340: **about 80 frames** visible | 413 to 493 (80) |
| Fade Bolt F4 | 254 to 318: full to ~312, gone by 318: **about 64 frames** | 409 to 473 (64) |

**Findings.**
1. **Beam Count is not 1/30 s frames**: Count 30 showed for 16 recorded
   frames (0.53 s) on both beams, both shots; the decay tail added 7 (0.23
   s). The ratio fits the Bible's "Count + 16 - CoronaFalloff" (30 : 42)
   counted at the game's ~56 Hz drawing rate (16 / 30 x 56 = 30; 23 / 30 x
   56 = 43). GUESS: beam lifetimes tick per drawn frame, not per 1/30 s.
2. **A Decay beam does not shrink**: its length stayed 300 px to the last
   frame; only its corona thinned (pixel count -20% over the tail).
3. **Sprite fade**: Falloff 0 (no fade) lived about 90 frames = Count 90 at
   30 a second and vanished at once. Falloff 1 faded over the last ~16
   visible frames and was gone by ~80; Falloff 4 by ~64. A fade that STARTS
   32 frames before the end and runs Falloff times faster fits both (alpha
   1 - F (t - (Count - 32)) / 32: invisible at the counting threshold,
   alpha 0.35, by 79 for F1 and 63 for F4); a fade over the LAST 32 / F
   frames would keep F4 bright to about 87.

**NovaJS (main 6d529ae0): two mismatches, one match.**
- Beam life: `beamShrinkFraction`
  (`N/display/beam_display_plugin.ts:32-60`) keeps Count in 1/30 s (1.0 s
  for Count 30) and SHRINKS the length linearly over the tail. **Proposed:**
  keep the beam at full length for its whole life and thin the corona over
  the tail; the Count unit (about 1/56 s here) wants one more check before
  any change (a hub question: is it the drawing rate?).
- Sprite fade: `N/display/projectile_fade_plugin.ts:30-55` fades over the
  final `32 / falloff` frames (ending at the Count). **Proposed:** start the
  fade 32 frames before the end for every Falloff and run it Falloff times
  faster, so a Falloff-4 sprite is gone 24 frames early. Confidence: medium
  (a pixel-threshold reading, two shots each).
- Falloff 0 and the bolt's Count: **match**.

### Ionization's cap and the afterburner (E6 leftovers), wave 40: a Deionize-50 hull was STILL ionized 150 s after leaving the ion gun (a charge capped at IonizeMax 100 would drain in about 7 s), so the charge is not capped; the afterburner still works on a saturated hull (2026-11-26)

**Rig** (`wave40Resources` "E6"). shïp 604 Kit Ring Ion D50 (the Kit Ring
Ion: IonizeMax 100, **Deionize 50** = 0.5 a frame, 15 a second) with the Kit
Beam Turret and the stock Afterburner; pilot `w40_e6d` at Kit Port with bit
9046 (wave 6's immobile Ion Target Near, Ionization 200 a hit every 10
frames). Land, accept, Leave; 4 s by the gun; z 2.5 s; Tab, Space (meant to
kill the gun); Right held 150 s. Headings per frame (`tools/headings.mjs`,
`SPOKE=vw`), speed from the star shift.

**What happened.** The afterburner carried the saturated hull away from the
gun at once (from about 2 px a frame to well above its top speed in under
2 s; the star shift aliases at that speed, so no exact figure), the turret
then had nothing in range (the Ion Target stayed at Armor 100%), and the hull
sat far from the gun with Right held: **10 deg net in 150 s** (no turn), its
ring BLUE (ionized) in every sampled frame to the end. It had been hit for
about 14 s (about 40 hits of 200).

**Findings.**
1. **The charge is not capped at IonizeMax** (wave 39's GUESS, now
   measured): at 15 a second, 100 would drain in 6.7 s, but the hull was
   still fully ionized (no turn) 150 s later, i.e. it held more than 2,300;
   40 hits of 200 (8,000) would last about 9 minutes.
2. **A saturated charge does not block the afterburner**: z moved the
   unturnable hull off at high speed.
3. The turn's scaling with the charge is still not read (the drain was too
   slow to reach the half line in the run).

**NovaJS (main 6d529ae0):** the charge is clamped to IonizeMax by the
recharge system (`N/nova_plugin/ship/health_plugin.ts:88`, "decay-and-clamp",
`N/nova_plugin/ship/ionization_plugin.ts:128-132`): **mismatch**.
**Proposed:** let the ion charge pile up past IonizeMax (each hit adds its
Ionization), keep "fully ionized" at or above IonizeMax and the half-line
release, and drain at Deionize / 100 a frame; the afterburner is unaffected
(matches today). Confidence: medium-high for the cap (one 150 s run on top
of wave 39's 50 s), high for the afterburner.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w40/e6d_a/`
(`recording.mp4`), `e6d.head.txt`.

| run | closed planet | first `l` | second `l` |
|---|---|---|---|
| r17_a / r17c_a | (300, 0) | (the click missed: (716, 302) is on the HUD; both relanded at the origin) | |

Demand Tribute, Close Channel), 6 s, `r` + Space (meant to kill one
defender), Up held 17 s (out past 1,000 px), `\` `j`, and in the SAME keys
step 7.5 s later `\` `j` back; then shots every 3 s, four Tabs, a second
demand, four Tabs. Recording frames and the radar (`tools/radarseries.mjs`)
read the rest.

| t (s) | what happened |
|---|---|
| 22 | "Eat vacuum, sucker - our defense fleet is on its way.", Hostile |
| 37 | two red defenders up beside the player |
| 39-47 | `r` + Space; two defenders still up 3 s and 8 s later (a kill, if any, was replaced at once, as in wave 40) |

| 77 / 84 | the return jump went through: "Jumping into the Kit Tribute Leave system on June 25th" |

### Ionization below a full charge (E6 leftover), wave 41: with Deionize 1 the hull was ion-tinted from the SECOND 20-point hit (about 40 of IonizeMax 100) and turned 0 deg/s through 70 s of Right held; with Deionize 0 it was NEVER tinted, yet every hit cut the turn for about a second (to about 58 then 68 deg/s, back to 87 within 20-30 frames) (2026-11-26)

**Question** (wave-40 leftover): how does the turn cut scale with the ion
charge below a full charge?

**Rig** (`wave41Resources` "E6"). sÿst 1428 Kit Ion Tick Range: mïsn 1031
(bit 9266) puts shïp 628 Ion Tick Target (wave 6's immobile ion target)
on the port, firing wëap 305 Kit Ion Tick (one turreted bolt, Ionization
**20**, Reload 60). Pilots `w41_e6` (shïp 629 Kit Ring Ion D0: the Kit Ring
Ion with IonizeMax 100, **Deionize 0**) and `w41_e6b` (wave 39's shïp 596
Kit Ring Ion, **Deionize 1**). Land, accept, Leave; move about 150 px off
the planet (Up 0.6 s, Down 0.9 s); Right held 40 s + 30 s. Hits read off the
recording as the bolt reaching the player (`tools/colorcount.mjs` orange);
headings per frame (`tools/headings.mjs`, `SPOKE=vw`), folded on the hits
(`e6.head.txt`, `e6.bolts.txt`); the ring's colour in a 40 px box (cyan
vs ion blue).

**The hits** came every **108-111 recorded frames (3.6 s)** in both runs,
not every 60 frames (2 s) as Reload 60 reads (the AI's own pacing; the
turret was always in range).

| run | ring colour | turn with Right held |
|---|---|---|
| e6_a (Deionize 0) | cyan (never ion-tinted) in 70 s and about 20 hits | 81.7 deg/s on average; folded on the hits: **58** deg/s in the first 10 frames after a hit, **68** in the next 10, then 78-93 (about the control's 87.8) until the next hit |
| e6b_a (Deionize 1) | cyan after the first hit (frame 842), **ion blue from the second** (frame 953), flickering blue to the end | **0** deg/s (the heading never moved in 70 s) |

**Findings.**
1. **Deionize 0 is not "no drain"**: twenty hits never tinted the hull,
   and each hit's turn cut was gone within about 20-30 frames, so the
   charge drained at roughly 1 a frame (GUESS: Deionize 0 falls back to a
   default of about 100, i.e. 1 a frame; Deionize 1 is 0.01 a frame, as
   wave 39 assumed).
2. **A charge far below the half line already slows the turn**: about 20
   of 100 (no tint) cut it to about two thirds for a few frames,
   recovering as it drained. So the turn cut is not "nothing until the
   half line" (NovaJS's GUESS), but this run cannot give the curve's shape
   (headings come in 10 degree steps, so 10-frame windows scatter by
   +-30 deg/s; 19 hits folded).
3. **The tint came at about 40 of 100** (the second 20-point hit with
   Deionize 1), below the half line NovaJS uses for "ionized"; and from
   there on (about 40-80 and up, with a hit every 3.6 s) the hull did not
   turn at all. Wave 39's "saturated = no turn" therefore already holds
   from the tint on (GUESS: the tint marks "ionized" at about IonizeMax x
   0.4 or less, and an ionized hull does not turn).

**NovaJS (main e047c530):** `N/nova_plugin/ship/ionization_plugin.ts:22-30`, `:111-115`
(ionized above HALF of IonizeMax) and the slowdown (`:80-98`) "linear in the charge
from the half line to IonizeMax" (GUESS); the stat's Deionize is
used as given, 0 = no drain (`N/nova_plugin/ship/ship_plugin.ts:381`). **Mismatches:** (a) Deionize 0 drains (about 1
a frame) in the original; (b) "ionized" (tint, and with it no turn) starts
at about 40 of 100, not above 50; (c) a sub-threshold charge already cuts
the turn. **Proposed:** treat Deionize 0 as 100 (GUESS from the drain time);
mark ionized at charge >= 0.4 x IonizeMax (GUESS: the measured 40 could be
anything in 20-40) with the full cut (turn 0, accel a third) there; below
it, scale the turn by (1 - 1.5 x charge / IonizeMax) as a first fit to the
58-68 deg/s dips (GUESS). Confidence: high for (a) and for "no turn once
tinted"; medium for the 40 tint point (one run); low for the sub-threshold
curve.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w41/e6_a/`,
`e6b_a/` (`recording.mp4`, `e6b_c.png`), `e6.head.txt`, `e6.bolts.txt`,
`e6b.bolts.txt`.

### Gravity damping and strength (U7, the hub's questions), wave 41: no damping: a Probe A swinging through a Gravity-5 or Gravity-10 well kept its peak speed (about 5-6 px a frame) for 75 s; what wave 40 read as a damped swing is the swing turning from x into y and back; the pull from rest reached top speed in about 0.7 s at Gravity 5 and 0.27 s at Gravity 10 (about 39 and 55 px/s² per unit) (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (the hub, on the wave-40 combat fix): does a ship swinging in a
weak well with no input lose amplitude over 30-60 s? And the per-unit
strength at Gravity 5 against 10.

**Rig.** Kit Probe A (inertial, Speed 300 / Accel 300) on a decoration
300 px east of the well, no input for 75 s, recorded from before Enter
Ship (`scenarios/w41_space_early.json`): sÿst 1438 Kit Gravity 5 (added:
spöb 1998 the well, Gravity 5; spöb 1999 the start; pilot `w41_g5`) and
wave 40's sÿst 1423 Kit Gravity 10 (pilot `w40_g10_300`). Velocity from
the star field's shift per frame (`tools/starshift.mjs`, `g5_a.shift.txt`,
`g10_a.shift.txt`), peak |vx| / |vy| per 2 s window.

| t after Enter Ship (s) | Gravity 5 peak vx / vy (px a frame) | Gravity 10 peak vx / vy |
|---|---|---|
| 1-10 | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 (one 15 is a misread) |
| 12-20 | 5 -> 3 / 2-4 | 5-6 / 0-2 |
| 20-28 | 2 -> 1 / **5-6** | 3 -> 1 / **5** |
| 30-40 | 2-4 / 5-8 | 2-4 / 2-5 |
| 40-56 | **5-6** / 1-2 | 1-2 / 6 then 4-7 / 1-2 |
| 56-70 | 4 -> 1 / 4-5 | 3-5 / 3-5 |

(Single-frame 15-30 readings are star-match misreads and are left out.)

**Findings.**
1. **No damping in 75 s.** The swing's peak speed stays at about 5-6 px a
   frame throughout; only its DIRECTION turns: the x component falls to
   about 1 while the y component grows to about 5-6, then back (about a
   40 s cycle at Gravity 5). Wave 40's "damped swing (5 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1)" at
   Gravity 10 was the first 20 s of that turn, read on one axis.
   GUESS: the ship falls through the well slightly off centre each pass,
   and the orbit precesses; nothing takes energy out except the top-speed
   cap.
2. **The pull from rest**: Gravity 5 took the ship 1 -> 5 px a frame in
   about 0.7 s (about 6.5 px a frame per second, 195 px/s², **39 px/s² per
   unit**); Gravity 10 in about 0.27 s (about 18 px a frame per second, 550
   px/s², **55 px/s² per unit**; wave 40's estimate was 15 px a frame per
   second, 45 per unit); wave 40's Gravity 1 gave about 30 per unit. The
   per-unit pull grows with the field, or the short ramps at 5 and 10
   (integer px steps, 8-20 frames) overstate it; a Gravity-5 ramp at 2,000
   px out would be cleaner.

**NovaJS (main e047c530, 007b23eb):** `N/nova_plugin/travel/gravity_plugin.ts:37-42`
adds GRAVITY_ACCELERATION (`:58`, 30 px/s² per unit) x Gravity each tick
toward the well, linear in the field, with the ordinary top-speed clamp as
the only brake: **matches** on damping (none; its comment's "Weak wells let
it swing through and back, damped", `:30-31`, should drop "damped").
The constant: 30 a unit fits Gravity 1 only; Gravity 5 / 10 read about 39 /
55. **Proposed:** keep it linear (GUESS) but raise the constant toward 40,
or measure a Gravity-5 ramp from far out before changing it. Confidence:
medium-high for "no damping" (two runs, 75 s each), low for the constant.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w41/g5_a/`,
`g10_a/` (`recording.mp4`), `g5_a.shift.txt`, `g10_a.shift.txt`.

### Beam Count's unit (E10, the hub's question), wave 41: Count 60 showed for 32 recorded frames and Count 10 for 5, two taps each (wave 40: Count 30, 16): the beam lasts Count / 56 s, about one unit per frame of the game's 56 fps drawing (2026-11-26)

**Question** (the hub, on the wave-40 fix): wave 40 read about 1/56 s per
Count unit from one beam (Count 30, 16 recorded frames); is it a unit, or
an offset?

**Rig** (added during the wave). wëap 307 / 308 Kit Plain Beam C60 / C10
(wave 40's Kit Plain Beam 301, a fixed green beam with Decay 0, at Count
**60** / **10**) + oütf 488 / 489 on the Kit Ring Lancer at Kit Port
(pilots `w41_e10c60`, `w41_e10c10`); two Space taps 5 s apart. Frames with
the beam drawn (more than 20 beam-green pixels in the play area,
`tools/colorcount.mjs green`), from each press's recorded frame.

| Count | recorded frames (30 fps), each tap | seconds | s per unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 5, 5 | 0.167 | 1/60 |
| 30 (wave 40) | 16 | 0.533 | 1/56 |
| 60 | 32, 32 | 1.067 | 1/56 |

**Finding.** The duration is proportional to Count (no offset: 5 / 16 / 32
frames for 10 / 30 / 60), at about **Count / 56 s**: one unit per frame of
the game's own drawing rate (F12 reads about 56 fps on this iMac), not per
1/30 s tick. GUESS: the original counts a beam's life in drawn frames, so
on a faster machine a beam would be shorter; NovaJS should use a fixed
Count / 56 s (or the 1/60 s nominal of a 60 Hz Mac) rather than Count /
30.

**NovaJS (main e047c530): mismatch** by a factor of about 1.9. A beam's
Count is read as 30 Hz frames: `onScreenDuration: onScreenFrames * 1000 /
FPS` (`P/parsers/weapon_parse.ts:332-350`) and "A beam of Count frames
lives for exactly Count frames of ticks (two 60 Hz ticks per frame)"
(`N/nova_plugin/combat/beam_plugin.ts:189-195`), so Count 30 lasts 1 s
where the original's lasts 0.53 s. **Proposed:** beam life (and its damage
window) = Count / 56 s (GUESS: Count / 60 for a round nominal rate; the
Count-10 beam read 1/60 s a unit); the Decay tail likewise in 1/56 s
units. Confidence: high for the proportionality (three Counts, five taps),
medium for 56 against 60.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w41/e10c60_a/`,
`e10c10_a/` (`recording.mp4`).

**Question** (catalogue A6): do a warship (AI 3) and an interceptor (AI 4)
of a govt that holds the player as a criminal engage him whatever the
odds, or only within the govt's MaxOdds?

**Rig** (`wave41Resources` "A6"). gövt 284 Kit Odds Govt (CrimeTol 10,
**MaxOdds 100**, not xenophobic); sÿst 1436 Kit Odds Warship / 1437 Kit Odds
Interceptor (owner 284, avgShips 1 of düde 526 AI 3 / 527 AI 4: shïp 653 Kit
Odds Warship, a yellow disc of **Strength 100**, Shield 3,000, the Kit
Escort Gun turret), ports 1996 / 1997. Player hulls shïp 654 / 657 Kit Odds
Lancer **S50 / S200** (the Kit Lancer with that Strength, Shield 3,000, no
recharge), on the port, record **-1,000** in that system (hostile). 90 s
untouched, shots every 15 s, two Tabs.

| run | player Strength (odds against the NPC) | what the NPC did |
|---|---|---|
| a6w50_a, AI 3 | 50 (0.5) | attacked from the first shots: shield 100% -> about 75 / 60 / 40 / 20 / 10 / 0% at 15 s steps; Tab: "Kit Odds Warship", red brackets |
| a6w100_a, AI 3 | 100 (**1.0**) | attacked the same way: shield 100% -> 0 by 90 s, red brackets |
| a6w200_a, AI 3 | 200 (2.0) | **no attack**: it came by the port (twice in the shots) and was gone by 90 s (Tab: No Target); the shield bar never moved |
| a6i50_a, AI 4 | 50 (0.5) | attacked: shield 100% -> about 90 / 75 / 50% at 15 / 30 / 45 s (the run then hung on a lost connection; see the reliability notes) |
| a6i200_a, AI 4 | 200 (2.0) | **no attack**: parked ON the port (the yellow disc over the planet in every shot) for the whole 90 s; Tab: "Kit Odds Warship", **yellow** brackets, Shield 100%; the player's shield never moved |

**Findings.**
1. **MaxOdds gates an AI 3 warship's attack on a criminal player**: at
   enemy-to-own Strength 0.5 and at exactly 1.0 (MaxOdds 100) it engages,
   at 2.0 it does not and leaves the
   system like a warship with no enemy (the Bible's "jumps out if there
   aren't any"). The player counts by his hull's Strength field, as NPCs
   do (waves 33 / 37: MaxOdds between NPCs).
2. **An AI 4 interceptor obeys MaxOdds the same way**: it engaged at 0.5
   and at 2.0 "parks in orbit around a planet" (the Bible's idle
   interceptor), not even turning red.

**NovaJS (main e047c530):** the warship branch engages only if
`oddsFavorable(maxOdds, myStrength, chosenStrength)`
(`N/nova_plugin/npc/npc_decision.ts:935-975`, per pair, with the
shield-scaled `effectiveStrength`, `N/nova_plugin/reputation/
govt_disposition.ts:131-150`): **matches** the three warship runs
(0.5 and 1.0 engage: `<= maxOdds`; 2.0 does not); the interceptor branch
should hold the same rule (not checked here). Left: 1.01 (`w41_a6w101`)
to confirm the edge is inclusive and not a rounding. Confidence: high for
the warship cases (one run each, unambiguous), medium for AI 4 at 0.5.

**Question** (catalogue A12): do mission goal ships other than chase-off
targets linger in the system, before or after their goal is met? NovaJS
holds every goal ship but a chase-off target until its goal resolves.

**Rig** (`wave41Resources` "A12"). sÿst 1435 Kit A12 Range (port spöb 1995,
linked to 1431); mïsn 1033 (bit 9268, AvailLoc 3 at 1995, ReturnStel
1995) with ShipGoal **4 (observe)**, ShipBehav -1, ShipStart -1, one shïp
652 Kit A12 Observee (a yellow disc, AI 1, gövt 363 Kit Neutral, Speed 300,
fuel 3,000; düde 525). Pilot `w41_a12` (the Kit Lancer on the port). Land,
accept, Leave; 120 s untouched (shots every 15 s); Tab; 120 s more; `i`.
The disc read per half second off the recording (pure-yellow pixels away
from the player) and the radar (`tools/radarseries.mjs`).

| t after take-off (s) | what happened |
|---|---|
| 0-18 | no observee on screen or radar (it was on the port: GUESS landed, as AI 1 traffic placed at a stellar) |
| 18.5-22 | the yellow disc comes out from under the player (the port) and flies straight north off screen (about 12 px a frame) |
| 22-40 | one radar dot moving north, out to about 1,100 px |
| 40 on | **gone**: no dot for the remaining 3.5 minutes; Tab at 120 s: "No Target" |
| 286 | `i`: "Kit A12 observe" still ACTIVE (the goal never met) |

while its goal is outstanding: the AI 1 target behaved like ordinary AI 1

ships leave 30-40 s after appearing) and left, stranding the mission. So
the "after the goal" half of the question does not arise for this goal; a
mission author keeps an observe target around with its AI type (or a
ShipBehav), not through the goal.

**NovaJS (main e047c530): mismatch.** `N/nova_plugin/missions/
mission_ship_spawn.ts:97-116` and `:411-440` give every goal ship but a
chase-off target (and GOAL_NONE) a suppressed departure timer
(`MISSION_SHIP_NO_DEPART_MS`) and a SystemHoldComponent until the goal
resolves ("Goal targets must stick around to be fought/boarded/observed").
**Proposed:** do not hold an observe-goal (4) ship: let it keep its AI's
ordinary departure (GUESS for the other goals: the same, measured only for
observe; destroy / disable / board targets of AI 3/4 hunt or patrol anyway,
so a hold matters mostly for AI 1/2 targets). Confidence: medium-high for
observe (one run, unambiguous), low for extending it to other goals.

### DatePostInc on an immediate auto-abort (R16), wave 41: it IS applied: a DatePostInc-7 auto-abort mission moved the date a week further than its DatePostInc-0 twin (July 2 against June 25), and not at the accept: the pilot written at the Leave right after the accept still read June 24 with the mission active (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue R16): does an auto-abort mission's DatePostInc
advance the date ("after successful completion or auto-aborting", the
Bible), and when?

**Rig** (`wave41Resources` "R16"). mïsn 1034 / 1035 (bits 9269 / 9270,
AvailLoc 3 at Kit Port): Flags 0x0001 (auto-abort), one Kit Escort special
ship (wave 10's shape), **DatePostInc 7 / 0**. Pilots `w41_r16` / `w41_r16c`
(the Kit Lancer at Kit Port, June 23 1177). Land, accept, Leave (pull
`leave1`), 3 s in flight, `i`, land, Leave (the final pull).

| run | `leave1` (Leave after the accept) | after the take-off, a landing and a Leave |
|---|---|---|
| r16_a (DatePostInc 7) | June 24, mission **active** | **July 2**, no active mission |
| r16c_a (DatePostInc 0) | June 24, mission active | June 25, no active mission |

**Finding.** An immediate auto-abort applies its DatePostInc: seven extra
days (June 25 + 7 = July 2). It does not come at the accept: the pilot
written at the Leave that follows the accept is a day on (the Leave's
ordinary day) with the mission still active; the abort, and with it the
date jump, come after the take-off (wave 10: the abort fires when the
special ships appear, in flight).

**NovaJS (main e047c530):** `state.dateAdvance += Math.max(0,
mission.datePostInc)` at the ACCEPT of an immediate auto-abort
(`N/nova_plugin/missions/mission_accept_offer.ts:173`), while OnAbort
itself runs at the lift-off (`runLiftoffAutoAborts`, applied in 0cf672ea):
the week is **the same**, the moment **differs** (NovaJS's would already
show in a pilot saved at that Leave). **Proposed:** add DatePostInc where
OnAbort runs (the lift-off, `N/spaceport/mission_session.ts`), not at the
accept. The deferred (përs) auto-abort is still untested (no përs kit).
Confidence: high for the +7 (pilot dates), medium for the moment (one
pilot at the intermediate Leave).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w41/r16_a/`,
`r16c_a/` (`pilot-leave1/`, `pilot-after/`).

| run | weapon -> target | target panel after 3 s / 6 s / +1.5 s |
|---|---|---|
| e4pn_a | planet-type -> plain | **Shield 100% / 100% / 100%**, yellow brackets |

== ship.planetType (passing through otherwise, no damage, no provocation);
destroyable stellars take only planet-type fire (the Bible; not tested

### Map keys, minimap routes and ctrl-clicks (K4, M2, M3), wave 41: in the map `=` zooms in, `-` zooms out (like the - / + buttons) and `f` opens Find ("Enter the name of a system to find:"; Return centres and selects it); the `h` minimap draws a multi-jump route in strong green, clipped at its box, and keeps it (pale) beside a single jump picked on it; a ctrl-click on the minimap picks the system AND fires the selected secondary (ctrl is the secondary key), a ctrl-click in space fires it too; the minimap shows no borders (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (catalogue K4, M2, M3): the map's zoom and Find keys; a
multi-jump route and borders on the minimap; does a click with the
secondary key held on the minimap fire the secondary?

**Rig.** Wave 2's map region (sÿst 2140 Map Hub and its neighbours). Pilot
`w41_map` (wave 2's map pilot, the Kit Lancer at Map Hub) with a stock IR
Missile launcher and 10 missiles. One hand-driven run (`map_a`, shots plus
frames off the recording for the 2.2 s minimap peeks): `m`, shift-click
East, Void, Far (a three-jump route), Done, `h`; `w`; `h` and a ctrl-click
on the minimap's SW; a ctrl-click in empty space; `m`, `=`, `shift+=`, `-`,
`-`, the - button, the + button twice, `f`, the Find button, `text:"Map
Far"`, Return; Show Borders; Done; `h`.

| step | the original |
|---|---|
| the route, Done | a strong green route Hub -> East -> Void -> Far; nav "Hyperspace / Unexplored System" (East, the first hop) |
| `h` (frame 23 after the press) | the minimap with the route in strong green running off its right edge (clipped at the box) |
| `w` | "IR Missile - 10" |
| `h`, ctrl-click on SW | **"IR Missile - 9"** (a missile fired) and nav **"Hyperspace / Map SW"**; the minimap: a thin green line to SW (red brackets on it) and the multi-jump line still drawn, pale |
| ctrl-click in space | "IR Missile - 8" |
| `m` again | "Destination System: Map SW"; both routes drawn (strong east, thin SW) |
| `=` | zoomed IN one step |
| `shift+=` | no further change (already as far in as `=` went, or ignored: not separable) |
| `-`, `-` | out one step (back to the opening zoom), then out again (Map Far, Map Island in view) |
| - button, + button, + button | out one more step, then in two: the same steps as the keys |
| `f` | **the Find dialog**: "Enter the name of a system to find:", Cancel / Find (the Find button opens the same dialog) |
| type "Map Far", Return | the map re-centred on Map Far, "Destination System: Map Far", the Hub -> Far route drawn |
| Show Borders | blue and red borders; the button reads **"Hide Borders"** |
| Done, `h` | the minimap shows **no borders** (and the route to Far) |

**Findings.**
1. **K4**: `=` / `-` are the map's zoom keys (one step each, the same step
   as the - / + buttons); `f` opens Find; Find takes a system name and
   centres and selects it. (Escape is not sent by novaref.)
2. **M2**: the minimap draws a multi-jump route like the map (strong green),
   clipped at the box; a single jump picked on the minimap is drawn thin
   and the multi-jump route stays, pale; the minimap never shows borders.
3. **M3**: a click with the secondary key (ctrl) held fires the secondary,
   on the minimap as anywhere: the game reads the key, not the click (the
   click still picks the system).

**NovaJS (main e047c530).** The star map's keys are Done (`m` / depart),
Tab, Space and the arrows (`N/spaceport/starmap.ts:291-304`): **no `=` /
`-` zoom keys and no `f` for Find** (the buttons exist: `:285-290`):
**mismatch** (K4). The minimap's click rules (`N/spaceport/mini_map.ts:
36-48`: ctrl-click picks like a plain click) and secondary fire on the held
key: **match** as far as read (not run headless here). Proposed: bind `=`
(and `+`) / `-` to the zoom buttons' steps and `f` to the Find dialog while
the map is open. Confidence: high for the keys (shots), medium for the
pale multi-jump line (one frame).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w41/map_a/`
(`m1.png`, `m2.png`, `m3.png`, `mfs.png`: the minimap frames 1210 / 1680 /

| Return (accept) | 2.00M -> 1.99M; status line **"w41-r8, you're cleared to land. Commence final approach."** | the same |

| land on the open port, Leave (about 45 s after the payment) | | |
| `l` at the bribed port | **"Landing request denied."** | **"Landing request denied."** |
| hail | "What do you want?" / "What?", **Hostile**, Offer Bribe offered again | the same |
| jump out and back, `l` | "Landing request denied." | the same |

**Finding.** A paid planet bribe clears the player at once (the clearance
line comes with the payment) and is gone after his next landing (here at
the system's other port, about 45 s and one day later): the bribed port
denied him and was Hostile again on the comm, offering a new bribe. A
landing or the day's advance ends it, not a long clock (GUESS: it lasts
until the player lands anywhere; a 3-minute wait in flight would tell a
timer apart).

**NovaJS (main e047c530):** `STELLAR_BRIBE_MS` = 120,000 (2 minutes,
"TUNABLE / ASSUMPTION", `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts:545-554`),
read as `bribedUntil` (`N/nova_plugin/reputation/stellar_clearance.ts:
319-343`): **mismatch** (the original's ended within 45 s at a landing).
**Proposed:** keep a paid planet bribe until the player next lands (any
stellar) or leaves the system, with no clock (GUESS on the clock; the
landing end is measured twice). Confidence: high that a landing elsewhere
ends it (two runs), low on whether time alone does.

### The asteroid field after a landing (E9's "asteroid re-roll"), wave 42: NOT the same field each time: at the same ages after two take-offs from one port the rocks were in different places (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue E9): does the original give a system the same
asteroid field on every entry (NovaJS builds it from the system's seed), or
a new one?

**Rig.** Wave 4's Kit Rock Range 4 (sÿst 2170, Asteroids 4, every röid
type). Pilot `w42_rock` (the Kit Lancer at Kit Rock4 Port). Shots, land and
take off, shots, land and take off, shots; the first in-space frame after
each take-off read off the recording (frames 1025 and 1939), and the frames
2 s and 5 s after it.

**Result** (`rock_takeoffs.png`): at take-off both fields were out of view;
2 s after the first take-off three rocks sat up and to the right of the
port, 2 s after the second two came in from the left; at 5 s the first
showed four rocks to the north-east, the second four in a ring west and
south of the port. The start of the run (before any landing) showed yet
another layout.

**Finding.** The original does not hand back the same asteroid layout at a
take-off: the field after each landing is a different one (re-rolled, or
the old field moved on while the player was landed; one run cannot tell
these apart, but either way it is not a fixed per-system field).

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e):** `spawnAsteroids`
(`N/nova_plugin/combat/asteroid_plugin.ts:459-500`) draws the field "from
the world's deterministic Random (same system seed -> same field)" at
makeSystem, and the room seed (`N/nova_plugin/spawn/npc_spawn_plugin.ts:
1408-1427`) reseeds only what is drawn afterwards, so the INITIAL field is
the same on every entry, offline and online. **Mismatch (minor).**
**Proposed:** draw the initial field after `applyRoomSeed` (from the room's
Random) so each room instance gets its own layout, as NPC genesis already
does; offline, seed it per entry. Confidence: medium (one run, two
take-offs, clear difference); low on re-roll vs drift.

| a13r1m_a | 1,000,000 | **4.6-5.1 / 5.7-6.0** (whole run 4.8 / 5.7) | 200-265 px |

(Waves 15-18: the 0x0040 hull ran a median 5.3, p90 5.7; the plain hull

`npcAfterburning` (`N/nova_plugin/npc/npc_afterburner.ts:79-85`) burns only
for `alwaysHasAfterburner` (0x0040). **Proposed:** burn also when
`afterburnerAtAdvancedRating` and the TARGET player has a combat rating
above 0, in spells (GUESS: redraw every 20-30 s with a burn chance of
min(1, rating / 6,400)), with the same factor and attack-only rule; the
target's rating, not the room's (multiplayer, GUESS). Confidence: high for
rating 0 against a high rating (two clean runs, 4,300 frame pairs each),

`SPOKE=vw`, `V=1`), turn rate between hits (`tools/e6fold.py`); the tint
from the ring's colour in a 40 px box (`tools/ringtint.py`).

| hits so far (nominal charge) | ring | turn with Right held, deg/s, each inter-hit interval: e6c_a / e6c_b |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (the control, wave 39) | cyan | 87.8 |
| 1-4 (5-20) | cyan | 60.5, 58.4, 51.8, 69.0 / 69.7, 52.6, 60.1, 56.2 (mean **60**) |
| 5-12 (25-60) | **blue from the 5th hit** (frames 1847 / 1838, two frames after it), flickering | 28.2-31.8 (mean 29.6) / 27.3-31.7 (mean 29.8) |

**Findings.**
1. **The cut comes in steps, not a ramp**: about two thirds of the turn for

   at a third at a nominal 40-60, where the 20-point hull (here and in wave
   41) did not turn from a nominal 40. A drain between the hits reconciles
   them: with D points drained per 3.6 s interval, the 5-point tint at hit
   5 (but not 4) and the 5-point no-turn at hit 13 (but not 12) against the
   20-point no-turn by hit 2 need D > 2; Deionize 1 read as 0.01 a game
   frame at the original's 56 fps gives D = 2.0, and then the tint line is
   about 15-17 and the no-turn line about 38 of IonizeMax 100 (GUESS: 1/6
   and 3/8 of IonizeMax, or 0.15 / 0.4). The 20-point hull's tint after
   its first hit (20) fits (wave 41 read that ring as cyan; here it was blue
   at once).
3. The acceleration was not measured here (the hull turned in place).

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e):** `ionSlowdown`
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/ionization_plugin.ts:108-123`) ramps the turn
linearly from full at 0 to none at the ionized line, `ION_IONIZED_FRACTION`
0.3 (`:82`), and holds none (accel a third) above: **mismatch** in shape
(steps; a third of the turn, not none, between the tint and the second
line) and in the lines. **Proposed** (GUESS on the lines): ionized (tint)
at 0.16 x IonizeMax; turn x 2/3 for 0 < charge < 0.16, x 1/3 from 0.16 to
0.38, 0 above; the acceleration cut left as is; and the drain 0.01 x
Deionize a 1/56 s (or 1/60 s) frame, about 0.56-0.6 a second at Deionize 1,
where NovaJS reads it per 1/30 s frame (0.3 a second, `P/parsers/
ship_parse.ts:82-83`: half, and too slow for finding 2's D > 2), the same
frame-rate question as the beam's Count / 56 s (E10, wave 41). Confidence: high for the three plateaus (two identical
runs), medium for the lines (they rest on the guessed drain).

| D (100 / 300), `u4d_c` | 1.49, 1.51, 1.52, 1.44, 1.52 | 2.62, (1.58: a misread), 2.72 | 1.77 | 2.6, 2.2, 1.7, 2.1, 1.5, 1.7 |

**Findings.**

   39-42) is pulled toward 1. Taking the faster cluster instead

   scattered, and unreliable the other way.

   two cleanest readings across the waves are now A 1.5 (wave 39), B 1.75
   (wave 40) / 1.79 (here), C 1.34-1.53, D 1.73-1.77: no function of Speed
   (or Accel) fits them all (GUESS: a flat factor of about 1.6 is as good

3. **The coast-down with both keys released** takes 1-2 s on Probe C
   (Accel 600) and about 6 s or more on Probe B (Accel 150, still 11 px a

   with the hull's Accel (roughly half of it, as wave 40 found); wave 41's
   "Probe C stayed fast for 10 s with Up held" was not repeated: here it
   was back at top speed within 2 s.

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e):** `afterburnerFactor` = max(1.5, 1.25 + Speed /
1200) (`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:36-39`): D gets 1.5
where it read about 1.75. **Proposed:** no change on this evidence (the
reading cannot separate the candidates, and waves 39-41's factors that the

not use the stars: decoration rulers at known spacing (wave 30's moon
rulers) passed at cruise and at boost, timed off the recording. The coast-down at about half
the acceleration matches. Confidence: low for any factor rule; medium for
the coast-down's dependence on Accel.

1. **The pull falls off with distance.** From rest at 2,000 px the ship
   took about 9 s to reach its top speed (about 0.5 px a frame per second,
   15 px/s², while 2,000-1,450 px out); from 1,000 px about 3 s (about 1.5
   px a frame per second, 45 px/s²); wave 41 from 300 px about 0.7 s (195
   px/s²). Roughly 1 / d^1.5 (GUESS from three distances read in whole-pixel
   star steps). Waves 40-41's "no falloff out to 2,000 px" came from
   Gravity 100 / 1000, which reach the cap within a frame anywhere, so they
   could not show one.
2. **The fall-in levels off at the hull's top speed**: about 4.4 px a frame
   (1 s means 4.2-4.37 just before the well, Probe A's own 4.4), although
   the pull was growing as it closed. So the original DOES cap a gravity
   swing at the ship's top speed, as NovaJS's MovementSystem clamp does. The
   5-6 px a frame "peaks" wave 41 read (and the hub's fix agent quoted)
   were the per-frame maxima of whole-pixel star steps: in this run single
   frames read 6-7 while the 1 s mean sat at 4.4.

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e):** `gravityAcceleration` = 23 x G + 3.2 x G x |G|
px/s² (`N/nova_plugin/travel/gravity_plugin.ts:59-75`), applied the same at
any distance (`gravityDeltaV`, `:87-100`; the module comment's point 3, "No
falloff with distance", `:35-36`), with the top-speed clamp as the cap:
**matches** the cap (keep the clamp); **mismatch** on the falloff (NovaJS
pulls the Gravity-5 ship at 195 px/s² at 2,000 px, the original about
15). **Proposed:** keep the measured strength as the
value at 300 px and scale it by (300 / d)^1.5 (GUESS from three distances;
capped at, say, the 300 px value inside 300 px; with the top-speed cap,
strong wells still pin the ship at any range, as waves 40-41 saw), and
rewrite point 3 of the module comment. Confidence: high for the cap (a clean
plateau at top speed), medium for a falloff existing, low for its exponent.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w42/g5f_a/`,
`g5m_a/` (`recording.mp4`), `g5f.shift.txt`, `g5m.shift.txt`.

### Bay launch kicks under the fighter's top speed (E8 leftover), wave 42: a Speed-200 bay's fighter stopped about 18 px out; a FAST fighter (Speed 1000) from the Speed-400 bay coasted its kick at about 4.5 px a frame for about 0.8 s, out to about 140 px, then stopped within about 8 frames and came back (2026-11-26)

**Question** (wave-41 leftover): does the fighter's AI brake a kick that is
under its own top speed (a Speed-200 bay; a fast fighter from the Speed-400
bay)?

**Rig** (`wave42Resources` "E8"). wëap 310 Kit Disc Bay Slow (Speed 200,
carrying wave 40's Kit Bay Disc 602: Speed / Accel 300) + oütf 490; shïp 691
Kit Bay Disc Fast (the green disc at Speed / Accel 1000, Turn 60) carried by
wëap 311 Kit Fast Disc Bay (Speed 400) + oütf 491. Pilots `w42_e8s` /
`w42_e8ff` (the Kit Lancer at rest on Kit Port, four fighters). `w`, then two
launches 8 s apart; the first launch read per frame (`tools/greendisc.mjs`:
the green centroid's distance from the carrier, and its step).

| run, first launch | distance from the carrier per recorded frame (px) |
|---|---|
| e8s_a (Speed-200 bay, Kit Bay Disc) | 1.9, 0.8, 2.7, 5.9, 10.8, 10.3, 14.1, 15.3, 16.4, 16.8, 17.3, 17.7, **18.4** (0.45 s), then back in: 16.7, 15.3, 14.0, 11.5, ... 0.1 (1.1 s), and settled about 7 px off the carrier (the disc fully drawn, beside / over it) |
| e8ff_a (Speed-400 bay, Kit Bay Disc Fast) | 3.0, 2.9, 12.6, 19.1, 21.9, 25.1, 29.7, then **+4.5 a frame, steady** (37, 41.5, 46, 50.5, ... 126, 131) for about 25 frames, then 134, 137, 139, 141, 142, 143, 144, **145.6** (frame 374, 1.4 s), back at about 2.8 px a frame, then about 2 px a frame, and settled about 34 px out |

**Findings.**
1. **A Speed-200 kick (2 px a frame) is gone almost at once**: the Kit Bay
   Disc got about 18 px out (about half its 35 px from the Speed-400 bay,
   waves 40-41) and came straight back. With waves 40-41: rest at about 18 /
   35 px for kicks of 2 / 4 px a frame, i.e. roughly kick² / (2 x about 220
   px/s²) once the sprite-clearing frames are discounted, consistent with
   the fix's 200 px/s² brake.
2. **A fighter FASTER than its kick does not brake at once**: the Speed-1000
   disc held the 4 px a frame kick (read 4.5) for about 0.8 s, out to about
   130 px, and only then shed it, in about 8 frames (roughly 500 px/s²,
   its own Accel-1000 thrust), stopping about 145 px out. So the braking
   is the FIGHTER'S own (turn and thrust at its Accel), after a short
   coast, not a fixed rate: the slow disc (Accel 300, 54 px/s²) could not
   brake itself in 0.7 s, so it is not that simple either (GUESS: a kick is
   shed at a rate that grows with the fighter's Accel; two fighters cannot
   pin the law).

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e):** `BAY_LAUNCH_BRAKE` = 200 px/s² for any kick at or
under the fighter's top speed (`N/nova_plugin/escorts/bay_plugin.ts:
251-269`, applied at `:390-397`, shed at `:433-460`): **matches** the slow
disc from both bays (18 / 35 px), **mismatch** for the fast fighter (NovaJS
stops it 36 px out in 0.6 s; the original's coasted about 0.8 s to about
145 px). **Proposed:** keep 200 px/s² for a fighter at or below about
Accel 300, and for a faster-engined fighter let the kick coast about 0.8 s
before its own brake (GUESS; or scale the brake's onset with Accel).
Confidence: high for the two tracks (one clean launch each), low for the
rule.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| r8_u | "Pay us 4,000 credits.", accepted (1.99M), "w41-r8, you're cleared to land. Commence final approach." | "You're too far away to land on this planet." (still cleared) | **"Landing request denied." x4** | "What?", Hostile |
| r8_v | the same offer and payment, cleared | too far away (cleared) | **denied x4** | the same |

Finer (`r8_w`, the same payment, then `l` at the still-selected bribed port

| `l` after the payment | 17.7 s | 28.3 s | 39.1 s | 49.9 s | 61.0 s | 71.9 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Findings.**
1. **A paid planet bribe ends on its own**, with no landing and no jump:
   still cleared 12 s after the payment, refused 73 s after it (two runs).
   With wave 41 (gone after a landing about 45 s later), the landing need
   not be what ended it there either.
2. A bribe offer can be refused outright ("You wish.", r8_t): the price
   popup never comes.

3. **The bribe is the clearance itself**: it ended between 18 and 28 s
   after the payment, the span in which an ordinary landing clearance
   lapses (about 24.4 s, waves 35-36). Paying buys one "cleared to land"
   and nothing that outlives it; once it lapses the port answers a new
   request as before (denied, Hostile on the comm, a fresh bribe offered).

**NovaJS (main 89fbe05e): mismatch** (since 1c9d7f62). A paid planet bribe
has no clock (`STELLAR_BRIBE_NO_EXPIRY`, `N/nova_plugin/travel/planet_plugin.ts:560`, set at
`N/nova_plugin/encounters/hail_plugin.ts:447`) and ends only at the next landing
or a system change (the R8 row: "GUESS: time alone does not end it").
**Proposed:** make a paid planet bribe an
ordinary landing clearance (the same life as a granted request, about 24 s;
GUESS: the same clock, since it ended inside that clearance's lapse window)
instead of a standing permission; the landing / system-change resets stay
harmless. Confidence: high that time alone ends it (three runs), medium
that it is exactly the clearance lapse (one run with 11 s steps).

### The afterburner with a ruler (U4), wave 43: a FLAT x 1.8 on five hulls (Speed 100 to 1,000, Accel 150 to 600), timed against moon decorations instead of the star field; the hull's top speed is 0.4375 px/s per Speed unit; the boost comes up in about half a second and the coast back down runs at roughly 0.7 of the hull's own acceleration (2026-11-26)

**Question** (the brief's item 1, the wave-42 leftover): settle the
afterburner factor with a speed reading that does not use the star field
(wave 42: the stars move in two speed clusters, so every factor of waves
39-42 was biased).

**Rig** (`wave43Resources` "U4"). sÿst 1450 Kit Ruler Start (the pilot on a
decoration 2,000 px out, outside the no-jump zone) linked to 1451 Kit Ruler
40 map units EAST, which holds 15 moon decorations (spöb 1012-1026) at x =
-1200 .. 5800 every 500 px, y = 80. A jump arrives about 1,350 px west of
1451's centre heading due east (wave 38), so the ship flies along the
ruler. Kit Probes A-D (waves 1 and 42) and the new Kit Probe E (shïp 699:
Probe A at Speed 1000) with the stock Afterburner; pilots `w43_u4a` ..
`w43_u4e` (regular play). One keys step: `\` `j`, Up from 5.2 s after `j`
(the arrival), z + Up 6 s, z released with Up held 8 s, both released
(Probe E: 3 s / 2.5 s / 4 s, so it stays on the ruler). The moons' screen
positions give the ship's world x per recording frame (`tools/ruler.mjs`:
each moon is X = Mx + 318 - sx, Mx known), and each phase's speed is the
least-squares slope of X over the phase, using the mp4's own frame times
(`tools/u4phases.sh`, `u4.phases.txt`).

| hull (Speed / Accel) | cruise, px/s | z + Up, px/s | factor | back to cruise after z (Up held) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (300 / 300) `u4a_a` | 131.4 (rms 1.3 px) | 237.2 | **1.805** | 131.3, about 2.4 s after release (about 44 px/s²) |
| B (600 / 150) `u4b_a` | 262.5 | 473.3 | **1.803** | still 329 when the ruler ran out 7.5 s after (about 19 px/s²) |
| C (200 / 600) `u4c_a` | 87.4 | 158.3 | **1.811** | 87.6 within about 1 s (70 px/s² or more) |
| D (100 / 300) `u4d_a` | 43.5 | 79.1 | **1.818** | 43.8, about 1 s after (about 30-35 px/s²) |
| E (1000 / 300) `u4e_b` / `u4e_c` | 437.5 / 443.6 | 790.4 / 794.6 | **1.807 / 1.791** | 575 after 6 s (about 37 px/s²) |

(`u4e_a`, E's first run, left the ruler: the slow Turn-10 hull was still
about 30 degrees off when it jumped, so it arrived off the line. Every
other run flew within 7 px of y = 0 for the whole ruler.)

**Findings.**
1. **The afterburner multiplies the top speed by a flat 1.8**, with no
   dependence on Speed (100 to 1,000) or Accel (150 to 600): five hulls
   read 1.79-1.82. The older readings (1.5 / 1.75 / 1.53 / 1.73-1.77)
   were the star-field bias wave 42 found.
2. **Top speed is 0.4375 px/s per Speed unit** on this machine (131.4 /
   262.5 / 87.4 / 43.5 / 437.5-443.6 for Speed 300 / 600 / 200 / 100 /
   1000), i.e. 1.5 x Speed / 100 px a game frame at about 29.2 frames a
   second: what NovaJS's ShipSpeedConversionFactor assumes at 30 (the
   known 3% clock difference, `P/parsers/constants.ts:27-44`).
3. **The boost comes up in about 0.4-0.5 s** on Probe A (131 -> 237 px/s:
   about 250 px/s², five times the hull's own 54 px/s², wave 39) and about
   1.5 s on Probe E (437 -> 790); the afterburner's thrust is far stronger
   than the hull's, not 1.8 x it (GUESS: about 250 px/s² whatever the hull,
   from two hulls).
4. **The coast back down with Up held** runs at about 0.6-0.8 of the
   hull's own acceleration (A 44, D 30-35, E 37 against 54 px/s² for
   Accel 300; B about 19 against 27 for Accel 150; C, Accel 600, too quick
   to read); wave 39-42's "about half" came from the biased star reading.

**NovaJS (main f6d587e3):** `afterburnerFactor` = max(1.5, 1.25 + Speed /

### The deferred (përs) auto-abort (R16), wave 43: the person's mission is ACCEPTED in flight from the hail and stays ACTIVE (the special ship, "Kit Pers Hulk", replaces the person at once, "Waiting"); boarding the special ship ("Target ship has been boarded.", no dialog) ENDS it at once in flight ("You have no active missions."), the ship no longer "Waiting", and its DatePostInc 7 comes WITH the board: the map's date went from June 28th to July 5th across it (2026-11-26)

**Question** (catalogue R16, the brief's item 2): what happens to a
board/rescue auto-abort mission offered by a përs whose ship the special
ship replaces (përs Flags 0x0040), and does its DatePostInc apply?

**Rig.** The kit's përs 1151 (wave 42) never appeared, not even listed in
a system's Person slot at 100% (`r16_a`: Enter Ship, a landing and take-
off, Tab "No Target" both times), so the slot is the right tool but 1151 is
not a live person for the base pilot. `kits/w43_pers225.mjs` (installed only
by `scenarios/w43_pers225_board.json`) overrides the STOCK Refuel Trader përs
225 into the same person ("Kit Refuel 225": shïp 697 Kit Pers Hulk, an
immobile magenta disc, Flags 0x0040, LinkMission 1044: auto-abort Flags
0x0001, ShipGoal 5 rescue, ShipCount 1 of düde 535, ShipSyst -6, DatePostInc
7, OnAccept b9281, OnAbort b9282, OnSuccess b9283), and sÿst 1455 Kit Pers
Slot lists përs 1151 and 225 in its Person slots at 100%. Pilot `w43_r16`
(the Kit Lancer at Kit Pers Slot Port, bit 9280, June 23 1177). Tab, hail
(`y`), Return, the mission list (`i`), then `loops/board.mjs` (magenta
colour), then the mission list again (`tools/r16b.mjs`).

| run | what happened |
|---|---|
| r16_a (përs 1151 only) | no person at Enter Ship, nor after a landing (Tab: No Target) |
| r16_b / r16_c / r16_d (225 override) | the person was there at once every time ("Kit Refuel 225", No Shields, a magenta disc 300 px out); the hail opened the mission's offer (No / Yes); Yes; the mission list showed **"Kit R16 deferred auto-abort" ACTIVE**, dated June 23rd; Tab now named the target **"Kit Pers Hulk", status "Waiting"** (the special ship had replaced the person). board.mjs then lost the hulk (r16_b in bracket mode, r16_c swept 118 px out, r16_d's radar fallback chased a blip 2,978 px away), and no board happened |
| r16_e - r16_h | r16_e: the person met on screen on the second roll; board.mjs walked in but swept at 28-30 px ("You're not close enough to board this ship.", 40 presses), no board; the mission list 5 minutes later still listed the mission, dated June 24th (one landing roll). **r16_f / r16_h**: six and twelve rolls never put the person on screen (the loop needs it there), nothing boarded. **r16_g** (sweep at 10 px): on screen at the tenth roll; the walk stopped 17 px out, the sweep turned in place, and one press answered **"Target ship has been boarded."** with NO dialog; the target line went from "Waiting" to "No Shields" and every later press said "You can't board this ship."; the mission list straight after the board: **"You have no active missions."** (status line, no dialog). **r16_i** (the same, with the map's date, bottom right of `m`): on screen at the sixth roll; the map read **June 28th, 1177** after the accept; boarded about 11 px out; right after, the map read **July 5th, 1177** (and still July 5th 10 s later), and "You have no active missions." |

**Findings.**
1. **A përs-offered rescue auto-abort is NOT aborted at the accept or when
   its special ship is created**: the mission is listed as active right
   after the accept in flight, with the special ship (the düde's hull, with
   the mission's name for its target line) in the person's place, its
   status "Waiting" (a rescue target, not "Disabled"). This is the
   Bible's deferral ("will auto-abort after the special ship is boarded"),
   unlike wave 10's mission without a përs, which aborted at the ship's
   creation.
2. **The board ends the mission at once, in flight**: one press boarded
   the "Waiting" ship with no plunder dialog ("Target ship has been
   boarded."), the ship was then an ordinary ship ("No Shields", not
   boardable again) and the mission list was empty seconds later, with no
   landing or jump in between.
3. **DatePostInc is applied at the board**: seven days (the mission's
   DatePostInc) between the map read after the accept (June 28th) and the
   one right after the board (July 5th), in flight, with no landing or
   jump (r16_i). With wave 41 (the immediate case: the week comes at the
   in-flight abort), DatePostInc always comes with the abort itself.

**NovaJS (main f6d587e3):** `deferredAutoAbort`
(`N/nova_plugin/missions/mission_auto_abort.ts:47-53`) keeps a përs-
replacing board / rescue auto-abort active (**matches** finding 1); the
board sets `autoAbortPending` and `runPendingAutoAborts`
(`N/nova_plugin/missions/mission_landing.ts:117-145`) runs OnAbort at the
next date advance through `autoAbortMission`
(`N/nova_plugin/missions/mission_transitions.ts:58-61`), which never adds
DatePostInc. **mismatch on the moment**: NovaJS keeps the mission in the list until the next date advance (a landing or a jump),
the original drops it at the board. **Proposed:** run the player-local half of
the deferred abort (OnAbort, the removal) at the board itself, as the
immediate in-flight abort does, and (GUESS, from wave 41's immediate case)
add DatePostInc there (measured: +7 at the board). Confidence: high that the mission stays active until the board and ends at it (four accepts, one board); high for the +7 at the board (one clean read: June 28th -> July 5th).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w43/r16_a/` ..
`r16_i/` (the `tab*`, `hail`, `info*`, `map*` shots, `recording.mp4`).

**mismatch** (about 140). **Proposed:** scale the strength so Gravity 5
gives 140 px/s² (x 0.72: GRAVITY_LINEAR 16.5, GRAVITY_QUADRATIC 2.3, GUESS:
the Gravity-10 point, 550, was read the same biased way, so scale both
until a Gravity-10 moon run); keep the falloff beyond 300 px. Confidence:
