### Outfitter long item names (the hub's question), wave 43: the grid shows the item's ShortName, split ONLY at the two characters "\n" and never wrapped: a long line stays one line in the same small font, centred on the cell and spilling over the neighbours (clipped by the grid's frame); an EMPTY ShortName shows no caption at all; the block is bottom-aligned (a second line grows upward); stock "Pirate Thunderhead Bay" is "Pirate Th-head\nBay" (2026-11-26)

**Question** (Matthew, via the hub): how does the original's outfitter (and
shipyard) grid render an item name too long for two lines? NovaJS wraps
"Pirate Thunderhead Bay" to 3 lines and the last runs into the cell border.

**Rig** (`wave43Resources` "LN", added during the wave). sÿst 1456 Kit Long
Names, port spöb 1034 (outfitter + shipyard, SpecialTech 9408 and, from
`ln_b`, 12: the stock pirate outfits with their icons); oütf 492-495 (the Kit
Escort Gun as "Pirate Thunderhead Bay", "Antidisestablishmentarianismus" (30
letters), "Heavy Kit Turret", "Kit Very Long Name For A Test"), 496 "Kit
Short Name Set Long Turret"; shïp 728 / 729 "Pirate Thunderhead Long Hull"
(2). Pilot `w43_ln` (the Kit Lancer on the port): land, `o`, a full-screen
lossless shot and a window shot, Done, `s`, the same. In `ln_a` every kit
item's ShortName was its name; in `ln_b` 492-495 and 729 had an EMPTY
ShortName (as the stock outfits seemed to, read with the repo parser, which
does not read oütf ShortName), 496 and 728 kept theirs. The stock items'
ShortNames were then read raw from the stock files (oütf offset 811).

| item | ShortName | the cell |
|---|---|---|
| ln_a: the four kit outfits (22-30 characters) | = the name | ONE line each, the normal small white font, centred on the cell and running straight across the neighbouring cells (the four captions overprint one another in a row) |
| ln_a / ln_b: shïp 728 "Pirate Thunderhead Long Hull" | = the name | one line under its icon, centred, its start CLIPPED by the grid's left frame ("ate Thunderhead Long Hull") |
| ln_b: oütf 496 | "Kit Short Name Set Long Turret" | the same: one line, clipped at the frame |
| ln_b: oütf 492-495, shïp 729 | EMPTY | **no caption at all** (the icon cell only) |
| ln_b: stock Pirate Viper Bay (oütf 218) | "Pirate\nViper Bay" | "Pirate" over "Viper Bay" |
| ln_b: stock Pirate Thunderhead (285) | "Pirate\nThunderhead" | two lines |
| ln_b: stock Sensor Boost / Pirate Jammer / Pirate Viper | one line each | one line |
| Earth (`ui_screenshots/original_macos_screenshots/outfitter/earth_outfitter.png`) | "Light Blaster\nTurret" (oütf 130) and the like | two lines, the second on the same baseline as a one-line caption |

Stock ShortNames read raw: 284 Pirate Thunderhead Bay = "Pirate
Th-head\nBay", 138 Gravimetric Missile Launcher = "Grav Missile\nLauncher",
323 Illegal Quad Light Blaster Turret = "Qd Lt Turret\n- illegal -", 165
Thunderhead Bay = "Thunderhead Bay" (one line); the stock data abbreviates
by hand so that no line is wider than a cell.

**Findings.**
1. **No automatic wrapping, truncation or font shrink**: a caption line is
   drawn whole, centred on its cell, in the grid's one small font, over the
   neighbours and clipped only by the grid frame. Line breaks come only from
   the literal two characters "\n" in ShortName (the Bible's text, for oütf
   and shïp alike).
2. **The caption is the ShortName, not the resource name**: an empty one
   draws nothing (kit items; stock items always have one).
3. **Bottom-aligned**: a one-line caption sits on the cell's bottom line;
   a two-line caption keeps its second line there and its first one line
   higher (over the icon's lower edge), as in Earth's shot. Three lines were
   not tried (no "\n\n" item; the stock data has none).

**NovaJS (main f6d587e3):** the raw parser reads oütf ShortName as
`outfitterName` (`P/resource_parsers/outf_resource.ts:191`) but
`OutfitParse` never carries it into OutfitData (`P/parsers/outfit_parse.ts:411`
passes lcName only), so `captionSegments`
(`N/spaceport/item_grid.ts:91-98`) falls back to the resource name for every
outfit (and for a ship with a blank ShortName), and the caption text wraps
by width (`wordWrap: true`, `CAPTION_WRAP_WIDTH` 77, `:64` and `:146-153`):
"Pirate Thunderhead Bay" becomes three lines. **Mismatch** (outfits; ships
already use their ShortName). **Proposed:** carry `outfitterName` into
OutfitData as its `shortName` and caption outfits with it; turn `wordWrap` off for captions (each "\n"
segment one line, centred, allowed to overflow the cell; clip to the grid);
and for an EMPTY ShortName show nothing (the original) or, as a NovaJS
choice for plug-ins written against the resource name, the name on one
line. The stock "Pirate Thunderhead Bay" then reads "Pirate Th-head" /
"Bay", two lines, bottom-aligned. Confidence: high (two runs, nine stock and
seven kit items, raw ShortNames checked).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261126-w43/ln_a/`, `ln_b/`
(`*-full.png` are the lossless 1920x1080 shots, `*outfitter.png` /
`*shipyard.png` the window crops), `ln_b_outfitter_zoom.png`.

### Not reached in wave 43: E6's acceleration under each ion plateau and a direct drain reading (2026-11-26)

- **E6**: not run (an ionized hull's acceleration needs the ruler rig with
  an ion source on the arrival line, or the moon reading from rest; the
  ruler now makes that possible).

### The afterburner's thrust and the coast-down (U4 leftovers), wave 44: the boost accelerates at about 5.4 x the hull's own acceleration (about Accel px/s², whatever the top speed: Accel 150 hulls 125-148 at Speed 600 and 1,000, Accel 300 265-300 at Speed 300 and 1,000, Accel 600 about 600); the coast back down runs at about 0.8 x the hull's acceleration, a constant deceleration; the hull's own acceleration is 0.17 px/s² per Accel unit (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (the Wave 43 leftovers row): the boost thrust law (a third
hull's ramp: Probe A about 250 px/s², Probe E about 230), and the coast-down
rate on a fourth Accel (Probe B ran off the ruler in wave 43).

**Rig** (`wave44Resources` "U4"). Two readings without the star field.
(1) **The pad**: sÿst 1457 Kit Accel Pad, a decoration start (spöb 1035) at
the centre and 14 moon decorations (spöb 1036-1049) on a 200 x 300 px grid
around it, so the ship's world position is known in ANY direction (its
heading at Enter Ship is not chosen): each moon on screen gives it as G -
(screen offset), the frame's place the median (`tools/grid2d.py`). Kit
Probes A / B / C / E and the new F (shïp 738: Speed 1000, Accel 150) and G
(739: Speed 600, Accel 600), each with the stock Afterburner, at rest on the
start (pilots `w44_pada` .. `w44_padg`, regular play): Up 1.5 s from rest
(the hull's own acceleration), then z + Up 1.5 s (the boost's), both
released. The track is projected on its own direction; the hull phase is a
least-squares constant acceleration, the boost a piecewise fit (the hull
phase continued to an onset lag, then a constant acceleration until 1.8 x
the top speed; `tools/padramp.py`). (2) **Wave 43's ruler** (sÿst 1450 ->
1451, moons every 500 px on the arrival line): Probe B with a short boost
(Up 1 s, z 2.5 s, Up held 10 s: the whole coast stays on the ruler), G (Up
2 s, z 2.5 s, Up held 5 s) and F (Up 1 s, z 3 s, Up held 4 s); the ramp and
the coast fitted as a piecewise constant-acceleration change between the
known cruise and boosted speeds (`tools/rampfit.py`). Wave 43's A-E ruler
tracks were refitted the same way.

| hull (Speed / Accel) | hull from rest, px/s² | boost, px/s² (fit band) | boost / hull | coast-down with Up held, px/s² | coast / hull |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (300 / 300) `pada_a`, w43 `u4a_a` | 49.8 | 290 (235-610) | about 5.8 | 42 (40-46), w43 | 0.84 |
| B (600 / 150) `padb_a`, `u4b_a` | 28.1 | 145 (140-155) pad; 148 (126-182) ruler; 140 (120-174) w43 | 5.2 | **20** (the whole 473 -> 262 px/s coast on the ruler, linear: 472, 449, 429, 410, 391, 369, 349, 331, 309, 290, 271, 260 px/s a second apart) | 0.71 |
| C (200 / 600) `padc_a` | about 100 (top speed in 0.8 s) | too quick to read (71 px/s in a few frames) | - | too quick (w43) | - |
| D (100 / 300) w43 `u4d_a` | - | - | - | 38 (28-84) | about 0.76 |
| E (1000 / 300) `pade_a`, w43 `u4e_b` / `u4e_c` | 49.5 | 265 (255-285) pad; 302 / 282 ruler | 5.4-6.1 | 42 / 42 (36-50) | 0.85 |
| F (1000 / 150) `padf_a`, `u4f_a` | 25.4 | 125 (125-140) pad; 140 (130-154) ruler | 4.9-5.5 | 22 (18-26) | 0.87 |
| G (600 / 600) `padg_a`, `u4g_a` | 103 | 595 (460-935) pad; 638 (308-1408) ruler | about 5.8 | **84** (76-94) | 0.82 |

**Findings.**
1. **The boost's thrust follows Accel, not Speed**: the two Accel-150 hulls
   at Speed 600 (B) and 1,000 (F) both boost at 125-148 px/s², the two
   Accel-300 hulls at Speed 300 (A) and 1,000 (E) at 265-300, the Accel-600
   G at about 600: about 5.4 x the hull's own acceleration (4.9-5.8 over
   five hulls), i.e. roughly Accel px/s² on this machine. Wave 43's "about
   250 whatever the hull" was two Accel-300 hulls.
2. **The coast back down is a constant deceleration of about 0.8 x the
   hull's own acceleration** (0.71-0.87 over six hulls; B's 10.5 s coast is
   a straight line), with Up held; with both keys released (`pada_a`) it
   ran at 39 px/s², the same as with Up held (42).
3. **The hull's own acceleration from rest is 0.17 px/s² per Accel unit**
   (49.5-49.8 for Accel 300, 25.4-28.1 for 150, 103 for 600): Accel / 5000
   px per frame² at the machine's 29.2 frames a second, as NovaJS's
   ShipAccelerationConversionFactor assumes at 30 (the known 3% clock).

**NovaJS (main 53f9c897, after the wave-43 fix):** the top speed boosts by
`AFTERBURNER_FACTOR` 1.8 (`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:28`:
**matches**); the boosted acceleration is a FLAT `AFTERBURNER_THRUST` 250
px/s² (max(hull, 250), `:43`, `:161-163`) and the overspeed sheds at
`OVERSPEED_DECAY_FACTOR` 0.7 x the hull's acceleration (`:75`, `:158`).
**Mismatch**: the thrust follows the hull's Accel (125-148 px/s² for Accel
150, about 600 for Accel 600), so the flat 250 is right only near Accel 300;
the coast is 0.8, not 0.7. **Proposed:** boosted acceleration =
`base.acceleration * AFTERBURNER_THRUST_FACTOR` with the factor 5.4 (GUESS
between 5 and 6; five fits scatter 4.9-5.8), replacing the flat 250;
`OVERSPEED_DECAY_FACTOR` 0.8. Confidence: high that the thrust scales with
Accel and not Speed (two Accel pairs at different Speeds, pad and ruler
agree), medium for the multiple (5.4 +- 0.4); high for 0.8 +- 0.1 and the
linear shape of the coast (six hulls, B's whole coast on the ruler).

### Gravity's law with moons (U7 leftovers), wave 44: pull = Gravity x min(30 px/s², 8.6e6 / d²): an INVERSE-SQUARE pull beyond about 535 px and a constant one inside, both in proportion to Gravity (Gravity 5: 150 px/s² and 4.3e7 / d²; Gravity 10: 300 and 8.5e7 / d²) (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (the Wave 43 leftovers row): the far falloff read off moons
(wave 42's 45 / 15 px/s² at 1,000 / 2,000 px were star readings), and a
second strength (Gravity 10) on the moon reading.

**Rig** (`wave44Resources` "U7"). sÿst 1458 Kit Gravity 5 Moons (the well,
spöb 1050, Gravity 5, the dark 40 px art, at the centre; moon starts at 600 /
1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 px on the x axis, each with reference moons at (x,

start (pilots `w44_g5_600` .. `w44_g10_2000`), no input, 20 s, recorded from
before Enter Ship (`w44_space_early.json`). Tracks by `tools/grid2d.py` on
the moons (`tools/u7sum.sh`); the pull per 1 s window (`tools/u7pull.py`),
and ONE law fitted to all four falls of a well from rest to 60 px out, the
ship's speed capped at its top speed (`tools/u7model.py`: x'' = -min(C, K /
x²), each fall's onset fitted).

| run | start | pull, 1 s windows (|x| px: px/s²) |
|---|---|---|
| g5_2000_a | 2,000 | 2,000: 11.0; 1,975: 11.2; 1,944: 12.0; 1,876: 12.3; 1,780: 10-15 |
| g5_1500_a | 1,500 | 1,502: 21.3; 1,480: 19.8; 1,439: 21.7; 1,377: 19.9 |
| g5_1000_a | 1,000 | 998: 45.2; 949: 45.2; 907: 54.1; 851: 62.3; 781: 72.7; 720 (the return's turn): 81.5-84.5; 600: 126-132 |
| g5_600_a | 600 | 582: 130.6; 527: 132.7; the return's turn at 614: 111-123 |
| g10_2000_a | 2,000 | 1,997: 22.9; 1,968: 22.7; 1,917: 21.8; 1,842: 26.2 |
| g10_1000_a | 1,000 | 987: 82.3; 949: 97.5; 887: 112.9; 796: 136.7 |
| g10_300_a / g10_150_a | 300 / 150 | 260-320 everywhere inside 300 px |

| well | best fit over its four falls | fit band (1.2 x rms) | rms |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gravity 5 | K = 4.3e7 px³/s², C = 150 px/s² | K 4.3e7, C 135-155 | 3.2 px (2.7-3.8 per fall, 83-460 frames each) |
| Gravity 10 | K = 8.5e7, C = 300 | K 8.5-8.8e7, C 265-305 | 2.4 px |

**Findings.**
1. **Beyond about 535 px the pull falls as 1 / d²**: K / d² with K = 4.3e7
   px³/s² at Gravity 5 fits every window from 2,000 px in to about 600
   (2,000: 11; 1,500: 19; 1,000: 43; 781: 71), and one such law fits each
   whole fall to about 3 px.
2. **Inside it the pull is constant**, 150 px/s² at Gravity 5 (wave 43's
   140 from 300 / 150 / 85 px, read off fewer moons, agrees), where K / d²
   would reach 150 at 535 px; the two pieces meet there.
3. **Both pieces are in proportion to Gravity**: Gravity 10 doubles both
   (K 8.5e7, C 300), so the meeting distance (sqrt(K / C), about 535 px) is
   the same. Per Gravity unit: C = 30 px/s², K = 8.6e6 px³/s².
4. Wave 42's star readings at 1,000 and 2,000 px (45 / 15) were close; wave
   41's Gravity-10 "about 550 px/s²" and wave 40-41's quadratic growth with
   the field were not (the star-field bias, wave 42).

**NovaJS (main 53f9c897, after the wave-43 fix):** `gravityAcceleration`
= 16.5 G + 2.3 G |G| (140 px/s² at Gravity 5, 395 at 10;
`N/nova_plugin/travel/gravity_plugin.ts:68-69`, `:89-92`) inside 300 px and
that times (300 / d)^1.5 beyond (`gravityFalloff`, `:112-118`): Gravity 5
inside about 300 px **matches** (140 against 150); **mismatch** at Gravity
10 (395 against 300: the strength is linear in G, not quadratic), in the
inner radius (300 vs 535 px) and in the exponent (1.5 vs 2: at 600 px
NovaJS gives 49 where the original pulls 120-130, at 1,000 px 23 vs 43, at
2,000 px 8.1 vs 10.8). **Proposed:** pull = |G| x min(GRAVITY_NEAR_PER_UNIT
30, GRAVITY_FAR_PER_UNIT 8.6e6 / d²) px/s² toward the well (away for a
negative G, wave 40), i.e. `gravityAcceleration(G)` = 30 |G| and
`gravityFalloff(d)` = min(1, (535 / d)²) with GRAVITY_REFERENCE_DISTANCE 535
(d² is exact arithmetic, no pow); the top-speed cap stays (the fall levels
off at the hull's top speed, wave 42: Probe E's swings came back only to
about 720 of the 1,000 px start because the fall reached 437 px/s). GUESS:
the linear-in-G strength holds for strong wells (Gravity 100+ would then
reach the top speed in a few frames, as wave 40 saw). Confidence: high for
the inverse square and the constant core (eight falls, one law to 2-4 px
rms each), high for the proportion to G (two strengths), medium for the
constants' last digit.

### Acceleration under ionization (E6 leftover), wave 44: a hull charged past the no-turn line thrusts at about 0.4 of its acceleration (20-22 against 50-52 px/s² for the same 0.57 s Up pulse from rest); the ion bolts also PUSH the ship (a steady drift building to 35-50 px/s), so the lower plateaus were not read (2026-11-26)

**Question** (the Wave 43 leftovers row): the acceleration under each ion
plateau (wave 42: two thirds of the turn untinted, a third tinted, none
past about 38 of IonizeMax 100).

**Rig** (`wave44Resources` "E6"). sÿst 1463 Kit Ion Pad: port spöb 1083 at
the centre and 8 moon decorations around it (the ship's position in any
direction, `tools/grid2d.py` grid "ion"); mïsn 1051 (bit 9286; wave 12's,

(Ionization 5). shïp 791 Kit Probe Ion: Kit Probe A (Speed 300, Accel 300,
inertial) with IonizeMax 100, Deionize 1. Pilots `w44_e6i20`, `w44_e6i5`
(the mission's bit) and `w44_e6c` (none): land, accept, Leave, then 0.57 s
Up pulses (the hull cannot turn, so every pulse pushes the same way); the
velocity before and after each pulse from linear fits of the track
(`tools/pulses.py`).

| run | pulses (s after the take-off) | acceleration over the pulse |
|---|---|---|
| e6c_a (no ion source) | +9.7, +13.8 | **52.0, 49.8 px/s²** (the hull's own, as on the accel pad) |
| e6i20_a (ion 20, hit since the take-off) | +9.9 (about three hits), +14.0 | **19.6, 22.3 px/s²** (0.39-0.45 of the control) |
| e6i5_a (ion 5) | +16.5, +22.6, +29.8 | not read: the ship had drifted off the pad's moons before the first pulse |

**Findings.**
1. **Past the no-turn line the thrust is about 0.4 of the hull's** (two
   pulses, 20-22 against 50-52 px/s²), close to wave 39's "about a third"
   (a star reading).
2. **The ion bolts push the ship**: in both ion runs the still hull began
   to drift at the take-off and the drift grew (about 12 px/s after 1 s,
   35 px/s by +9 s, 48 px/s by +16 s) in the bolts' direction, the same
   with Ionization 5 and 20; the control did not move. (The Kit Ion Tick
   weapons are clones of stock wëap 131, whose impact this presumably is:
   GUESS.) That drift is why the low-charge readings failed: a pad rig
   needs a stronger hull push budget or a non-pushing ion weapon (Impact
   0) to read the untinted and tinted plateaus.

ion.acceleration * boost` (`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:163`).

plateau table the turn uses, 2/3 / 1/3 / 0 for the turn, does not carry
over to thrust, which keeps 0.4 where the turn is 0). Confidence: medium
for 0.4 at saturation (two pulses, one run), none for the lower plateaus.

### Grid captions: a second "\n", the shipyard and the hire list (the hub's questions), wave 44: only the FIRST "\n" breaks the caption; a later "\n" is dropped and its two sides run together ("Kit Three\nLine\nCaption" shows "Kit Three" / "LineCaption"; "Kit Gap\n\nLine" shows "Kit Gap" / "Line"), so a caption has at most two lines; the shipyard and the bar's hire-escort list caption ships the same way, and a BLANK ShortName shows no caption in both (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (the Wave 43 leftovers row and the brief's item 2; the hub,
after the grid-caption fix landed): a three-line ShortName; does the
shipyard treat a shïp ShortName the same way (split at "\n", no wrap); and
does a shïp with a BLANK ShortName show no caption, or its name, in the
shipyard and in the bar's hire-escort list?

**Rig** (`wave44Resources` "LN"). sÿst 1462 Kit Long Names 2, port spöb 1082
(outfitter, shipyard and bar; SpecialTech 9409): oütf 497 ShortName "Kit
Three\nLine\nCaption", 498 "Kit Gap\n\nLine" (each "\n" the two
characters, as the Bible writes it and the stock data stores it); shïp 761
"Kit Two\nLine Hull", 766 "Kit Three\nLine\nHull Name", 767 "Kit Very Long
Single Line Hull Short Name", 888 "" (blank), all four HireRandom 100. Pilot
`w44_ln` (the Kit Lancer on the port): land, `o`, shots, Done, `s`, shots,
Done, Bar, Hire Escort, shots (full-screen lossless and window crops).

| item | ShortName | the cell (outfitter / shipyard / hire list) |
|---|---|---|
| oütf 497 | "Kit Three\nLine\nCaption" | **"Kit Three" over "LineCaption"**: two lines, the second "\n" gone and "Line" and "Caption" joined with no space |
| oütf 498 | "Kit Gap\n\nLine" | **"Kit Gap" over "Line"**: two lines, no empty middle line |
| shïp 761 | "Kit Two\nLine Hull" | "Kit Two" over "Line Hull", shipyard and hire list alike |
| shïp 766 | "Kit Three\nLine\nHull Name" | "Kit Three" over "LineHull Name" (both lists) |
| shïp 767 | 41 characters, no "\n" | one line, centred on its cell, spilling over both neighbours (both lists) |
| shïp 888 | "" (blank) | **no caption** in the shipyard and in the hire list: the icon alone (the text in its cell is 767's overflow) |

(Wave 43's `ln_b` shipyard showed the same for shïp 729, blank: no caption,
where 728 with its ShortName had one; `ln_b_shipyard.png`.)

**Findings.**
1. **At most two lines**: the first "\n" in a ShortName breaks the
   caption; every later "\n" is removed and the text on its two sides is
   drawn together (no space, no third line, no empty line). The stock data
   never has a second "\n" (wave 43), so this only shows in plug-ins.
2. **Ships caption exactly like outfits** in the shipyard (split at the
   first "\n", never wrapped, long lines spill over the neighbours).
3. **A blank ShortName shows no caption** for a ship in the shipyard (729
   in wave 43, 888 here) and in the bar's hire-escort list (888); the
   ship's name is NOT used as a fallback. The hire list uses the same grid
   and captions as the shipyard.

**NovaJS (main 53f9c897):** `captionSegments`
(`N/spaceport/item_grid.ts:129-136`) now captions outfits and ships from
ShortName with no wrap, and an empty ShortName gives no caption (finding 3:
**matches**, shipyard and hire grid both, per the hub). It splits at EVERY
"\n" and drops empty lines (`:132-134`): "Kit Three\nLine\nCaption" becomes
three lines. **Mismatch** (finding 1). **Proposed:** split at the first
"\n" only and delete the later ones with no space: `const [first, ...rest]
= source.split(/\\n|\n/); lines = [first, rest.join('')]` (then trim and
drop an empty one as now). Confidence: high (two outfits and two ships, the
same in three grids).
**Applied 2026-11-27 (cef99737)**: `captionSegments` splits at the first
"\n" only and joins the rest with no space, then trims and drops an empty
line as before; the blank-ShortName rule (no caption, no name fallback)
already matched in the shipyard and the hire grid (the same `ItemGrid`).

### Jump chaining on a route, wave 44: with `j` held the ship jumps again AT ONCE on each arrival (arrivals 4.90 s apart, the same 4.8-4.9 s as a press from rest), through the whole route; a tap jumps once and keeps the rest of the route; a second tap during the departure sequence or the transit, up to 0.2 s before the arrival flash, is IGNORED (not remembered), while one 0.2 s after the arrival starts the next hop (2026-11-26)

**Questions** (Matthew, via the hub): with a 3-jump route plotted, (a)
does one press of `j` jump once or chain through the route; (b) with `j`
held, does the ship jump out again as soon as it arrives, as soon as it
clears the no-jump zone, or never until re-pressed (and the arrival-to-
next-jump timing); (c) is a `j` pressed during the hyperspace transit /
flash ignored or remembered on arrival? (Wave 11 answered (a) and the
chaining half of (b) at a 2 s shot rate: "Multi-jump routes and the `j`
key, wave 11".)

**Rig** (`wave44Resources` "JC", added during the wave). sÿst 1469-1472
Kit Chain Alpha / Bravo / Charlie / Delta, linked in a line, empty but for
Alpha's start decoration (spöb 1096) 2,000 px out (outside the no-jump
zone); pilot `w44_jc` (the Kit Lancer, all four explored, fuel 3,000). The
route: the map, Find "Kit Chain Delta" (centres on it), shift-clicks on
Bravo, Charlie and Delta (wave 11's way: a Find alone, `jc_a`, or a plain
click on Delta, `jc_a2`, plotted NO route and `j` did nothing), Done; the
nav panel then reads "Hyperspace / Kit Chain Bravo". Then one keys step:
`jc_b3` `down:j` held about 48 s; `jc_c1_a` `j`, a second `j` 3.15 s later;
`jc_c4_a` / `jc_c3_a` / `jc_c2_a` the same at 4.20 / 4.61 / 5.04 s; window shots every ~4 s, the map at
the end. Times off the recording: the nav panel's text changing at each
arrival (`tools/regionchg.mjs`, window x 646-822, y 252-292) and the
one-frame white arrival flash (`tools/flash.mjs`).

| run | `j` | arrivals (s after the first press) | where it ended |
|---|---|---|---|
| jc_b3 | held from 49.46 s | **4.81 (Bravo), 9.71 (Charlie), 14.61 (Delta)**: arrival to arrival 4.90 s twice; status "Arriving in the Kit Chain Bravo system on June 24th, 1177 NC." ... "Delta ... June 26th"; the nav panel "Hyperspace / Kit Chain Charlie" from the first arrival | Delta, "Nav System Off" (route used up) |
| jc_c1_a | tap, tap again at +3.15 s (in the departure sequence) | **4.82 (Bravo) only**; nothing in the next 45 s | Bravo, the rest of the route kept (nav: Kit Chain Charlie) |
| jc_c4_a | tap, tap again at +4.20 s (0.61 s before the arrival) | **4.81 (Bravo) only**; the white arrival flash at +4.78 | Bravo |
| jc_c3_a | tap, tap again at +4.61 s (0.21 s before the arrival, in the transit) | **4.82 (Bravo) only** | Bravo |
| jc_c2_a | tap, tap again at +5.04 s (0.21 s AFTER the arrival at +4.83) | 4.83 (Bravo); **the second hop began at once** (the nav panel dimmed 0.52 s after the second press) and arrived 5.69 s after it (Charlie) | Charlie |

**Findings.**
1. **(a) One press, one jump**: the rest of the route is kept for the next
   press (jc_c1_a, as wave 11's tap).
2. **(b) A held `j` jumps again the moment the ship arrives**: arrival to
   arrival took 4.90 s, the same as a press from rest to the first arrival
   (4.81-4.83 s), so the next departure sequence starts with no gap; the
   ship arrives outside the 1,000 px no-jump zone (about 1,350 px out, wave
   38), so "on arrival" and "on clearing the zone" are the same moment
   here. Whether a held key would wait out an arrival INSIDE the zone was
   not tested (no rig puts an arrival inside it).
3. **(c) A press before the arrival is ignored, not remembered**: second
   taps 3.15, 4.20 and 4.61 s after the first (the last 0.21 s before the
   arrival, in the transit) gave no second jump;
   one 0.21 s AFTER the arrival started the next hop at once (jc_c2_a). The
   key is read only while the ship can jump.

**NovaJS (main 53f9c897): matches.** `PlayerJumpControl`
(`N/nova_plugin/travel/jump_plugin.ts:598-650`) polls the held `hyperjump`
control every tick and refuses while a jump is under way (the `jumping`
blocker, `:631`), so a held key starts the next hop on the tick after the
arrival (the player arrives one second of flight outside the no-jump
radius, `PLAYER_JUMP_ARRIVAL_MARGIN_S`, `:165`), a tap starts one hop and
keeps the route, and a tap during the sequence is dropped (no latch). The
new `ARRIVAL_JUMP_GRACE_MS` (3 s, `:198`) only lets a press in the first 3 s
after an arrival start the next hop from INSIDE the zone (a NovaJS
allowance for the client's late first frame); it does not delay a held
key's chain, so the 4.90 s rhythm is kept; the original's behaviour inside
the zone is untested (it never arrives there). No change. Confidence: high
for (a) and (b) (wave 11 and jc_b3, three arrivals 4.90 s apart), high for
(c) (three ignored presses at 3.15-4.61 s, one taken 0.21 s after the
arrival).

| on screen | the Viper kept firing on the player; three fighters on screen just before the kill, one or two after |

white frame (within about 100 ms): does the hop chain? (2) is there any

frame after the arrival does the next sequence start? (4) the same at 2x
(the original has no fast-forward: not applicable). And the wave-44
leftover: a held `j` with an arrival INSIDE the no-jump zone.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| jzw4690_a | tap, tap | 46.10 | +0.07 | chained: Charlie 5.63 s after the press |
| jzw4770_a | tap, tap | 45.50 | +0.16 | chained: Charlie 5.64 s after the press |
| wave 44 jc_c3_a / jc_c2_a | tap, tap | | -0.21 / +0.21 | ignored / chained (Charlie 5.69 s after the press) |
| jzf13_a | tap, tap | 45.40 (nav) | **+1.33** (the ship about 885 px out, 115 inside) | **refused**: "Can't initiate hyperspace jump - not yet far enough away from system center." at once; no jump |
| jzf25_a | tap, tap | 45.63 (nav) | **+2.46** (about 500 px inside) | **refused**, the same line; no jump |
| jzp_a (zone 2,000) | `j` held 30 s | 44.87 | (held) | NO jump for 9.5 s and no status line ("Entering the Kit Zone Bravo system" until 49.47, then nothing); the ship coasted east through the centre at 350 px/s, began the departure about 9.5 s after the arrival as it passed about x +2,000, and reached Charlie 15.4 s after arriving in Bravo |

**Findings.**
1. **(1) A tap in the arrival's white frame chains like a held key**: the
   press stamped 0.01 s before the flash reached Charlie 4.91 s later, the
   held key's arrival-to-arrival 4.90 s (wave 44 jc_b3). The game reads keys
   4-5 frames after they are posted, so this press reached the game just
   after the arrival. Taps 0.07-0.21 s after the arrival also chain, but
   take 5.6-5.7 s to the next arrival (0.7 s longer); a tap 0.21 s before
   the arrival is ignored (wave 44).
2. **(2) No fresh press inside the zone is accepted after an arrival**: at
   +1.33 s (about 115 px inside) and +2.46 s (about 500 px inside) the
   press is refused with STR# 2002's "not yet far enough away" line, the
   same as any press inside the zone. There is no arrival grace.
3. **(3) A held `j` starts the next sequence at the arrival** (4.90 s
   arrival to arrival against 4.81-4.83 s from a press at rest: within
   about 3 frames).
4. **The hyperspace dist mod does NOT move the arrival**: with a 2,000 px
   zone the ship still arrived where the standard hull does, inside the
   enlarged zone (anchored on wave 38's 1,350 px: the departure then began
   exactly as the ship passed +2,000 on the far side; a 2,350 px arrival,
   outside the zone, would have chained at once as in wave 44); **a held
   `j` waits silently** while the ship is inside the zone and jumps the
   moment it is outside, here after crossing the whole system.

**NovaJS (main b2c1834e):** (1) and (3) **match** (wave 44's analysis:
`PlayerJumpControl` polls the held control every tick, `jump_plugin.ts`).
(2) **Mismatch**: `ARRIVAL_JUMP_GRACE_MS` = 3,000
(`N/nova_plugin/travel/jump_plugin.ts:198`, `inArrivalJumpGrace` `:213-219`)
lets any press in the first 3 s after an arrival start the next hop from
inside the zone; the original refuses at +1.33 and +2.46 s. (The constant's
comment calls it an allowance for the client's late first frame, "nothing
here is measured": a maintainer call; a grace no longer than the client's
measured lag would keep the multiplayer reason without accepting presses
the original refuses.) (4) **Mismatch**: the arrival distance is
`jumpRadiusFor(JUMP_DISTANCE, jumpDistanceMod) + maxVelocity x
PLAYER_JUMP_ARRIVAL_MARGIN_S` (`:1041-1044`), so a +1000 hull arrives 2,350
px out, outside its zone, and chains at once where the original's arrives
inside and coasts through. **Proposed:** the arrival distance from the
UNMODIFIED `JUMP_DISTANCE` (1,000 + one second at top speed), the mod only
in the departure gate; and the grace either dropped or limited to the
client's lag (the `needs/maintainer` question). Confidence: high for (1)-(3)
(six runs plus wave 44's), high that the +1000 arrival is inside the zone
(9.5 s with no jump under a held key), medium for its exact distance (the
anchor).

**Applied 2026-11-27 (f3687e93)**: (4) only. The arrival distance in
`JumpSequenceSystem` is `JUMP_DISTANCE` + one second at top speed, without
the dist mod (was `jumpRadiusFor(JUMP_DISTANCE, jumpDistanceMod)` + one

arrival"). A negative mod arrives the same way (GUESS, unmeasured). (2), the
3 s `ARRIVAL_JUMP_GRACE_MS`, is left for the maintainer; while it stands a
held `j` inside the grace still chains at once from inside an enlarged zone.

### Knockback (the hub's KNOCKBACK), wave 46: a bolt hit adds 30 x Impact / Mass px/s along the shot (six times NovaJS's 5 x), capped at the hull's top speed; a beam pushes the same amount PER Count unit; an inertialess hull at rest sheds the push within 0.3-0.5 s; a disabled inertialess hulk coasts to rest like an inertial one (2026-11-27)

of known Impact on a still hull of known Mass, for a few pairs (NovaJS:

pushed speed capped at the hull's top speed, also for a light hull under
sustained fire (NovaJS since 323037c3: capped, GUESS)? (3) a beam's
Impact: once per shot or per Count unit? (4) a disabled inertialess
hulk's coast.

**Rig** (`wave46Resources` "KB" / "KC"). sÿst 1482 Kit Knock Pad: the

Turn-0 one never fired, `kb20_a`) ON the marker: shïp 417 with wëap 316
Kit Knock 20 (a 1-damage turret bolt, Impact 20, Reload 120, Speed 1500,
Count 150), 418 with wëap 317 (the same at Impact 100), 419 with wëap 318
Kit Knock Beam 20 (a 1-damage turreted beam, Impact 20, Count 30, 3,000

still with no keys; the shooter fires every 7-8 s (not every 4 s) while
the player is within about 1,200 px of it. The player's x / y per frame
from the moons (`tools/kbsum.sh`: `ruler.mjs` blobs, `grid2d.py` on the
pad grid), the velocity steps from linear fits between hits
(`tools/kbfit.py`). Hulls: Kit Probe A (700: Mass 50, Speed 300 = 131
px/s top, inertial), Kit Mass Hull 300 (845: the Shuttle at Mass 300,
Speed 400), Kit Bay Disc (602: Mass 20, Speed 300, inertial), the STOCK
Hyperioid (171: Mass 10, Speed 200 = 87.5 px/s, inertialess: shïp Flags2
0x00C0).

| run | hull (Mass, top speed) | weapon | measured | 30 x I / M |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| kb20_b | Probe A (50, 131) | bolt, Impact 20 | **+11.8, +11.2, +12.3, +12.3, +12.6 px/s** a hit (0 -> 11.8 -> 23.7 -> 35.4 -> 47.1 -> 57.9; then out of range) | 12 |
| kb100_a | Probe A (50, 131) | bolt, Impact 100 | **+58.3, +59.8** (0 -> 58.3 -> 116.7; no third shot in range) | 60 |
| kb100h_a | Mass Hull 300 (300, 175) | bolt, Impact 100 | **+9.8, +10.0, +10.0, +9.7, +10.9, +10.4** (0 -> 9.8 -> ... -> 69.6) | 10 |
| kb100d_a | Bay Disc (20, 131) | bolt, Impact 100 | **+134** in one hit, then **132-135 held** for 10 s and through the next hit | 150 uncapped |
| kbbeamh_a | Mass Hull 300 (300, 175) | beam, Impact 20, Count 30 | **+59.2, +59.0** a beam shot, ramping up over about 0.6-1 s | 2 a shot, 60 per Count |
| kbbeam_a | Probe A (50, 131) | beam, Impact 20, Count 30 | **+94.6** over 0.35 s, then no more push (the beam lost the fast target, GUESS) | 12 a shot, 360 per Count |
| kb20l_a | Hyperioid (10, 87.5, inertialess) | bolt, Impact 20 | each hit: about 9 px of travel over 0.3 s (2 px a frame falling to 0), then AT REST again; 9 hits, nothing kept | 60 |
| kb100l_a | Hyperioid (10, 87.5, inertialess) | bolt, Impact 100 | each hit: 21-22 px over about 0.5 s (about 2 px a frame, then slowing), then at rest; 5 hits, nothing kept | 300 |

**Findings.**
1. **One bolt hit adds 30 x Impact / Mass px/s** (inertial hulls, from
   rest and on top of a drift alike: 15 clean hits over three Impact /
   Mass pairs, 1:2.5, 1:0.5, 1:3; spread +-1 px/s), pointing away from
   the shooter (along the shot, within the fit's 10-25 deg scatter: the
   later hits of kb20_b / kb100_a grew a y part that the shooter-to-ship
   line does not explain; direction not settled). NovaJS's 5 x is SIX
   TIMES too small.
2. **The push is capped at the hull's top speed**: one Impact-100 hit on
   the 20 t disc gave 134 px/s, not 150 (the hull's top speed is 131,
   wave 43's 0.4375 px/s per Speed unit), and the speed stayed there
   through the next hit; pushes that stay under the cap add in full (the
   Probe's 58 -> 117, the Mass Hull's six steps to 70).
3. **A beam pushes per Count unit**, the bolt law each unit: a Count-30
   Impact-20 beam gave 59 px/s on the 300 t hull twice (30 x 2), spread
   over the beam's life (the speed ramped up over about 0.6-1 s), not 2
   px/s once. On the 50 t Probe the push stopped at 95 px/s after 0.35 s
   (about 8 units), most likely because the beam lost the target it had
   just shoved (one run).
4. **An inertialess hull at rest does NOT keep a push**: the Hyperioid
   moved about 9 px (Impact 20) or 21-22 px (Impact 100) at up to about
   2 px a frame (60 px/s) and stopped within 0.3-0.5 s, every hit, so
   nothing accumulated under sustained fire (14 hits in all). A
   300 px/s push (Impact 100, uncapped) did not show: the first frame's
   step was the same 2 px as Impact 20's.
5. **(4) A disabled inertialess hulk coasts to rest** (`kc_b`: wave 25's
   magenta Kit Coast Trader made inertialess, shïp 846, one Kit Disable
   Gun hit while it crept toward the port at 7-8 px/s): its speed fell to
   0 over about 8 s and it drifted 25 px (wave 25's exponential, tau 3.74
   s, predicts 28), then sat still for 20 s; it neither stopped at once
   nor kept its speed. `kc_a` fired too early (the trader about 470 px
   out and nearly at rest: nothing to read).

**NovaJS (main 9bdea902).** `KnockbackSystem`
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:373`) adds `damage.knockback x scale
/ mass x 5`: **mismatch** (x 6); `knockedVelocity` (`:339-342`) caps at the
hull's top speed (or the speed already held): **matches** finding 2 (its
GUESS is now measured). The beam's per-Count-unit `scale`
(`N/nova_plugin/combat/beam_plugin.ts:566`) **matches** finding 3's shape.
The inertialess model (`inertialessControls`,
`packages/nova_ecs/src/plugins/movement_plugin.ts:182-197`) pulls a pushed
hull back toward its heading x targetSpeed at 2 x its acceleration: on the
Hyperioid (45 px/s² x 2) a 60 px/s push would take 0.67 s and 20 px to
shed, against the original's 0.3 s and 9 px; the disabled inertialess
coast (`N/nova_plugin/encounters/disabled_plugin.ts:316-330`) **matches**
finding 5. **Proposed:** (a) the factor 5 -> 30 in `KnockbackSystem` (and
the asteroid push, `N/nova_plugin/combat/asteroid_plugin.ts:577`, GUESS:
the same law); keep the top-speed cap; (b) an inertialess hull sheds a
push faster: about 200 px/s² on the Hyperioid (60 px/s in 0.3 s; about
4.5 x the hull's own 45 px/s² thrust) — GUESS for other hulls and for a
thrusting hull; (c) check that the inertialess shove is capped lower than
the top speed (Impact 100 moved the Hyperioid at the same first-frame 2 px
as Impact 20: the cap may be about 60 px/s there, GUESS). Confidence: high
for (1) and (2) (16 hits, four hulls), high for the beam's per-unit shape
on the slow hull, medium for the inertialess shedding (two runs, one
hull), low-medium for (4) (one slow hulk).

`kb100_a/`, `kb100h_a/`, `kb100d_a/`, `kbbeam_a/`, `kbbeamh_a/`,
`kb20l_a/`, `kb100l_a/`, `kc_a/`, `kc_b/` (`recording.mp4`), `*.pos.txt`,

**Applied 2026-11-27 (82332752)**: (a) `KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT` = 30
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts`, was 5) in `KnockbackSystem`: bolt
hits, beams per Count unit (BeamDamageSystem's `scale`, unchanged) and a
ship's final explosion (its per-ton impact,
`SHIP_EXPLOSION_KNOCKBACK_PER_TON`, kept, so that push grows six-fold,
GUESS: unmeasured), and the asteroid push (AsteroidDamageSystem, GUESS: the
same law on the röid's Mass, still capped at `MAX_ASTEROID_SPEED`); the
top-speed cap kept (its comment now cites finding 2). (b) An inertialess
hull sheds speed ABOVE its throttle's `targetSpeed` at
`INERTIALESS_SHED_PER_ACCELERATION` = 4 x its acceleration
(`packages/nova_ecs/src/plugins/movement_plugin.ts`): 180 px/s² on the

px/s², gave 17 px for the latter); GUESS: a multiple of the hull's own
acceleration for every hull, the same for a thrusting hull. The heading
realign stays at 2 x (`INERTIALESS_REALIGN_PER_ACCELERATION`): pulling the
whole velocity at 4 x left inertialess bay fighters circling their carrier
inside their turning circle instead of docking. (c) Not adopted: the
Impact-100 reading (21-22 px) fits the top-speed cap under this shedding
(19 px), not a 60 px/s cap (8.6 px). The disabled inertialess coast

| cu_i | | **Cancel** | the alert and the plunder dialog close, **no status line**; the player is still in the ring hull with its 10 t of food; the prize is still the target, **"Disabled"** (not "Escort"); the `e` panel lists only the hired Freighter; `b` on the prize: **"You can't board this ship."** |

**Findings.**
1. **The prompt's keys are the buttons' letters: `m` = Use As My Ship, `e`
   = Use As Escort**; `a` (like wave 45's Return and `u`) does nothing.
2. **Cancel on the rename alert cancels the whole capture**: no swap, no
   escort, the player keeps his hull and hold, and the prize stays a
   disabled hulk that has had its one board (wave 8's rule), so the
   capture is simply lost.
3. **The prefill's number is not fixed** (681 here, 631 in wave 45): a
   draw, as the shipyard prompt's (wave 16).
4. **A Capture Ship attempt can trip the self-destruct** (cu_f, STR# 2002
   "Oops! You tripped ..."; wave 25 saw it on plunder takes). This rig's
   seven captures at a shown 75% (waves 45-46): 3 captured, 3
   "unsuccessful", 1 self-destruct.

**NovaJS (main 9bdea902).** `CaptureAssignmentDialog`
(`N/display/boarding_plugin.ts:651-656`): Return, `u` and Escape dead
(matches), and the GUESS "`accept` (A) answers Use As Escort":
**mismatch** (`a` does nothing; `e` answers Use As Escort, `m` Use As My
Ship). The rename alert's Cancel (abf626c0: "GUESS: keeps the prefilled
name and still swaps"): **mismatch** (the capture is abandoned). The
capture roll (`N/nova_plugin/encounters/boarding_plugin.ts:1940`) draws
only success / failure, the self-destruct only per booty take
(`tripPlunderSelfDestruct`, `:1781`): **mismatch** for cu_f.
**Proposed:** bind `m` and `e` to the two answers (not `a`); Cancel ends
the capture with nothing changed (no swap, no escort; the prize stays a
boarded hulk; no status line); let a capture attempt trip the
self-destruct (GUESS: the plunder take's chance; one in seven attempts).
Confidence: high for 1-3 (unambiguous screens), medium for 4 (one
occurrence).

### The ship-explosion push (the hub's knockback follow-up), wave 47: ONE fixed impulse, about 22,100 t px/s (737 impact units), whatever the wreck's mass: 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 t wrecks all threw the 300 t hull at 73-74 px/s and a 1,200 t cruiser at 18.5, radially away, inside the damage square only (none at 210 / 470 / 820 px, just outside it) (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the hub's item 3): the ship-explosion push per ton, on the
same 30 x basis as the weapons (NovaJS: knockback 0.05 x the wreck's tons,
then 30 x / the victim's mass since f40a0326, "ship explosions now 6x
bigger GUESS").

**Rig.** Wave 29's blast rigs unchanged (a live immobile pointer hulk on the
marker at (d, 0), placed exactly by a ShipStart -2 mission; one Kit Pulse
Beam shot kills it; DeathDelay 10), with INERTIAL player hulls instead of

px/s) and Kit Mass Hull 300 (845: Mass 300, Speed 400 = 175 px/s); pilots
`w47_kx*`. The player's velocity from the port planet's track over the 1.5
s after the push (`tools/bigblob.mjs`, `tools/kxfit.py`, `tools/kxrun.sh`).

| run | wreck | d (px) | inside the damage square (2 x (25.5 + 0.037 x mass))? | victim | pushed to | NovaJS main (1.5 x tons / victim mass, capped) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kx2000a_a | 2,000 t | 170 | yes (199) | Probe A, 50 t | **132.8 px/s** (its top speed) | 60 |
| kx2000h_a | 2,000 t | 170 | yes | Mass Hull, 300 t | **72.8** | 10 |
| kx5000h_a | 5,000 t | 380 | yes (421) | Mass Hull, 300 t | **73.9** | 25 |
| kx10000h_a | 10,000 t | 700 | yes (791) | Mass Hull, 300 t | **73.9** | 50 |
| kx2000h210_a | 2,000 t | 210 | no (199) | Mass Hull | **0** | 0 (outside) |
| kx5000h470_a | 5,000 t | 470 | no (421) | Mass Hull | **0** | 0 (outside) |
| kx10000h820_a | 10,000 t | 820 | no (791) | Mass Hull | **0** | 0 |
| kx2000c_a | 2,000 t | 170 | yes | the stock Aurora Cruiser (154: 1,200 t, 87.5 px/s) | **18.5** | 2.5 |

**Findings.**
1. **The push does not grow with the wreck's mass**: a 2,000, a 5,000 and
   a 10,000 t wreck each threw the 300 t hull to 73-74 px/s (+-1), from 170,
   380 and 700 px alike (no fall-off with distance inside the square).
2. **It reaches exactly as far as the damage**: nothing at 210, 470 or 820
   px, each just outside that mass's damage square (wave 29's brackets),
   so the push belongs to the blast, not to a separate radius.
3. **It is radial** (straight away from the wreck: vy 0.0 in every run)
   and arrives within 2-3 frames of the blast; the speed then holds (an
   inertial hull: no drag in 4 s).
4. It is capped at the victim's top speed like a weapon push (the 50 t
   Probe A at 132.8 against its 131).
5. **It goes as 1 / the victim's mass**: the same 2,000 t blast threw the
   1,200 t Aurora Cruiser at 18.5 px/s (read once the cruiser's sprite had
   left the planet's): 300 t x 73.5 = 22,050 and 1,200 t x 18.5 = 22,200
   t px/s, one fixed impulse of about 22,100 t px/s, i.e. about 737 impact
   units on the 30 x Impact / Mass law, whatever the wreck weighed.

**NovaJS (main 996e1c95):** `shipExplosionDamage` gives the blast
`knockback: tons x SHIP_EXPLOSION_KNOCKBACK_PER_TON` (0.05;
`N/nova_plugin/ship/ship_explosion.ts:212`, `:257`) and `KnockbackSystem`
scales it by `KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT` / the victim's mass
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:393-395`): **mismatch** (it grows with
the wreck's mass: 10 / 25 / 50 px/s on the 300 t hull where the original
gave 73-74 for all three). The reach (`insideShipExplosion`, the damage
square) **matches** finding 2, the radial direction (`knockbackDirection`)
finding 3. **Proposed:** a constant knockback for every damaging ship
explosion (100 t and up), about 737 impact units (22,100 t px/s / 30)
through the usual 30 x / the victim's mass; keep the square reach and the top-speed cap. Below
100 t (no damage) GUESS: no push either (not run). Confidence: high for
the mass-independence and the reach (eight runs, every one clean), high for the 1 / mass law (two victim masses, 300 and 1,200 t), the exact 737 good to about 2%.

### An inertialess hull's push shedding against its acceleration (KB leftover), wave 47: the stronger the engine, the faster the shed: an Accel-2000 ring moved 1 px a hit, the Accel-100 glide hull 12-14 px over about 0.55 s, wave 46's Hyperioid 21-22 px; the shove itself tops out near 0.7 of the hull's top speed (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the Wave 46 leftovers row and the hub's item 3): does an
inertialess hull's shed rate follow its acceleration (wave 46's Hyperioid:
about 200 px/s², 4.5 x its 45 px/s² thrust), and is its shove capped near
60 px/s?

**Rig.** Wave 46's Kit Knock Pad (sÿst 1482) with the Impact-100 shooter
(mïsn 1061, bit 9294); the player sits still on the port. Pilots
`w47_kbg100`: shïp 846 Kit Coast Glide Trader flown by the player
(inertialess, Mass 50, Accel 100 = about 17 px/s², Speed 100 = 44 px/s top),
and `w47_kbr100`: shïp 893 Kit Plain Ring (inertialess, Mass 50, Accel
2000 = about 340 px/s², Speed 300 = 131 px/s). Positions on the pad grid
per frame (`tools/kbsum.sh`); 30 x Impact / Mass = 60 px/s for both.

| run | hull (Accel, top speed) | per hit (Impact 100) | the shove | shed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| kbg100_a | Glide (100: 17 px/s², 44 px/s) | **12.5-14 px**, 9 hits | 1 px a frame (about 28-30 px/s) for 0.27-0.35 s | then to rest within about 0.25 s; the whole move 0.47-0.60 s |
| kbr100_a | Plain Ring (2000: 340 px/s², 131 px/s) | **at most 1 px** a hit (6 -> 7 -> 8 px over the watch) | none visible | within a frame |
| wave 46 kb100l_a | Hyperioid (about 45 px/s², 87.5 px/s) | 21-22 px | about 2 px a frame (60 px/s) | about 0.5 s |

**Findings.**
1. **The shed follows the engine**: the Accel-2000 ring keeps nothing of a
   60 px/s push (under one frame, so at least about 2,000 px/s², 6 x its
   thrust or more), the Accel-100 hull sheds about 30 px/s in about 0.25 s
   after a short hold (about 120 px/s², 7 x), the Hyperioid 60 px/s in
   about 0.3 s (200, 4.5 x): a multiple of the hull's acceleration of
   roughly 4-7, not a constant.
2. **The shove is capped well under the push**: the glide hull moved at
   about 28-30 px/s (0.65-0.7 of its 44 px/s top; the law gives 60) and the
   Hyperioid at about 60 (0.69 of 87.5; the law gives 300): GUESS, an
   inertialess hull's push is capped near 0.7 x its top speed (the
   positions step 1-2 px a frame, so +-15 px/s).
3. The glide hull HELD the shove for about 0.3 s before shedding (a
   short plateau, then a fast stop), where a constant deceleration would
   slow it from the first frame.

**NovaJS (main 996e1c95):** `INERTIALESS_SHED_PER_ACCELERATION` 4
(`packages/nova_ecs/src/plugins/movement_plugin.ts:250`,
`inertialessControls` `:182`, f40a0326): **matches** the scaling with the
acceleration (4 x is inside the 4-7 read); the push itself is capped at
the full top speed (`knockedVelocity`, `N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:360`):
**mismatch in part** for inertialess hulls (about 0.7 x the top speed,
GUESS). **Proposed:** keep the 4 x shed (GUESS: 5 would sit mid-range);
cap an inertialess hull's knocked speed at about 0.7 x its top speed
(GUESS from two hulls). Confidence: medium for the scaling (three hulls,
one run each), low for the 0.7 cap and the hold.

asteroids, AstTypes 0x0001: stock röid 128 Metal Small, Mass 150) and 1487
Kit Rock Push Huge (0x0008: röid 131 Metal Huge, Mass 1200), the player

(about 29 deg/s) and ONE forward unguided Kit Rock Knock (wëap 322 Impact

(pilots `w48_rps300` / `w48_rph1200` / `w48_rph300` / `w48_rps1200`).
A rock can't be targeted; the spinning gun sprays the screen, about one
bolt every 19 deg. Rock tracks per recorded frame (`tools/rockpts.mjs`:
blobs brighter than luma 60, linked frame to frame; the player sits still,
so screen = world velocities), and every track split at its velocity kinks
(`tools/kinks.py`: two straight-line fits, at least 0.4 s each side); a
hit is a kink whose velocity change points straight out from the player
(along the bolt, within 15 deg) during the spin, the rock's blob size
steady across it (passing rocks merge into one blob and fake kinks: about
half of all kinks, every one of them off the radial line).

| run | röid (Mass) | Impact | 30 x I / M | radial kinks (px/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rps300_a | Metal Small (150) | 300 | 60 | **57.7, 58.1, 58.2, 58.3** (clean, 90-370 frames a side); 107 once (two hits) |
| rph1200_a | Metal Huge (1200) | 1200 | 30 | **26.0, 27.0, 27.5, 28.1, 28.5, 28.6, 29.9** (the rock within 270 px, 40+ frames a side); 56.8 once (two hits); 13.9-25.4 for rocks half off the screen's edge |
| rph300_a | Metal Huge (1200) | 300 | 7.5 | **5.5, 6.3, 6.9, 7.2, 7.3, 7.5** |
| rps1200_a | Metal Small (150) | 1200 | 240 | the push CLIPPED: velocities after five radial hits (-51.4, -57.7), (-26.5, -58.1), (-61.6, -61.1), (57.9, -58.2), (-57.8, 58.0) px/s: each component that the hit drove past it stops at **about 58 px/s**, the other one unchanged (e.g. vx -26.5 kept, vy 23.9 -> -58.1) |

**Findings.**
1. **A bolt pushes a rock by the ships' law on the röid's Mass**: about
   29 x Impact / Mass px/s (58.0 of 60, 28.4 of 30, 7.0 of 7.5: 0.93-0.97
   of the 30 x that hulls showed in wave 46, i.e. the same law to within
   the reading), over an 8 x range of Mass and a 4 x range of Impact, as long as the
   result stays inside the cap (finding 4).
2. **Along the shot**: every clean kink points straight out from the
   player (within 10 deg), i.e. along the bolt.
3. **No drag**: a pushed rock keeps its new velocity (straight tracks for
   1.5-16 s after the hit).
4. **A rock's speed is capped PER AXIS at about 58 px/s** (2 px a
   physics tick at the game's 29.1 Hz, GUESS for the unit): Impact 1200 on
   a 150 t rock (240 px/s by the law) left every pushed component at
   57.7-58.2 (one pair 61), the untouched component as it was; over all
   four runs no rock was read faster than 58-62 px/s on either axis
   (one-second chords of every track, drift included), so the drift's own
   draw seems bound by the same box.

**NovaJS (main 064a8cd5):** `AsteroidDamageSystem` adds `damage.knockback x
scale x KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT / data.mass` along the damager's heading
(`N/nova_plugin/combat/asteroid_plugin.ts:563-583`; `KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT`
30, `N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:329`), the drift has no drag:
**matches** findings 1-3 (its GUESS is now measured). The cap
(`capAsteroidSpeed`, `MAX_ASTEROID_SPEED` 297 px/s on the speed,
`:115-125`) **mismatches** finding 4 (about 58 per axis); the drift draw
(10-50 px/s in a random direction, `:80-81`) stays inside it.
**Proposed:** keep the law (drop its GUESS); clamp each velocity component
of a rock to +-58 px/s instead of the speed to 297 (pushes and fragments
alike). Confidence for the clamp: medium-high (five clean hits, one run).
Confidence: high for the law (17 clean hits, three Impact / Mass pairs),
medium for the 3-5 % shortfall (it could be a bias of the blob centroids
of spinning rocks).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261127-w48/rps300_a/`,
`rph1200_a/`, `rph300_a/`, `rps1200_a/` (`recording.mp4`), `rp*.pts.txt`,
`tools/rockpts.mjs`, `tools/kinks.py`.

**Applied 2026-11-27 (636a60db)**: `capAsteroidSpeed` clamps each velocity

| run | the control hail (before) | the event | the hail right after it | the pilot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sd2_a | 59.9 s: "Communications channel open." (Greetings / Request Assistance / Close Channel): no offer | 103.3 s: the beam shot; the trader gone ("No Target") at 105.9 s | 108.9 s: **the No / Yes offer of mïsn 1066** (`12-h1.png`) | b9307, b9308, b9311 |

**Findings.**

   is read only when a visit's traffic is built (entry or take-off),
   not per arrival in flight (reliability note).

   ReturnStel, as usual.

(`N/nova_plugin/missions/mission_transitions.ts:113`; `docs/ncb_set_strings.md`

hail (`shipOffers`, `N/spaceport/ship_mission_offer.ts:115`), so NovaJS
would show no offer until the landing. **Proposed:** run OnShipDone when
the goal completes and OnFailure when the mission fails, in flight (the
pending-and-record pattern `docs/ncb_set_strings.md` already outlines for
OnDominate), and move the "Timing gaps" entry to measured. Confidence:

### A tractor beam (the KB leftover), wave 48: it does NOT pull toward an immobile beamer: it BRAKES the target toward the beamer's own (zero) velocity: Kit Probe A at rest never moved under four tractor shots; moving at 30 px/s it was slowed to 10.9 by one shot and stopped dead by the next, 30 px past the beamer, and stayed there (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the Wave 47 leftovers row): a negative-Impact (tractor)
beam (the Bible: "Smaller ships will be pulled towards the firing ship
with a strength proportional to the Impact value ... inertialess ships are
not affected").

**Rig** (`wave48Resources` "KT"). Wave 46's Kit Knock Beamer 20 with the
beam's Impact -20: wëap 324 Kit Tractor Beam 20 (Count 30, Reload 120,
3,000 px), shïp 843 Kit Tractor Beamer 20 (immobile, the stock Terrapin's
175 t, AI 3 of the always-hostile gövt 362), düde 548; mïsn 1073 puts it
on Kit Knock Pad's marker 250 px west of the port. `kta_a` (pilot
`w48_kta`): Kit Probe A (50 t, inertial) still on the port, 32 s;
`ktg_a` (`w48_ktg`): the inertialess glide hull (50 t), the same; `ktm_a`
(`w48_kta`): Probe A takes off, one 0.8 s Up pulse (its take-off heading
happened to point west, at the beamer), then coasts. Positions from the
moon ruler (`tools/kbsum.sh`); the beam's red line in the frames.

| run | the hull | under the tractor (a beam shot every 7-8 s, its line reaching the hull) |
|---|---|---|
| kta_a | Probe A at rest | **never moved** (0.0 px/s, 0 px, 98 s; four shots seen) |
| ktg_a | glide hull at rest | never moved |
| ktm_a | Probe A coasting west at 30 px/s, from the port toward the beamer | 30 px/s to 45 s (x -140); **slowed 30 -> 20.7 -> 10.9 px/s over 46.5-47.5 s** (x -186 .. -209, 40-60 px short of the beamer); coasted on at 10.9 past the beamer; **stopped dead at 53.9 s** (x -280, 30 px beyond it) and stayed there to the end (50 s) |

**Findings.**
1. **The tractor did not pull a still hull** toward the (heavier,
   immobile) beamer: zero motion under four shots.
2. **It brakes a moving one**: the first shot took about 19 px/s off a
   hull flying TOWARD the beamer (a pull would have sped it up), the next
   one stopped it outright while it moved away. So it drags the target's
   velocity toward the beamer's own (here zero), "latching" it to the
   beamer's motion, by about 20 px/s a shot or to a dead stop.
3. The inertialess hull at rest did not move either (the Bible's
   exemption is consistent; not separately tested in motion).

**NovaJS (main 064a8cd5):** a negative Impact is a reversed push
(`KnockbackSystem`'s `damage.knockback x scale / mass x
KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT` along the beam, `N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:385-396`),
so Probe A at rest would be pulled toward the beamer, inertialess hulls
too: **mismatch**. **Proposed:** a tractor beam (Impact < 0) moves the
target's velocity toward the firer's velocity, never past it, by about
20 px/s a 30-unit shot here (GUESS for how the rate scales with Impact and
Mass: not the push law's 360 px/s); inertialess targets exempt (the
Bible). Confidence: medium for the brake (one moving
run, two still ones), low for the rate.

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261127-w48/kta_a/`,
`ktg_a/`, `ktm_a/` (`recording.mp4`), `kt*_a.pos.txt`, `kt*_a.kb.txt`.

**Applied 2026-11-27 (ffda8706, e840c5f7)**: a negative-Impact hit no
longer pulls: `KnockbackSystem` moves the target's velocity toward its
FIRER's (the damager's `SourceComponent`, else the damager's own velocity)
by |Impact| x `TRACTOR_BRAKE_PER_IMPACT` / Mass a unit, never past it
(`tractoredVelocity`); an inertialess target is exempt (the Bible).
`TRACTOR_BRAKE_PER_IMPACT` 1.6 is a GUESS fitted to ktm_a: 20 x 30 x 1.6 /
50 = 19.2 px/s a Count-30 shot, so the 30 px/s Probe goes to 10.8 (read
10.9) and stops dead on the next shot (the push law's 30 would give 360 a
shot). The scaling with Impact and Mass is assumed like the push's. A
still hull never moves (kta_a / ktg_a match). Asteroids hit by a negative
Impact still take the reversed push (unmeasured).

(`RESPAWN_INTERVAL_MS`, `:79`): **mismatch** (a world-fixed field, not
rocks recycled at the viewer's edge). **Proposed:** keep N rocks around
each player's view: when one leaves the view (plus a margin), re-spawn it
1-4 s later at a random point of the view's edge, heading in, with a fresh
velocity (each axis within +-58 px/s); a take-off or arrival starts a
fresh set off screen. In multiplayer this needs a per-viewer (or shared
union-of-views) rule: a design question for Matthew, not a GUESS to
apply. Confidence: high for findings 1-2 (eleven crossings, one rock).

(fits over 0.85 s either side), matched to the bolt track that ended at
the hull just before it (`tools/kbdir.py`; angles in screen degrees, 0 =
+x, 90 = down).

| run, push (s) | step (px/s) | push dir | the bolt's travel (world) | bolt world speed | the runner's line to the hull at the hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kbw_a 59.5 | 6.0 | **-141** | **-140** (from the lower right) | 58.8 | **+39** (the runner off screen upper left) |
| kbw_a 92.2 | 6.9 | -163 | -128 | 53.9 | +46 |
| kbw_a 108.8 | 5.4 | +88 | +44 | 58.6 | -137 |
| kbw_b 60.2 | 5.4 | -148 | -140 | 58.6 | +40 |
| kbw_b 92.4 | 5.5 | -114 | -134 | 58.9 | +44 |
| kbw_b 110.0 | 5.2 | +96 | +38 | 56.2 | -139 |
| kbr_a 45.5 | 10.1 | -138 | -138 | 113.8 | -139 (the runner flying in behind its bolt) |

2. **A bolt's world speed depends on its firer's motion**: the same

**Question** (the hub's item 1, wave 49's KB finding 2-3): what fraction

gun and a turret, and whether the bolt's sprite faces its travel or the
gun's aim.

gives the player's world velocity, `tools/padsum.sh <run> pad`). An
inertial hull thrust from rest coasts on at a constant velocity while it
turns, so a shot's screen velocity is `s x aim + (f - 1) x v`: with f = 1
every shot moves on screen at its nominal speed along its aim, whatever
the aim; with f = 0 a shot along the motion would go BACKWARDS on screen.

the world travel = screen velocity + the player's (`tools/facing.py`).

**Findings.**
1. **A bolt carries ALL of its firer's velocity (f = 1), fixed gun and

### A turret's lead, and a lead into a blind sector (the T leftover), wave 50: the original leads to FIRST ORDER (the target's place plus its relative velocity times distance / shot speed), not to the exact intercept (47 shots within 0.6 +- 0.9 deg of first order, 7-30 deg off the intercept); a rear-blind turret FIRES with its lead 20 deg into the rear sector while the TARGET is at -128 / -134 deg, and stops when the target passes about 135 (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the Wave 49 leftovers row): does a turret whose LEAD falls
in a blind sector, with the target itself in a live one, fire?

**Rig.** `tx_a` .. `tx_d` above (`tx_c` and `tx_d` took off heading
almost straight at the target, so they add leads but no blind crossing): the rear-blind (shïp Flags 0x4000) Kit
Fast Blind Ring coasting at about 220 px/s past the still cyan target with
the 300 px/s turret, so the target's relative velocity (-v) swings the
lead well off the line. The heading is the coast direction (an inertial
hull thrust from rest; the spoke agrees within its 10-14 deg read bias);
the player's place from the grid (extrapolated off the grid at the fitted
velocity); the target at the first moon (-400, -300) (confirmed where it
showed on screen). `tools/tlead.py` prints per shot the target's bearing
off the nose, the aim off the nose (the screen motion: finding 1 above),
and the aims of a first-order lead and of the exact intercept.

| run, shot (s) | target off the nose | aim off the nose | aim | first-order lead | exact intercept | the line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tx_a 48.73 | -127.5 | **-151.2** | -172.3 | -171.1 | +174.0 | -148.6 |
| tx_a 49.07 | -133.6 | **-154.9** | -176.0 | -174.6 | +171.6 | -154.7 |
| tx_a 49.40 (next reload) | about -139.5 | (no shot until the retro turn brought the target back near -135 at 54.5 s) | | | | |
| tx_a return, 22 shots 59.6-66.3 | +12 .. +48 | +42 .. +91 | -158 .. -109 | -156.3 .. -102.9 | -179.2 .. -118.0 | |
| tx_b return, 18 shots 59.3-65.3 | -9 .. -28 | -36 .. -75 | -147 .. +174 | -146.2 .. +173.5 | -127.0 .. -159.5 | |
| tx_b at rest and outbound | +149 and on aft (astern) | no shot in 2.5 s at rest and the whole outbound coast | | | | |
| tx_d outbound (heading at the target), 48.80 / 49.10 / 49.43 | -3 .. -5 | -13 .. -23 | -153.9 / -157.8 / -164.1 | -152.9 / -155.0 / -161.0 | -146.0 / -146.9 / -149.5 | |
| tx_d return, 12 shots 59.1-62.3 (400 px+) | +3 .. +8 | +12 .. +30 | +50 .. +68 | +49.0 .. +67.0 | +42.4 .. +50.6 | |

**Findings.**
1. **The lead is FIRST ORDER**: over 47 coasting shots 380 px or more
   from the target (three runs, five passes) the aim lies 0.6 +- 0.9 deg
   from `angle(d + (v_target - v_shooter) x |d| / shot speed)` (range
   -1.9 .. +1.2), while the exact intercept is 7-30 deg off (e.g. tx_a
   63.03: aim -139.0, first order -137.5, intercept -165.4). Closer in
   (under about 300 px, `tx_d`) the aims drift between the two (the line
   swings several degrees a frame there; see the reliability notes). So against a fast crossing target the
   original's turret aims short of the intercept (it should miss; hits
   were not read). The lead does use the shooter's own velocity (the
   target was still).
2. **The blind sector is the target's, not the aim's**: with the target at
   -127.5 / -133.6 deg off the nose (the live side sector) the rear-blind
   turret fired with its aim at -151 / -155 (20 deg into the rear sector);
   the next reload, with the target at about -139.5, held fire, and it held
   until the retro turn brought the target back to about 135. `tx_b`
   (target astern from the start) never fired at rest or outbound.
   Waves 45-47's 90 deg sectors stand.

**NovaJS (main 055be356):** the blind test is on the TARGET's quadrant
(`blindSpotBlocksQuadrant` on `getQuadrant(...)`,
`N/nova_plugin/combat/fire_weapon_plugin.ts:543-591`), and the aim is not
tested: **matches** finding 2. The turret aims with
`firstOrderWithFallback` (`fire_weapon_plugin.ts:347-350`), which despite
its name solves the EXACT intercept quadratic
(`N/nova_plugin/combat/guidance.ts:57-96`): **mismatch** with finding 1.
**Proposed:** a projectile turret's (Guidance 4; GUESS for the quadrant guns'
in-arc aim) angle = `angle(d + dv x |d| / shotSpeed)` with `d` the target's
position from the exit point and `dv` = target velocity - shooter
velocity (no quadratic, no fallback); leave missile guidance (`guidanceAngle`)
alone. GUESS for beam turrets (instant, no lead). Confidence: high for
the lead (47 shots, three runs), medium-high for the blind
edge (one clean crossing plus `tx_b`'s turn at about the edge).

**Evidence:** `~/.local/share/novaref/evidence/20261127-w50/tx_a/`,
`tx_b/`, `tx_c/`, `tx_d/` (`recording.mp4`), `tx_*.tracks15.txt`,
`tx_*.pos.txt`, `tx_*.hd.txt`, `tlead_all.txt` (the 47 shots),
`tools/tlead.py`.

**Applied 2026-11-27**: a projectile turret (wëap Guidance 4) aims with
`firstOrderLead` (`N/nova_plugin/combat/guidance.ts`):
`angle(d + dv x |d| / shotSpeed)` from the exit point, `dv` = target
velocity - shooter velocity, no quadratic and no fallback (a zero shot
speed points straight at the target); GUESS: first order at every range
(the under-300 px drift is not modelled). Unchanged, as not measured:
the quadrant guns' in-arc aim (Guidance 7 / 8) and projectile point
defence (9) keep the exact intercept (`firstOrderWithFallback`); beam
turrets and point-defence beams point straight at the target
(`BeamWeaponEntry.guidance`); missiles steer by `guidanceAngle` (the
room's default `simple` mode points at the target, `smart` takes the
exact intercept); fixed guns and the AI's own facing do not lead. The
blind test stays on the target's quadrant (finding 2 matches).
MAINTAINER RULING (Matthew, 2026-11-27): "the original game's turrets are
rather inaccurate. We can have a toggle for the player ship to use one or
the other." NPC turrets (escorts' and bay fighters' included) always lead
to first order; a player's OWN ship aims at the exact intercept unless
its pilot turns off the Enhancements toggle "Accurate turret aim"
(`enhAccurateTurretAim`, default on). The choice is synced ship state
(`TurretAim`, `N/nova_plugin/player/turret_aim.ts`), stamped by every
insertion record and changed in flight by a `setTurretAim` input record.

**Findings.**
1. **Beyond a range the tractor PULLS**: a still hull 500 px out is
   accelerated toward the beamer while the beam holds, about 300 px/s² on
   50 t and about 115 on 150 t (roughly in inverse proportion to Mass:
   about 15,000 / Mass px/s² for Impact 20, i.e. 0.86 x the push law's
   30 x |Impact| / Mass a 1/30 s tick), each velocity AXIS capped at the
   hull's top speed (so 1.4 x the top speed on the diagonal, as the rocks'

/ Mass a unit, never past it, with no range or Mass condition
(`tractoredVelocity`, `KnockbackSystem`,
`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:401-470`); inertialess targets
exempt: **matches** 4 and the near hold of 2; **mismatch** for 1 (no
pull at range) and 3 (a 300 t hull would lose 3.2 px/s a shot).
**Proposed:** only a target lighter than its firer (GUESS: strictly) and
not inertialess is affected; beyond about 450 px (GUESS between 425 and
500) a tractor hit accelerates it TOWARD the firer at 0.86 x 30 x |Impact|
/ Mass px/s a tick (per beam Count unit), each velocity axis clamped at the
target's top speed; within that range keep the present brake toward the
firer's velocity. Confidence: high for 3 and 4 and for the pull's
existence (two identical 50 t runs), medium for its rate and axis clamp
(two hulls), medium for the range (one far distance, three near ones,
two geometries).

toward the firer's velocity is unchanged. They never mix within one
unit: a hull pulled in is braked once inside, one that coasts back out is
pulled again. The per-shot totals match (310 px/s of pull on 50 t, cut
to the per-axis cap, 103 on 150 t), but NovaJS lands a Count-30 beam's
units over 30 / 56 s (`BEAM_COUNT_RATE`), so its pull runs at about
580 px/s² on 50 t where the original read 300-325 over about 1 s: the
beam's unit clock and this rate do not agree, unresolved. Asteroids hit
by a negative Impact still take the reversed push (unmeasured).

39-50 used Turn-30 hulls (87.6 deg/s: two thirds untinted, a third

spoke, which drags a least-squares fit on the fast hulls but not this).

| Turn (control deg/s) | untinted, q 0.21-0.33 | 1/3 < q < 1/2 | 1/2 < q < 0.59 | saturated (q 0.88-1.75) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 (29.0) | **0** (k6 after the first hit; k2's tail to q 0.21) | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| 20 (57) | **30** (k6, one hit, q 0.30) | **29-33** (k2 from 67 s, q < 0.5) | **0** (k2 to 65 s) | **0** |
| 30 (87.6, wave 50) | 58.4 | 29 | 29 (wave 50's e6k_d: 27-31 all the way from 58.9 to 33) | 0 |
| 60 (175.0) | **116-120** | **86.5-88.6** | **56-60** | **29.2** (27-31 for 42 s) |
| 100 (290.5) | **204** (q 0.21-0.30), 175-177 (0.30-0.40) | 147-149 (0.40-0.50) | **118-119** | **87.5-88** |
| 200 (581) | 378-379 (0.31-0.33), 408-410 (0.26-0.30), 436-438 (0.22-0.25) | 350 (0.37-0.39), 322 (0.41-0.44), 292 (0.45-0.50) | 262-265 (0.51-0.54), 234-239 (0.55-0.57) | **174.5** (two 15 s windows) |

Every reading is a whole multiple of 29.15 deg/s (one degree a frame at
this machine's 29.15 Hz tick; Turn / 10 degrees a frame uncharged). The
Turn-200 hull's two-hit run steps one degree a frame at a time as the
charge drains, each step where floor(20 x (1 - q)) predicts it (8 at q
0.57-0.55, 9 from 0.54, 10 from 0.50, 11 from 0.44, 12 from 0.39, 13 from
0.34, 14 from 0.29, 15 from 0.25: 25 windows of 5 s, every one on the
predicted step, the changes inside the predicted windows); Turn 100 steps
4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 at q 0.50, 0.40 and 0.30 (67, 101 and 136 s), Turn 60
2 -> 3 -> 4 at 0.50 and 1/3 (66.5 and 124 s), Turn 20 0 -> 1 at 0.50 (67
s), as predicted to about a window.

**Findings.**
1. **Ionization does NOT stop every ship turning**: the saturated turn
   is 0 for Turn 10 / 20 / 30 but 1, 3 and 6 degrees a frame for Turn 60,
   100 and 200 (29.2, 87.5, 174.5 deg/s), i.e. the WHOLE degrees a frame
   strictly below Turn / 30: the charge's cut stops growing at about two
   thirds of IonizeMax (six 30-point hits, q up to 1.75, turned exactly as
   three).
2. **Below that the turn is floor(Turn / 10 x (1 - q)) degrees a
   frame**, LINEAR in the charge and truncated to whole degrees: neither
   thirds of the turn (Turn 10 would turn at 19.5 deg/s untinted; it
   never turns once hit) nor a fixed number of Turn units per stage (Turn
   200 saturated would be 437). The truncation is why a slow hull loses
   everything at once (Turn 10: floor(0.99) = 0 from the first point of
   charge) and why Turn 30 showed exactly three levels at 1/3 and 2/3:
   those lines are where 3 x (1 - q) crosses 2 and 1. A hull whose Turn is
   a multiple of 30 has steps at 1/3 and 2/3; Turn 60 also at 1/2, Turn
   200 every 0.05.
3. **The tint line (1/3) is a visual line, not a turn line**: Turn 200
   changed its turn at q 0.35 (12 -> 13) inside the tint and at 0.30 (13
   -> 14) outside it, nothing at 0.333 itself.
4. **The saturation's exact form** is either q held at 2/3 with the turn
   STRICTLY below Turn / 10 x (1 - q) (ceil(x) - 1, which equals floor(x)
   for every non-whole x), or floor with q held at about 0.7; the hulls
   flown here (Turn / 10 x 1/3 = 0.33, 0.67, 1, 2, 3.33, 6.67) cannot tell
   them apart, and nothing else here depends on it.

**NovaJS (main ff820fb6):** `ionSlowdown` multiplies the turn by thirds
of the full cut whatever the hull: two thirds up to `ION_IONIZED_FRACTION`
(1/3), a third up to `ION_NO_TURN_FRACTION` (2/3), `ION_FULL_TURN_FACTOR`
0 above (`N/nova_plugin/ship/ionization_plugin.ts:80`, `:95`, `:107`,
`:118-119`, `:174-197`; applied as `base.turnRate x ion.turnRate`,
`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:168`): **matches** only for
Turn 30 (and any hull at no charge); **mismatch** for every other Turn: a
saturated Turn-60 / 100 / 200 hull is stopped (the original keeps 29 /
87.5 / 175 deg/s), a Turn-10 hull keeps 19.5 deg/s untinted and 9.7
tinted (the original 0 at any charge), Turn 60 tinted turns 58 deg/s
throughout (the original 87.5 while q < 1/2), Turn 200 untinted 387 deg/s
fixed (the original 379-437 by the charge).
**Proposed:** replace the turn's thirds by the staircase: with q =
min(current / max, 2/3) and the uncharged turn in degrees per 1/30 s
frame d = Turn / 10 (the parse's `ShipTurnRateConversionFactor` scale), an
ionized ship (current > 0) turns ceil(d x (1 - q)) - 1 whole degrees a
frame (equivalently floor(d x (1 - q) - 1e-9)), never below 0, i.e. a
turnRate multiplier of that over d; the acceleration and the tint keep
their own lines. GUESS for a Turn that is not a multiple of 10 (the
uncharged turn may itself be whole degrees; not measured) and for the
strict-below form at exactly 2/3. Confidence: high (five hulls, three
stages each, a 25-window staircase on Turn 200 and the step times on
Turn 20 / 60 / 100 / 200 all where the formula puts them).

`ION_CHARGE_HOLD` 0.7 (GUESS inside the 2/3-0.72 bracket: floor at 0.7,

**Question** (from the staircase above): is the uncharged turn of a Turn
that is not a multiple of 10 (102 of the 288 stock hulls: 25, 35, 39,
55, ...) also whole degrees a frame, and does the charge cut the raw Turn
or the truncated one?

**Rig.** shïp 776 Kit Ring Ion T25 (added; wave 4's S50 jam set retired),
pilot `w51_t25`: `c_t25` (no landing, Right held 20 s) and `k2_t25` (two
hits, the kill at 5.5 s, Right held 45 s: q from about 0.57 to 0.43, tinted
throughout, G/B 0.49-0.51). Rates by `tools/hough.py`; the phase vote's
score at 58.3 / 72.9 / 87.5 deg/s is printed against the best.

| run | best rate (deg/s) | votes at 58.3 / 72.9 / 87.5 (of the samples) |
|---|---|---|
| c_t25 (19 s) | **58.5** | 332 / 109 / 106 (of 555) |
| c_t20 (14 s) | 56-58.5 | 251 / 85 / 81 (of 419) |
| k2_t25, q 0.57-0.50 (40-64 s) | **29.5** (all 309 samples on the line) | |
| k2_t25, q 0.48-0.43 (70-84 s) | **29.5** | |

**Findings.**
1. **Turn 25 turns exactly as Turn 20 uncharged** (58.5 against 56-58.5
   deg/s; 72.9 has a third of the votes of 58.3): the uncharged turn is
   floor(Turn / 10) whole degrees a frame.
2. **The charge cuts the raw Turn**: floor(2.5 x (1 - q)) is 1 for q in
   0.43-0.57 and the hull turned 29.5 deg/s throughout; cutting the
   truncated 2 would have given floor(2 x (1 - q)) = 0 until q fell below
   1/2 (about 67 s). So one law covers both: floor(Turn / 10 x (1 -
   min(q, about 0.7))) degrees a frame, q = 0 uncharged.

**NovaJS (main ff820fb6):** the turn rate is Turn x
`ShipTurnRateConversionFactor`, continuous (`P/parsers/ship_parse.ts:432`):

with the ion staircase above, turn = floor(Turn / 10 x (1 - min(q, 0.7)))
degrees per frame for every ship (q = 0 uncharged), i.e. the base turn
rate floor(Turn / 10) x 10 x the conversion factor. GUESS from one
non-multiple Turn (25); a Turn-35 / 55 hull should confirm before a change
that moves 102 stock hulls. Confidence: medium-high (one hull, two runs,

### A tractor beam's pull frame by frame, its Impact scaling and the brake's Mass gate (the hub's item 3, the KB leftover), wave 51: the pull builds STEADILY for the beam's whole ~1 s (about 345 px/s² on a 50 t hull at Impact 20, about 705 at Impact 40: in proportion to Impact), about 30 x |Impact| / Mass px/s a 1/30 s unit, the push law itself; the NPC tractor's Count-30 beam shows for about 1 s (30 units a second) while the player's Count-30 beam in the same system shows for 17 frames (wave 41's Count / 56); the near brake does take a LIGHTER moving hull (29 -> 10 -> 0 px/s at about 350 px) and did not touch a heavier one (wave 50's `trm_b`, 300 t at 357 px) (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the hub's item 3): wave 50's pull (300-325 px/s² on 50 t
over about 1 s) against NovaJS delivering a Count-30 beam's units over
30 / 56 s; how the pull builds within one firing (a velocity per frame),
and whether the near brake is gated by the firer's Mass too (wave 50's fix
GUESSES it is).

**Rig.** Wave 50's Kit Tractor Beamer 20 (düde 548: immobile, Impact -20,

moon (mïsn 1078), 500 px from the port on the -143 deg diagonal; and

Probe A (50 t) on Kit Tractor Range 350's port, a 0.6 s Up pulse sends it
west at 28.5 px/s toward the beamer 350 px away (`tr350m_a`, `tr350m_b`,
pilot `w50_tr350`). Places on the grid per frame (`tools/padsum.sh`), the
velocity over +-5 frames (`tools/trtrace.py`), the beam's frames by its
red line (`tools/redcount.py`).

| run | beam (s, video) | the hull's speed toward the beamer, every 0.1 s from the beam's start | after |
|---|---|---|---|

**Findings.**
1. **The pull builds steadily for the whole beam**: from the first beam
   frame the speed toward the beamer grows about 33-35 px/s every 0.1 s
   (345 px/s² at Impact 20 on 50 t) until the beam goes out after about
   1.0 s, then holds (330 px/s on trb_c, the x axis just at its 262 cap):
   one unit of pull a 1/30 s frame for the beam's 30 frames, about 11.5
   px/s each, i.e. **about 30 x |Impact| / Mass a unit, the push law's own
   30** (wave 50's 0.86 came from per-axis-capped Probe A readings).
2. **It is in proportion to Impact**: Impact 40 built 707 and 657 px/s²
   (two runs, 0.1-0.4 s: 55 -> 267, 40 -> 237), 1.97 x Impact 20's 345,
   until each axis met the 262 cap (x at 0.5 s, y at 0.7-0.8 s: 372 px/s
   at -135 deg).
3. **The NPC tractor's beam lasts about 1 s for Count 30** (29-31 frames
   of red line in every beamer shot of waves 50-51), and the pull lasts as
   long; the PLAYER's Count-30 Kit Plain Beam (wave 40's fixed beam, wëap
   301) shows for **17 and 17 frames on the same Kit Knock Grid** (`e10g_a`,
   F12 reading 56 fps there) and 16 and 16 at Kit Port (`e10p_a`): wave
   41's Count / 56 s. So it is not the system's drawing rate: the NPC (or
   turret, the tractor is Guidance 3) beam counts its units at about 30 a
   second, the player's fixed beam at about 56.
4. **The near brake takes a lighter MOVING hull**: Probe A coasting at
   28.5 px/s toward the beamer 185 px off lost 19 px/s over one shot
   (to 9-10) and stopped at the next, twice, exactly wave 48's ktm_a (30 ->
   10.9 -> 0); still hulls there never moved (wave 50). Wave 50's `trm_b`
   (Kit Mass Hull 300, 300 t against the 175 t beamer) coasted at 40.8 px/s
   357-360 px from the beamer through a whole shot (40.27-41.23 s) and kept
   all of it: **the brake is gated by Mass too** (at least for a hull
   heavier than the beamer; the 175-300 t gap is unread).

**NovaJS (main ff820fb6):** the pull beyond `TRACTOR_PULL_RANGE` is
`TRACTOR_PULL_PER_IMPACT` = 0.86 x 30 a unit with the per-axis cap
(`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:430`, `:449`, `:460-468`), a beam's units landing
over Count / `BEAM_COUNT_RATE` (56) s (`P/parsers/constants.ts:13`,

`:550-566`): **matches** the shape (one push-law unit a beam unit, in

the brake's Mass gate and rate (finding 4; `tractoredVelocity`,
`TRACTOR_BRAKE_PER_IMPACT` 1.6, `:404-418`; the Mass gate `:514`); **mismatch** in the clock (a
Count-30 shot pulls for 0.54 s at about 580 px/s² where the original
pulls for 1.0 s at 345) and in the size (0.86 against about 1.0 x the
push law: 310 against 330-345 px/s a shot). **Proposed:**
`TRACTOR_PULL_PER_IMPACT` = `KNOCKBACK_PER_IMPACT` (30), and an NPC
beam's Count (life, damage and pull units) at 30 a second, the player's
fixed beam keeping `BEAM_COUNT_RATE` 56 (GUESS which of NPC / turret
decides it: a player turret beam and an NPC fixed beam are unread). Confidence: high for the steady build and the Impact scaling
(two clean runs at Impact 40, one clean and one jumpy at Impact 20), high
for the two beam lives (every shot of two waves against four player
taps in two systems), medium for the 1.0 x (the x axis met its cap in
the last 0.1 s of the Impact-20 shot), high for the brake's Mass gate on a
heavier hull (one run, a whole shot unchanged).
