### The UNCHARGED base turn on every hull (the hub's item 1, E6), wave 52: whole degrees a frame, max(1, floor(Turn / 10)): Turn 7, 9 and 15 all turn 1 degree a frame (29 deg/s), Turn 25 two (58.5, again), 35 three (87.5), 55 five (146), 95 nine (262); a saturated Turn-95 hull turns 2 a frame (58), so the charge is held at q 0.7 (floor), not 2/3 (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the hub's item 1; wave 51 saw Turn 25 turn as Turn 20): is
the uncharged turn whole degrees a frame for EVERY hull? If so it moves
the 102 stock hulls whose Turn is not a multiple of 10 (and the five
Aurora Carriers at Turn 7-11). And the wave-51 leftover: is the
saturation hold floor at q 0.7 or "strictly below" at q 2/3 (a saturated
Turn-95 hull turns 2 or 3 degrees a frame)?

**Rig** (`wave52Resources` "E6B"). Wave 51's Kit Ring Ion (the white-spoke
inertialess ring, IonizeMax 100, Deionize 1) at Turn 7 / 9 / 15 / 35 / 55
/ 95 (shïp 606-611, wave 40's E11 hulls retired) and wave 51's T25 (776),
pilots `w52_t<Turn>` at Kit Knock Grid Port. `c_t<n>`: Enter Ship (no
landing: no mission, no charge), off the port (Up 0.8 s, Down), Right
held 20 s (30 s for Turn 7 / 9). `k6_t95`: land, accept mïsn 963 (the Kit
Ion Shot Target, 30 a hit), Leave and turn at once, Tab + the Kit Beam
Turret kill it 19 s later after six hits (q about 1.8), Right held 30 s
more. The spoke's heading on every frame (`tools/e6b.sh`: headings.mjs
SPOKE=vw step 1), the rate by `tools/hough.py`'s phase vote over the whole
hold and per 5 s window, and the unwrapped total turn over the hold.

| Turn | continuous (NovaJS) deg/s | whole degrees a frame (deg/s at 29.15 Hz) | measured: phase vote over the hold | total turn / time | degrees a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 20.4 | 0 (floor) / 1 | **29.0** (58 % of 870 samples) | 864 deg / 29.06 s = **29.7** | **1** |
| 9 | 26.2 | 0 (floor) / 1 | **30.0** (61 %) | 838 / 29.07 = **28.8** | **1** |
| 15 | 43.7 | 1 = 29.2 | **29.5** (57 %) | 551 / 19.07 = **28.9** | **1** |
| 25 (again) | 72.9 | 2 = 58.3 | **58.5** (69 %) | 1,123 / 19.07 = **58.9** | **2** |
| 35 | 102.0 | 3 = 87.5 | **87.5** (69 %) | 1,619 / 19.07 = **84.9** | **3** |
| 55 | 160.3 | 5 = 145.8 | **146.0** (66 %) | 2,837 / 19.07 = **148.8** | **5** |
| 95 | 276.9 | 9 = 262.4 | **262.0** (68 %) | 4,993 / 19.07 = **261.8** | **9** |
| 95 saturated (k6_t95, 56-84 s, q 1.5-1.8) | 0 (NovaJS's no-turn third) | 2 (q held 0.7) / 3 (q 2/3) | **58.0** (97 % of 354 samples; every 5 s window 58.5-65.5) | | **2** |

The 5 s windows of the slow hulls scatter (Turn 15: 17.5-47.5; a slow
ring reads +-20 deg a frame, wave 51's note), so the whole-hold vote and
the total are the readings; the fast hulls' windows sit on the line
(Turn 95: 263-264 in every full window).

**Findings.**
1. **The uncharged turn is whole degrees a frame on every hull**: Turn
   35, 55 and 95 turn exactly 3, 5 and 9 degrees a frame (87.5, 146, 262
   deg/s), Turn 25 two again: floor(Turn / 10).
2. **But never below one degree a frame**: Turn 7 and 9 (floor 0) and 15
   (floor 1) all turn 1 degree a frame (29 deg/s): Turn 7 turns 45 %
   FASTER than its Turn says, Turn 9 11 % faster. So the uncharged law is
   max(1, floor(Turn / 10)) for any Turn > 0 (Turn 1-6 unread; the stock
   minimum is 7).
3. **The ion cut has no such floor**: wave 51's Turn 10 never turned once
   hit (floor(1 x (1 - q)) = 0 from the first point of charge), so the
   minimum of 1 applies to the uncharged turn only (GUESS: the game takes
   floor(Turn / 10 x (1 - q)) when ionized and max(1, floor(Turn / 10))
   otherwise; a charged Turn-7 hull would then stop dead, unread).
4. **The saturation hold is q = 0.7 with floor**: a saturated Turn-95
   hull turned 2 degrees a frame (floor(9.5 x 0.3) = 2), not 3 (strictly
   below 9.5 / 3 = 3.17). With wave 51's Turn 200 (6 a frame saturated:
   20 (1 - q) in [6, 7) gives q in (0.65, 0.70]) the hold sits in (0.684,
   0.70]: 0.7, the thrust's hold too (wave 51's 0.28-0.32).

**NovaJS (main 14052c16, with wave 51's ion fix 125c551a):** the base
turn rate is still Turn x `ShipTurnRateConversionFactor`, continuous
(`P/parsers/ship_parse.ts:432`); the ion cut is now wave 51's staircase,
floor(d x (1 - min(q, ION_CHARGE_HOLD))) / d with d = the uncharged rate
in degrees a frame (`turnFactor`, `N/nova_plugin/ship/
ionization_plugin.ts:162-171`, `ION_CHARGE_HOLD` 0.7 at `:80`, applied at
`N/nova_plugin/travel/afterburner_plugin.ts:149` / `:168`): **matches**
the hold (finding 4: 0.7 with floor, the GUESS in `:70-79` is now
measured); **mismatch** in the base turn for every hull whose Turn is not
a multiple of 10 (Turn 35, the 18 stock Star Liner / Terrapin / Argosy /
IDA Frigate / Valkyrie / Rebel Destroyer class hulls: 102 against 87.5
deg/s; Turn 55: 160 against 146; Turn 45: 131 against 117) and the other
way for Turn 7-9 (the Aurora Carriers nova:297-300: 20-26 against 29
deg/s); Turn 11 / 14 turn 32 / 41 against 29. Because `turnFactor` takes
d from the continuous base rate, a charged Turn-25 hull keeps floor(2.5 x
(1 - q)), as measured (wave 51) — the fix must keep that raw d for the
cut while the UNCHARGED rate becomes whole degrees. **Proposed:** the
uncharged turn max(1, floor(Turn / 10)) degrees per 1/30 s frame (that x
10 x the conversion factor) for Turn > 0, the ion cut unchanged
(floor(Turn / 10 x (1 - min(q, 0.7))) on the RAW Turn / 10, no minimum of
1), i.e. `turnFactor` returns kept / that uncharged whole-degree rate.
GUESS for Turn 1-6 and for a charged Turn < 10. Confidence: high (seven
hulls, every one on its whole-degree line within 2 %, the continuous rates
8-46 % away; the saturated Turn 95 on 2 a frame in every window).

### A tractor shot that starts outside the pull range and crosses inside it (the hub's extra, KB), wave 52 (re-read of wave 51's runs, no new run): the pull goes on for the WHOLE shot: the pulled hull passed 425 px (where a still hull is never pulled) about 0.6-0.7 s into the 1 s beam and kept speeding up toward the beamer to the beam's end, never braked; so the pull / brake choice is made per SHOT, not per beam unit (2026-11-27)

**Question** (the hub, with wave 51's tractor fix landing): NovaJS decides
pull or brake per beam UNIT by the distance (`TRACTOR_PULL_RANGE` 450).
Does a shot that starts outside the range keep pulling after the target
crosses inside, or switch to braking mid-shot?

**Data** (wave 51's `trb_c` and `trb40_d`, "A tractor beam's pull frame
by frame ... wave 51"): Kit Probe B (50 t) at rest 500 px from the
immobile beamer, one Count-30 shot (1.0 s). Integrating the measured speed
toward the beamer (every 0.1 s from the beam's first frame) gives the
distance during the shot:

| run | 0.4 s | 0.5 s | 0.6 s | 0.7 s | 0.8 s | 0.9 s | 1.0 s (beam out) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| trb_c (Impact 20): distance px | 477 | 464 | 447 | 426 | 401 | 373 | 343 |
| trb_c: speed toward the beamer, px/s | 114 | 149 | 194 | 228 | 264 | 296 | 317 |
| trb40_d (Impact 40): distance px | 477 | 457 | 431 | 399 | 364 | 327 | 289 |
| trb40_d: speed px/s | 162 | 237 | 296 | 343 (x at its cap) | 363 | 374 (both caps) | 374 |

Wave 50 held a STILL hull at 425 px (and 350, 250) through whole shots:
a shot that starts inside 425 never pulls (and brakes a moving lighter
hull, wave 51 `tr350m_*`).

**Finding.** Once a shot starts pulling it pulls to its end: in trb_c the
hull was inside 425 px for the last 0.3 s and inside 400 for the last 0.2
s and kept gaining 30-35 px/s every 0.1 s (the same steady 345 px/s² as
outside), and the Impact-40 shot pulled on from 431 px to 289 px until
both velocity axes met their cap. A per-unit choice at any edge in the
measured 425-500 bracket would have braked those last units toward zero.
So the original chooses pull or brake when the SHOT starts (by the
distance then), GUESS: the same per shot for the brake (a shot that starts
braking inside the range brakes to its end even if the hull leaves it).

**NovaJS (main 14052c16):** per beam unit: each unit tests the current
distance against `TRACTOR_PULL_RANGE` (450) and pulls beyond it, brakes
inside (`N/nova_plugin/ship/death_plugin.ts:438`, `:548-555`):
**mismatch** for a hull that crosses 450 during a pulling shot (NovaJS
would brake its last units: trb_c's from about 0.55 s). **Proposed:** fix
the mode per shot at its first unit (store pull / brake with the beam
entity, beam_plugin.ts) and apply it to every unit of that shot.
Confidence: medium-high (two shots of two Impacts, distances integrated
from the measured speeds within about 10 px; the exact edge in 425-500 is
still unread).

### Reliability notes (for anyone running the reference)

- **Stock mission bits live above 9000 too (wave 51 `trb40_a` / `_b`):**
  the stock data tests or sets 9011-9015, 9111, 9200-9208, 9215-9216,
  9333-9334, 9500-9501, 9666, 9812, 9995 and 9998-9999. A pilot holding
  bit 9334 is offered stock mïsn 861 "Head Back to Merrol" on landing,
  which the scripted Return accepts instead of the kit's mission (no
  beamer came, the pilot went home with the stock job). Check a new kit
  bit against the stock list (README) before using it; wave 50's mïsn
  1081 sits on 9333, which stock mïsn 142's OnAccept only clears.
- **A spoke reading of a fast or tinted ring needs `tools/hough.py`
  (wave 51 E6T):** a least-squares fit, even with outlier clipping, is
  dragged by misread headings (a grid moon under the ring, the tint's
  green flicker, the 10 deg sprite steps at 6-20 deg a frame), giving 85-400
  deg/s for a steady 175; the phase vote reads it to 1-2 deg/s with
  33-100 % of the samples on the line. A slow ring (Turn 10) reads +-20
  deg a frame, so use windows of 7 s or more.
- **Bolts on the port are invisible (wave 51 `a6_*`):** a hull sitting on
  the port under the Kit Ion Shot Target shows only the Leave's hit in
  `colorcount.mjs` (the rest land over the planet's cloud); count its hits
  by the target's 3.6-3.8 s reload instead.
- **`grep -q 'c_t20'` matches `c_t200` (wave 51):** a queue wait on a run
  name must anchor it (`'== c_t20 '`), or it returns on a longer name.
- **The grid track's velocity jumps at moon hand-offs (wave 51 `trb_a`):**
  two-frame differences of `grid2d.py` places swing +-30-60 px/s at 300
  px/s as moons enter and leave; read a pull's profile over +-5 frames or
  by quadratic fits of the places (`tools/trtrace.py`).
- **The open_pilot flake again (wave 51 `trb_b`):** "could not open pilot
  ... (panel still open; cancelled)", not retried by `run`; rerun it.

- **A stock hull's red markings defeat `redcount.py` (wave 50 `tre_a`):**
  the Enterprise counts as a beam every frame; read beam times off a kit
  hull's run in the same rig (the beamer's 7.1-7.2 s cycle).
- **Launches can take 20 s (wave 50 `tr350_a`):** the Leave came at 45 s
  of video instead of 32-35; read every time off the events file.
- **Count ion hits from the Leave (wave 50 E6):** the first hit lands
  the instant the ship appears (a one-frame bolt at the ring, Leave +
  0.1-0.5 s, over the planet), and a ship on the port takes a hit every
  reload until it moves off. Wave 42 counted from its move off the planet
  (frame 1300) and missed three or four, which halved its tint / no-turn
  lines (and led to the 56 fps drain GUESS). Read the episodes from the
  Leave (`tools/episodes.py` on a colorcount from the Leave's frame).
- **A one-frame yellow blob beside a thrusting ring is its engine glow
  (wave 50 `e6r_*`)**, not an ion hit: colorcount's orange class takes it.
- **Put a timed kill in the SAME keys step as the Leave (wave 50
  `e6k_a`):** separate `shot` steps between the Leave and the kill cost
  about 13 s (ask round trips through terrapin), so six 30-point hits
  landed instead of one and the hull never turned again in 170 s.
- **The ring's white spoke reads 10-14 deg off an inertial coast's
  direction (wave 50 TX)**: `SPOKE=white` on the 36-frame sprite; for an
  inertial hull thrust from rest, take the heading from the grid velocity.
- **The streak sprite's blob axis is biased 13-16 deg at diagonal aims
  (wave 50 FX):** the tapered Medium Blaster streak's second moments
  read -144 deg as -158; calibrate a facing reading with shots at rest at
  the same aims.
- **`grid2d.py` re-acquires off-grid only by luck (wave 50 TX):** its
  stale last place picks the nearest grid point when moons come back on
  screen; extrapolate off-grid places from the coast velocity and check
  them where a known object (the cyan target) shows on screen.
- **Hit sparks on a still target track like bolts moving at -v (wave 50
  `tx_c`, `tx_d`):** a straight run through the target leaves orange
  sparks fixed in the world; `bolttracks.py` lists them at the player's
  speed opposite its motion (aim "180 off the nose"); drop them.
- **Turret leads near the target (under about 300 px) drift between the
  first-order and exact aims (wave 50 `tx_d`):** the line swings several
  degrees a frame there, so a one-frame error in a shot's birth or a
  20 px error in the extrapolated place shows; use shots 400 px+ out.

- **A mission's cargo is checked against the player's OWN hold; the
  HUD's Free is the fleet's (wave 49 `cu90_a`):** with a hired AI 1
  Kit Trader the HUD read Free 100 (50 + 50) and the BBS still refused a
  90 t job ("Your ship doesn't have enough cargo space ..."). Size a job
  to the hull's own Cargo, and leave cargo-capable escorts out of a hold
  reading (wave 45's "Free: 80" prize was 30 + the trader's 50).
- **An AI 3 shooter flies AT its target (wave 49 KB / T):** a Turn-30
  runner closed head-on with its slow bolt beside it, and even a Turn-10,
  Speed-500 one made straight passes through the player rather than
  circles, so the bolt, the shooter's line and its heading coincided and
  turret leads stayed under 3 deg. A shooter that moves ACROSS the line
  needs a different AI (a lane trader, an orbiting mission ship).
- **A pushed hull leaves a 400 px grid fast (wave 49 `kbr_a`):** Impact
  100 on 300 t (10 px/s a hit, no drag) took Kit Mass Hull 300 off Kit
  Knock Grid within about 25 s; Impact 50 kept it on for the whole minute
  (`kbw_*`).
- **The radar's white dot is a ship, its grey dots stellars (wave 49):**
  `analysis/radar_blips.mjs --colour red` found no hostile ship (ship
  dots are white, 252); keep blips with min(rgb) > 200 and carry the last
  one over blink gaps.
- **A carrier's fight off screen is read on the radar (wave 49 `ecq_a`):**
  the fighters docked about 1,000 px out, where the carrier stood; window
  shots showed only an empty port. `tools/radarseries.mjs` every 0.5 s.
- **A stopped hand-driven run needs `novaref recover` (wave 49
  `cu90_a`):** SIGTERM to the run's node ended it with the game, the
  plug-in and the parked Last Pilot still in place; `recover` cleaned
  them (plug-in uninstalled, Last Pilot restored, Matt verified).
- **`rm` of a shell-variable glob is refused by the harness (wave 49):**
  write each frame dump to a fresh directory instead of clearing one.

- **Traffic AppearOn is no in-flight bit reader; a person's hail is
  (wave 48 SD2 / SF2):** wave 47's magenta traffic gated on OnShipDone's
  bit never came in flight although the bit was set at once; AppearOn is
  read when a visit's traffic is built. A stock përs overridden by a
  run-only plug-in (`kits/w48_pers225.mjs`), in a kit system's Person slot
  at 100 %, whose LinkMission's AvailBits test the bits, reads them at
  the hail: a No / Yes offer instead of the comm dialog. Hail it once
  before the event as the control.
- **Passing rocks fake velocity kinks (wave 48 RP):** two rocks that
  touch merge into one blob, and the tracker follows the merged centroid:
  about half of all kinks in a dense field, every one off the radial line
  from the player. Keep only kinks along the bolt (radial within 10-15
  deg) with a steady blob size; a huge rock half off the screen's edge
  reads low (its centroid lags).
- **Rock speeds are clipped per axis (wave 48 RP):** no rock moves faster
  than about 58 px/s on either screen axis, so a push read on a rock
  already near the box reads short; push experiments need the result to
  stay inside it (Impact 1200 on a 150 t rock was all clip).
- **`padsum.sh` needs the `ion` grid on the Kit Ion Pad (wave 48 E6):**
  its default `pad` grid (Kit Accel Pad) fits nothing once the probe has
  left the port ("no track"); run `padsum.sh <run> ion`.
- **`waitready.mjs` and a second interactive step (wave 48 CU):** in a
  scenario with two interactive breaks, waitready returns at once on the
  first break's `{"done":true}` line; wait for the SECOND `"ready":true`
  in the outbox (`grep -c`) before driving the second break.
- **A copied `mkpilots.mjs` rebuilds the previous wave's pilots (wave 48,
  again):** retargeted by sed it kept the old wave's names and specs and
  rewrote `pilots/w47/*` (same specs, so harmless this time). Replace the
  copy before the first run, as wave 45 said.
- **A carrier outside the beam's reach survives the CD bursts (wave 48
  `cd_d`):** the two 1.5 s Kit Beam Turret bursts killed the Fed Carrier
  in waves 46-47 but not here (it stayed out of the 1,500 px beam); read
  the target panel after the bursts before watching for orphans.
- **A kit ring hull coasts after an Up pulse (wave 47 `trear_a`):** the Kit
  Plain Ring (shïp Flags2 0x00C8, Accel 2000) took off at rest, and a 1 s
  Up pulse sent it about 1,600 px before a Down press stopped it (wave 3:
  inertialess hulls do NOT stop on thrust release; Down brakes). Never
  "nudge" an inertialess hull off a port without a Down right after.
- **Bolts over a planet are lost; read them past its disc (wave 47 T):**
  `analysis/bolt_births.mjs` misses bolts born over the port's cloud
  pixels; a spin on the port reads them where they leave the disc (35-120
  px out, flying radially) and puts each back to its firing frame by its
  speed (`tools/spinsum.mjs`): trear_a's 31 broken runs of fire became 14.
- **oütf ModType 9 is not in Turn units (wave 47 T):** -260 on a Turn-30
  hull left it turning 29 deg/s (Turn about 10), not the 12 deg/s that
  "100 = 30 deg/s" read as Turn x 10 predicts. Measure the turn on the run.
- **The player's turret holds fire at a friendly mission escort (wave 47
  `sf_a`):** the Kit Pulse Beam never fired at a targeted ShipBehav-1
  protector (2.5 s of Space); a muzzle blast (Kit Blast Bomb) hurts it.
- **A retried run leaves two dirs (wave 47 `tside_a`):** the failed first
  attempt's dir sits beside the `-retry1` one, so `run/2*/` globs both;
  take the last (`ls -d run/2*/ | tail -1`).
- **The radar shows no asteroids, and rock velocities bunch (wave 47
  E9):** a field cannot be read off the radar, and two rocks can share a
  velocity within about 1 px/s by chance.
- **Traffic AppearOn as an in-flight bit reader is weak (wave 47 SD /
  SF):** the gated traffic never showed in flight, which fits both "the
  bit is set late" and "AppearOn is checked only when a visit's traffic is
  built"; pair it with a reader known to work in flight.
- **The planet blob merges with a big victim hull (wave 47 `kx2000c_a`):**
  a 1,200 t cruiser at the centre overlaps the port planet's blob until it
  has moved off it; fit only the frames whose blob size is back to the
  planet's own.


- **An immobile AI 3 shooter needs a Turn (wave 46 `kb20_a`):** a Turn-0,
  Speed-0 AI 3 with a turret bolt sat 250 px from the player for 50 s and
  never fired (waves 44-45's Turn-0 ion targets fired at a player ON TOP
  of them); with Turn 60 it fired at once. Its Reload 120 bolt came only
  every 7-8 s, and only while the player was within about 1,200 px (the
  bolt's own reach was 2,250).
- **A single moon row loses a drifting ship (wave 46 `kb100_a`):** the
  pushed ship picked up a y drift and the y = 150 row left the screen at
  about y +440; give a pad ruler two rows (or a grid) when the push
  direction is not certain.
- **A dark decoration is invisible to `ruler.mjs` (wave 46 JC):** spöb
  143's dark-red planet art stays under the luma-60 blob threshold; read
  such an anchor off a frame grab. Ruler moons 400 px apart ALIAS in the
  trackers (a moon "moving the wrong way"): pin the place with the anchor
  or the radar (about 31.5 px per radar px: Bravo's 400 px moons are 12.5-13
  radar px apart).
- **Fire at a coasting NPC while it cruises (wave 46 `kc_a`):** wave 25's
  near-18 radar px trigger caught the AI 1 trader 470 px out and nearly at
  rest (creeping to the port at 7-8 px/s at 9 radar px too); a coast reading
  wants a trader on a lane, not one arriving at the port.
- **The capture odds shown are not what the rig gets (waves 45-46):** at a
  shown 75%, seven Capture Ship attempts gave 3 captures, 3
  "unsuccessful" and 1 security self-destruct; budget two or three attempts
  per capture.
- **Stopping a queue that is still waiting (wave 46):** `pgrep -f q2.sh`
  finds the zsh wrapper AND the bash; kill both, then restart the queue
  with the change (never edit it in place).

- **A live mission's ship cannot be boarded at all (wave 45 `cu_a`):** a
  ShipGoal -1 / ShipBehav -1 mission prize answered every press "You can't
  board this ship." (wave 3's rule, easy to forget). For a capture rig use
  wave 11's protector (ShipBehav 1, ShipGoal 3): disabling it fails the
  mission ("Mission failed.") and leaves an ordinary hulk that boards and
  captures (`scenarios/w45_capture_use.json`).
- **The player's turret did not disable a protector (wave 45 `cu_b`):** seven
  Kit Escort Gun taps left the ShipBehav-1 prize at "No Shields", not
  Disabled (whether the turret held fire at a friendly target or missed
  was not read). Disable allies with the Kit Blast Bomb through
  `loops/disable.mjs`, as wave 11 did.
- **Stopping a run inside the board loop (wave 45 `cu_b`):** SIGTERM is only
  handled when the loop's synchronous ssh call returns (it did not within
  a minute); SIGKILL the run's node process, then `novaref recover`
  (it stopped EV Nova, moved the plug-in and the recording out, restored
  Last Pilot; Matt matched the backup). Stop the waiting queue first, or it
  starts its next run on the run's "exit".
- **A hull parked on a planet defeats the frame readers (wave 45 T):** the
  white-spoke heading (`tools/headings.mjs`) and `analysis/bolt_births.mjs`
  miss over cloud pixels (bolts born over the planet were not detected
  for a whole pass). Read the heading on zoomed frames (or off a quadrant
  gun's straight shots) and check every "held fire" pass on a frame sheet;
  better, start such rigs on a decoration.
- **The moon ruler is periodic (wave 45 JC):** moons every 400 px give
  displacements, not the absolute place (grid2d.py needs a start x); put a
  distinct marker on the line (a planet, a different decoration) when the
  absolute distance matters, as for an arrival distance.
- **A copied `mkpilots.mjs` runs the OLD wave's specs (wave 45):** the
  sed-retargeted wave-44 copy rebuilt every wave-44 pilot into `pilots/w44/`
  (the same specs, harmless). Replace `mkpilots.mjs` before running it in a
  new wave's tools.
- **The queue scripts run under /bin/bash 3.2 (wave 45):** no `mapfile`;
  build step arrays with loops.
- **A captured, inertial, slow hull lands with `tools/inertland.mjs`
  (wave 45 `cu_c`):** velocity matching off the planet's shift and `l`
  presses whenever the planet is within 150 px; a plain thrust-and-brake
  walk overshot for 50 steps.
- **A map route needs shift-clicks (wave 44 `jc_a`, `jc_a2`, `jc_b`,
  `jc_b2`):** the map's Find ("f", a name, Return) centres on and selects
  the system but plots NO route, and a plain click on a system three hops
  away does not either ("Clear Route" stays grey, the nav panel "Nav System
  Off", `j` does nothing). Find the end, then shift-click each hop in turn
  (wave 11's way; `{"click":[x,y],"win":true,"mods":"shift"}`) and check
  the nav panel reads "Hyperspace / <first hop>" before timing anything.
- **A sÿst's Visibility is re-read only at a landing (wave 44 `r16_a`,
  `r16_b`):** a system gated on a bit set in flight did not appear on the
  in-flight map; it did after a landing and Leave. A map is no in-flight
  bit reader.
- **The Kit Ion Tick bolts push the ship (wave 44 `e6i20_a`, `e6i5_a`):** a
  hull sitting under the wëap 131 clones drifts off at a growing speed (12
  px/s after a second, about 50 by 16 s), so a still-hull rig under them
  needs a non-pushing ion weapon.
- **board.mjs never stops after a no-dialog board (wave 44 `r16_a`):** a
  special ship's board answers "Target ship has been boarded." with no
  dialog, so the loop kept sweeping (92 sweeps, 13 minutes) with the
  mission already over; give such scenarios `sweep.repeat` 1.
- **Reordering a running queue (wave 44 q2 -> q4):** kill only the queue's
  own bash pid while a run is going (the run and its steps.sh finish), then
  start the new queue gated on that run's `runsh.log` "exit" line; never
  edit the running script.
- **An early recording starts on the title screen (wave 44 U7):** the
  title's 40-odd bright blobs fill the first seconds of a
  `w44_space_early.json` recording; start a decoration track at the first
  in-space frame (`tools/u7sum.sh` finds it) or the tracker locks onto the
  title. A moon decoration's bright-pixel centroid sits about 5 px off its
  centre (its lit side), a constant offset that cancels in speeds.

- **Single-frame steps are no speed reading, even of stellars (wave 43
  `u4a_a`):** at a steady 131 px/s (4.4 px a recording frame) the moon
  rulers' frame-to-frame shift jumped between 1 and 6 whole pixels (the
  30 fps capture beats the game's drawing), exactly like wave 42's star
  clusters. Read speeds as least-squares slopes of a POSITION over 0.5 s or
  more against the mp4's own frame times (`tools/ruler.mjs`: the ship's
  world x from decorations of known place); per-frame shifts only for
  matching.
- **A slow hull may jump before it has turned (wave 43 `u4e_a`):** Kit Probe
  E (Turn 10, Speed 1000) arrived about 30 degrees off the line toward the
  centre and left the ruler; A and D (also Turn 10) arrived aligned. Check
  the arrival track's y before reading a ruler run.
- **The kit përs 1151 is not a live person (wave 43 `r16_a`):** it did not
  appear even from a sÿst Person slot at 100%, where the overridden stock
  përs 225 appeared at once in four runs out of four. A person rig needs a
  stock përs id (override it in a run-only plug-in such as
  `kits/w43_pers225.mjs`) and the Person slot.
- **board.mjs and a far or moving start (wave 43 `r16_b`-`r16_e`):** the
  bracket mode lost the hulk off screen, the radar fallback chased a blip
  2,978 px away, `startOnSilent` swept 118 px out, and `sweep.atPx` 30
  swept where the game said "You're not close enough to board this ship."
  (a 24 px disc boards from about 12 px). Start the loop with the target on
  screen (`tools/r16b.mjs` re-rolls until it is) and sweep at 10 px.
- **`r` selected no tribute defender (wave 43 `tk_e`):** two hostile red
  guards beside the planet and `r` left "No Target", so the turrets never
  fired; Tab took the nearest guard at once (`tk_f`).
- **steps.sh's waitfile accepts a failed first attempt's result.json, again
  (wave 43 `g300_b`):** the open_pilot flake ("panel still open") was
  retried by `run`, but the queue counted the run as finished and started
  the next one, whose `start.sh` cleared the shared inbox while the retry
  still ran (harmless here: the retry had already taken all its steps). Wait
  for the `-retry1` dir's result.json, or check `ok` in the newest
  run-*.json, before moving on.
- **The star field moves in two speed clusters (wave 42 `u4a_c`, `g5f_a`):**
  per-frame star steps in a steady cruise split between about 3.6 and
  about 4.5 px (Probe A), and in an afterburner boost the 3.6 cluster stays
  beside the 9-10 px one, so a 1 s mean of `tools/starshift.mjs` blends
  them and reads low (Probe A's cruise 4.4 then 3.4 within five seconds;
  every afterburner factor of waves 39-42 is biased toward 1). Read the
  per-frame steps' histogram (`tools/u4mode.py`, the g5 tables), or time
  the ship past decoration rulers, before trusting a speed RATIO.
- **A planet bribe offer can be refused outright (wave 42 `r8_t`):** "You
  wish." in the hail's text box and no price popup; the scripted Return then
  only closed the dialog and the whole duration run measured nothing.
  Check the `paid` shot's credits before reading a bribe run.
- **`l` does not fly the ship in from beyond the landing window (wave 42
  `tk_a`, `tk_b`):** after a jump the ship arrives about 1,350 px out; `l`
  then selects the port and is cleared, but a second `l` answers "You're too
  far away to land on this planet." instead of flying there, so a landing after a jump needs the port
  near the arrival point (wave 42's Kit Tribute Land Next port at (-1300,
  0)) or a steered approach. The ship arrives about 5.1 s after `j` (from
  rest) still faster than its top speed: `Down@300` did not stop the Kit
  Tribute Slow ("You're moving too fast to land on this planet."); Down
  held 1.5 s from 5.0 s did, and `l` `l` then landed (`tk_d`).
- **A stock any-system person can answer a kit Tab (wave 42 `r16p_c`):**
  "David Dunham" (Ambrosia) showed up in a sealed kit system and jumped
  out when hailed; a person-driven run must check the target's NAME.
- **The base pilot marks only stock persons alive (wave 42):** its
  personAlive array holds indexes 0-515 (përs 128-643) and 1023 (përs 1151);
  a kit përs at 1151 still never appeared (`r16p_a`), so try an override of
  a stock one (pilot-make has no personAlive edit).
- **A 0x0020 burn comes in spells (wave 42 A13):** read a rating's effect
  over a minute or more per run; a 20 s window can land in a burn or a lull.


- **The play area is x 0-639, the player at (318, 302) (wave 41 `r17_a`,
  `r17c_a`):** the HUD starts at x 640, so a click aimed at a stellar
  300 px east of the player, (716, 302), hit the HUD and selected nothing;
  `l` then took the nearest stellar. Clicking a stellar in the play area
  selects it for `l` (Stellar Navigation shows it, blue brackets).
- **Deionize 0 is not "no drain" (wave 41 `e6_a`):** a Deionize-0 hull
  shed each 20-point ion hit within about a second and was never tinted;
  use Deionize 1 for a charge that holds.
- **An AI's turret reload is not its Reload (wave 41 E6):** the Ion Tick
  Target (Reload 60) hit every 108-111 recorded frames (3.6 s); time hits
  off the recording.
- **`tools/radarseries.mjs` assumes 30 fps** (its time column is frame /
  30): on a 10 fps recording (`w41_space_early10.json`) use
  `tools/a11.mjs <dir> 10`.
- **Read a beam's or a gravity swing's speed on BOTH axes (wave 41 `g5_a`,
  `g10_a`):** wave 40's "damped" Gravity-10 swing was its x component
  turning into y; the speed itself did not fall.
- **Only the first bay launch of a run reads clean (wave 41 `e8_b`):**
  `tools/greendisc.mjs` takes one centroid of all green pixels, so later
  launches mix with the fighters already out.
- **A lost connection hangs a run with the lock held (wave 41
  `a6i50_a`):** at 11:05 the MacBook left the network that may reach the
  NovaRef VLAN (it came back on 192.168.0.x, not 192.168.1.199); the run's
  ssh call hung for 4 h 40 min holding the lock, so every later queued run
  printed "START FAILED" after its lock-wait. Kill the run's own ssh child
  to let it exit, then `novaref recover` once `status` answers again.
- **A scenario's queue file must not be edited while bash runs it:** bash
  reads a script as it goes; to reorder queued runs, stop the waiting
  queue (TaskStop) and start it again (wave 41 restarted q3-q6 twice).

- **A return jump must be pressed within about a second of the arrival
  (wave 40 `tsl_a`, `tsl_b`):** the ship arrives about 1,350 px out flying
  inward at top speed, so after about 1 s it is inside the 1,000 px zone and
  `j` answers "Can't initiate hyperspace jump - not yet far enough away
  from system center." Even 1.1 s in one keys step was too late; turn
  away or fly out before jumping back.
- **A player's fighter bay is a SECONDARY (wave 40 `e8_a`):** without `w`
  first, `down:ctrl` launches nothing and the panel reads "No Secondary
  Weapon".
- **A Kit Ring hull parked on a planet fools `tools/headings.mjs` (wave 40
  `e2_a`, `u8r_a`):** the light test picks up the planet's clouds (the
  heading jumped by 100 deg between frames). Take the heading from a drift
  (Up from rest, the star shift's direction), a fixed beam, or zoomed
  frames.
- **`run` does not retry an open_pilot failure (wave 40 `tst0_a`):** "could
  not open pilot ... (panel still open; cancelled)" ends the run (start.sh
  prints START FAILED); rerun it.
- **Radar blip counts miss ships parked next to the player (wave 40
  `a11n_a`):** `tools/radarseries.mjs` drops the player's own dot, and
  ships beside him merge with it (0 blips while two traders sat on screen
  for five minutes). Check the play area too.
- **Beam Count is not 1/30 s on this machine (wave 40 E10):** a Count-30
  beam showed for 16 recorded frames (0.53 s); time beams in recorded
  frames, not from the field.
- **A hold's length does not set a heading (wave 40 `u8r2_a`, `u8r3_a`):**
  `Left@6200` on the Turn-10 hull (29 deg/s, so 180 deg) left it at about
  350 deg, `Left@3100` at about 200 deg, from an Enter Ship heading that
  need not be the 90 deg of `u8r_a`; read the heading off the recording.

- **A novaref pilot holds 0 defence ships for every KIT stellar (wave
  39):** the pilot file keeps each stellar's defence ships LEFT
  (`stellarShipCount`), filled from DefCount only when the game creates a
  pilot; the base pilot predates the kit, so every kit planet reads "fleet
  destroyed" and a 12,800 tribute demand is accepted at once. Wave 38's
  whole R18 section measured that case. Set `"stellarShipCount"` in the
  pilot spec (pilot-make, README "Custom pilots"). Other per-stellar pilot
  state (destroyed stellars, persons alive) is the base's too: check it
  before trusting a kit rig that depends on it.
- **A dominated planet zeroes its count, so a pilot with "dominated" set
  needs no count (wave 39 `payB_a`).**
- **Return on a price popup ACCEPTS the price (wave 39 `k5p_a`):** a
  script that "closes" a hail with Return while a bribe or mercy price is
  up pays it (1.00M -> 997,000); close with Close Channel's click.
- **An ionized Kit Ring hull is redrawn blue with a VIOLET spoke (wave
  39):** `analysis/pointer.mjs`'s white test reads nothing (or the
  exhaust); use `tools/headings.mjs` with `SPOKE=violet` / `vw`. Its ring
  flickers teal while ionized, far from any ion gun too (`e6f_b`: 50 s
  after leaving it), so the flicker is not a hit marker.
- **Radar ship dots are single grey pixels that blink (wave 39 `a11_a`):**
  a per-frame count drops to 0 every other sample; take the maximum over
  a few seconds. Stellars are grey too (bigger). Ships out of the radar's
  reach (about 1,600 px) vanish like departures.
- **The star field's shift steps in whole pixels at 30 fps (wave 39
  `u4_a`):** per-frame readings scatter by a third; average the shift
  VECTOR over 1 s windows (about ±0.3 px a frame).
- **zsh does not word-split `set -- $r` (wave 39):** a `for r in "a b"`
  loop that splits with `set --` passed one argument and the tool read
  nothing; pass the numbers explicitly.
- **A stock bounty hunter can show up in a kit system for a pilot with a
  bad record (wave 39 `fr_a`):** Tab met a "Pirate Enterprize (Bounty
  Hunter)" in wave 31's freighter rig (record -50); a driver that Tabs
  "to a freighter" must check the target panel's name.

- **A gövt 0x1000 | 0x0004 warship is never hostile to the player (wave
  38 `a9_a`, wave 37's three runs):** it comes up with yellow brackets and
  leaves. Every stock pirate govt is xenophobic (0x0001, Pirate 137 is
  0xf2b3); make a plunder rig 0x1000 | 0x0001 (or use gövt 137) and place
  the pirate by a mission on the player's port.
- **The player's weapons are locked once `j` is pressed (wave 38
  `u8_d1` / `u8_d2`):** a self-disable cannot cut a jump short; an NPC's
  disabling hit can (time `j` about 1 s before the disable: `tools/a9j.sh`).
- **zsh aborts a wait loop on an unmatched glob (wave 38):** `until [ -n
  "$(ls -d $E/sub/2*/)" ]` printed "no matches found" every pass and never
  ended; use `find $E/sub -maxdepth 1 -name '2*'`.
- **On a dominated planet the hail's second button is Release (wave 38
  `t25600_a`):** `tools/tribute.sh`'s second demand clicked it and freed the
  planet ("You release the planet from its debt to you."); read the button
  before clicking (246,382) twice.
- **A run can fail before Enter Ship with "could not open pilot ... (panel
  still open; cancelled)" (wave 38 `b25600_a`):** no retry is made for it;
  the queue moves on, so check each subdir's `run-*.json` for `"ok":false`.
- **R13 draws belong to the system visit (wave 24), so each Enter Ship is
  one sample set:** a BBS of eight missions with `<DST> (<DSY>)` in their
  NAMES reads eight draws off one shot of the list.
- **A mobile ship you bribe LEAVES (wave 37):** three bribed AI 3
  warships were entering hyperspace 13-23 s after Accept, so a watch of a
  bribe's life needs a ship that cannot leave (wave 37's anchored Kit
  Bribe Warship, sÿst 1384). A hail with no target does nothing (no
  dialog, no line), so a script that keeps hailing a ship that has gone
  just takes empty shots.
- **Tab never targets the player's hired escorts (wave 37 `r12_a`):**
  seven Tabs among six hired escorts in empty Kit Range gave no target
  and no hail; read wages from the credits across a day (or click an
  escort to target it, as wave 23 did).
- **`ctrl@120` does not fire the secondary (wave 37 `r6_bay`):** the
  Kit Fighter Bay stayed at 2 after two `ctrl@120` taps; `down:ctrl wait
  200 up:ctrl` (wave 7's form) launched both. Launched bay fighters fly
  formation and leave a non-hostile target alone until ordered (`f`).
- **A kit traffic system can stay EMPTY (wave 37 `a9_a` / `a9_b`):** Kit
  Pirate Plunder Range (one AI 3 düde of a gövt 0x1000 | 0x0004, avgShips
  1, then 2) showed no ship at all in two 4.5-minute runs, while the
  same rig with a 0x0004-only govt had its pirate at Enter Ship. Check
  the first Tab census before a long watch, and stop the run when it is
  empty.
- **An NPC never fired a one-frame beam turret with Reload 30000 (wave
  37 `a9_p`):** the Kit Pirate (AI 3, hostile, red brackets) circled the
  player for 4.5 minutes without a shot; wave 13's Kit Disabler BOLT
  (reload 30000) does fire. Give NPCs bolts for one-shot rigs.
- **`hunt.sh` can report "finished" for a run that is still in its
  retry (wave 37 `hunt_m200_10_b`):** after the Enter Ship flake, the
  failed first attempt's directory satisfies `waitfile.mjs`; the next
  queued run then waits on the lock, harmlessly, but read the `-retry1`
  directory for the results.
- **A clearance-lapse edge moves from run to run (wave 36):** wave 35's
  250 px planet rig landed at 24.617 / 24.649 s on its evening and lapsed
  at every interval down to 24.356 s on wave 36's; tonight's rigs spread
  24.18-24.54 s. Run a CONTROL rig in the same session as any comparison
  of lapse times, and never read a difference under about 0.3 s between
  two sessions as a property of the stellar.
- **`hitat.mjs`'s far mode fires 2.5 s after the shot it judged (wave 36
  `tr560`):** a mobile victim read at 19.7 radar px (about 570 px) was
  about 360-450 px off at the press. Read the hit distance from the
  recording at the press's frame (+4), not from the hit log.
- **`linesheet.sh`'s default thresholds (lit 90, 8 frames) missed "Sensors
  detect ..." in several wave-36 hunts:** `tools/huntsum.sh` runs it at
  lit 30 / 4 frames and prints the census times beside it.
- **The Kit Hulk (wave 7's slow-pass target, sÿst 2020) carries NO
  credits:** its Credits button is grey ("None"); take Energy (or Cargo)
  when a board must take something.
- **An unarmed AI 3 hull of an always-hostile govt (0x0004) never closes
  on the player (wave 36 `coast_raid_a`):** it stayed beyond the radar for
  150 s; give an attacker a harmless gun.
- **macOS has no `timeout`, and a zsh glob with no match aborts the whole
  command (wave 36 setup):** `rm q*.sh` with no q*.sh left the copied
  tools' old queue scripts in place until rerun under `bash -c 'shopt -s
  nullglob; ...'`.

- **A press interval inside one keys step is the wait plus about 150 ms
  (wave 35 `lapse_*`):** "l wait 24650 l" put the presses 24.80 s apart,
  "wait 24380" 24.53 s; read the intervals from `recording.events.json`
  (the `press` events' `video_t`, `tools/lapsesum.sh`) and request
  about 0.15 s less than the interval wanted.
- **A record-hostile warship need not be hostile at Enter Ship (wave 35
  `r7_after`):** on `w22_bribe_plain_100m` (record -50) the targeted Kit
  Bribe Warship answered seven hails over 2.5 minutes with "What is it?" /
  Greetings / Request Assistance (no Beg For Mercy) and was hostile on the
  eighth; the next run on the same pilot was fired on at once, as every
  wave-33 run. Check the first hail for Beg For Mercy and re-hail (or wait)
  before counting pleas.
- **NPC-fight compositions drift (wave 35 R19):** AI 3 traffic leaves and
  arrives within a minute or two, so a call 60-130 s into a watch cannot
  be tied to the first census's ships. Record from before Enter Ship
  (`scenarios/w35_space_early.json`) and read only calls in the first
  seconds; small traffic (avgShips 2) gives one ship of each side about
  half the time.
- **A shield that recharges 30 points a frame hides the fight (wave 35):**
  the Full hunters and preys read 100% throughout, so a no-call watch
  cannot show that they fought; the Weak twin (a 10-point shield, "Shields
  Down" once hit) can.
- **A system-placed fleet (DudeTypes -id) gives a fixed side but may change
  the call (wave 35 packs):** three hunters as a flët never called, which
  fits the summed odds but also "a fleet member does not call"; use single
  ships when the caller matters.
- **One subdir per run (wave 35 round 1):** `r19q35.sh` run twice without
  a SUFFIX put two attempt dirs in each subdir and overwrote the first
  run's `.ask.log` / `.drive.log`; the sheets take the LAST attempt dir.

- **Copy the interactive SCENARIO with the tools, not only the tools
  (wave 34):** `w33_space_interactive.json` names its own inbox
  (`inbox/w33.jsonl`), so wave 34's retargeted drivers waited on
  `w34.jsonl` while the run listened on the old one (no step ever ran).
  Each wave needs its own `wNN_space_interactive.json` with its inbox.
- **Stopping a driver's shell task kills the novaref run under it (wave
  34):** the game stayed up with the kit installed; `novaref recover`
  cleaned it (EV Nova stopped, plug-in out, Last Pilot and prefs back).
  End a hung interactive run with `{"done":true}` in ITS inbox instead.
- **A landing (take-off) advances the date one day (wave 34
  `huntday_b1`):** the pulled pilot went from June 23rd to 24th and the
  status line said "Departing ... on June 24th"; "the same day" cannot be
  reached by landing and taking off, and a call after a re-landing is the
  next day's.
- **An R19 call can come before the recording starts (wave 34
  `hunt_s15` .. `hunt_s40`):** an NPC fight already on at Enter Ship
  called the fleet within the 4 s before `record start`, so the "Sensors
  detect" line was missing or caught at 0.4 s; the fleet ("Kit RF Lead",
  "Kit RF Guard") in the first Tab census is the reading.
- **A retried run leaves two attempt dirs (wave 34 `hunt_s40`):** `ls -d
  <sub>/2*/` returns both (the failed one first); take `| tail -1`, as
  `capsum.sh` does.
- **zsh does not split an unquoted `$R`:** a run list kept in one variable
  reached `capsum.sh` as one argument; pass the names literally (or use an
  array).
- **`restsum.mjs`'s landed test misreads a dark station spaceport (wave
  34 S100):** its picture area lit only 20%; the status line (no "too
  far") and the shot settle it.
- **A decoration clipped at the play area's edge needs its edge, not its
  centroid (wave 34 walk-out):** `moonx.mjs` put the half-hidden moon at
  310 (the visible half's centroid); `tools/moonedge.mjs` (a y window, the
  left edge plus the vertical radius) reads it, about 2.6 px high against
  an unclipped centroid.
- **`move.mjs`'s heading is good to a few degrees, so a coast must start
  close (wave 34 `worm_toward`):** 5.8 degrees over 1,100 px put the ship
  280 px wide of the wormhole; start a coasting rig within about 300 px.
- **A stock përs can join kit traffic after a take-off (wave 34
  `huntday_b1`):** "Matt Burch / 31337 / ATMOS" showed in a Tab census of
  Kit Reinf Hunt B; read census names, not counts.

- **gövt MaxOdds gates NPC-vs-NPC fights too (wave 33, wave 32 re-read):**
  wave 32's Strength-10 hunters (MaxOdds 100) never engaged Strength-500
  preys; with the odds in their favour (Strength 100 vs 1) they attacked at
  once, and armed Strength-500 preys attacked Strength-10 hunters. Size an
  NPC-vs-NPC rig's Strengths for the side that must start the fight.
- **A driver must check that its run STARTED (wave 33 `plea_war`):** a
  wrong pilot path failed the run at once, but `plea.sh` went on sending
  steps into an inbox nobody read (ask.mjs waits 180 s per step), and the
  queue's next run then started behind it. `plea.sh` now stops unless
  `start.sh` printed a line starting "ready" (waitready's failure line is
  "not ready", so grep for "^ready").
- **A window shot can hang for minutes (wave 33 `plea_hails`):** one shot
  step took 9 minutes and failed (the ssh round trip was 2.7 s right
  after); the driver found no file, skipped its Lower Price, and its later
  clicks fell on the open popup. Check that each shot a branch reads
  exists, and stop the run when one is missing.
- **ask.mjs gives up on a step after 180 s:** one `keys` step longer than
  that (a cascade of lapsed clearances) needs `ASK_TIMEOUT` (ms;
  `oneshot.sh` sets 600000), or the driver moves on while the step still
  runs and its `done` never reaches the inbox.
- **The Capture Ship click can trip the self-destruct (wave 33):** "Oops!
  You tripped this ship's security self-destruct mechanism." answered a
  capture attempt, like a plunder take; a capture run is one reading per
  board.

- **Time a press interval inside ONE keys step (wave 32):** the ask
  round trip between two hand-driven steps (a shot, scp, the inbox poll)
  added 4.4 s in one run and 5.5 s in the next, so `lapse.sh`'s targets
  came out a second off; `tools/oneshot.sh` sends "l wait W l wait W2 ..."
  as one step (intervals exact to a frame) and the outcome is read from
  the recording afterwards. `l` in the spaceport does nothing, so a
  cascade may run past its landing.
- **Read what an Ammo take delivered on the secondary panel (wave 32):**
  `w` and a window shot before and after the board ("IR Missile - 0" /
  "- 10") answers it in flight; no re-landing or pilot pull needed.
- **A two-düde traffic mix can draw none of one (wave 32 `hunt1`):** at
  50 / 50 and avgShips 4 the census found four preys and no hunter. Read
  the Tab census before the watch, and weight the düde you need.
- **Two kit govts listing each other as Enemies did not fight (wave 32
  `hunt2` / `hunt3`):** AI 3 hunters left AI 1 and AI 3 preys at 100%
  shield for three minutes in three runs. Do not build an NPC-vs-NPC rig
  on gövt Enemies alone.
- **Copied tools carry the older wave's queue scripts (wave 32):** the
  retargeted wave-31 `q2.sh` was started by mistake and spun forever on a
  `batch1.log` that this wave never wrote (killed). Delete the old `q*.sh`
  / `batch*.sh` after copying a wave's `tools/`.
- **A provoked freighter's target is dropped when it turns hostile, and a
  long hold can lose it (wave 32 `freight2`):** `freight.sh`'s six 3 s
  holds ended on No Target; Tab to a yellow (neutral) freighter, ONE
  1.5 s hold, then hail.

- **U9's 212 px landing cap is superseded (wave 31):** at rest a 250 px
  planet cleared at 230 / 245 px and LANDED on the next press, and a
  cleared ship that backed away landed from 294, 359 and 425 px (1.7 W, no
  cap). Wave 6 stepped IN from outside with a request made long before, so
  its readings near 210-235 px mixed the clearance's time lapse (13-25 s)
  and the 249 px automatic clearance with the window; the "cap" was never
  the window. Measure a landing window only with a ship cleared seconds
  earlier.
- **Turn BEFORE the clearing press (wave 31 `walk_1500`):** `move.mjs`
  took about 20 s to turn the Ring Crawler, so the press after the walk
  came 25-27 s after the clearance and met a lapsed one (a fresh request).
  `tools/walkout2.sh` turns first (`NO_THRUST=1`), then clears and walks
  (l1 -> l2 under 14 s). `move.mjs` now takes `TOL` (the sprite reads in 10
  degree steps, so 173.4 for a 180 target failed the old fixed 6).
- **The board loop's `-dialog-<label>-` shot is taken AFTER that click:**
  with an Abort-only `dialogClicks` the dialog is already gone in it. Read
  the dialog (Capture Odds) from the shot before it (`tools/odds.sh`).
- **"No Secondary Weapon" does not mean the launcher is missing:** it shows
  until a secondary is selected (`w`); the pulled wave-31 Ammo pilots held
  wëap 289 with its outfit and rounds all along.
- **A run's open_pilot failure (1 in about 40 in wave 31) now stops the
  driver at once:** `tools/waitready.mjs` also reads the run's
  `run-*.json` for `{"ok":false}`; rerun the cell under a new subdir.
- **`pilot-after` is the pushed copy unless the scenario lands again:**
  a pilot is written when the player leaves a spaceport, so a plunder run
  that ends in flight cannot show what a take delivered (wave 30's "the
  pulled pilot still held 0 rounds" read nothing). Land and take off
  before the pull when the hold matters.
- **The kit's self-fed launcher (wëap 289, MaxAmmo 5, no ammo outfit) is
  not plunderable ammo:** the dialog lists its rounds as a bare "5" and the
  Ammo button does nothing; a stock pair (IR Missile, wëap 134 + oütf 134 /
  135) lists "10 IR missiles" and the take works.

- **Two driver scripts can feed one run (wave 30 `gate_diag180`):**
  `tools/waitready.mjs` only sees a failure that reaches `run.err`, but a
  run's `{"ok":false}` line goes to `run-*.json`, so after a failed launch
  it kept polling its full 400 s; when the rerun's inbox said ready, BOTH
  scripts sent their steps into it (every step twice, two `l` before the
  first shot). Never start a second batch while an earlier driver may
  still be waiting; read a doubled run from the recording.
- **The spöb Type picks a stellar's art (wave 30 `gate_small140`):** a
  kit stellar cloned from one spöb but given another's Type (the kit's
  `gate()` sets Type 1) draws spïn 2000 + Type, not the clone's art. Keep
  the clone's Type to keep its graphic.
- **The idle gate is drawn under the ship you start on (wave 30, wave 24
  re-read):** a pilot started ON a gate sees the closed gate's grey
  sprite at the centre, easily taken for the ship. Start gate rigs on a
  decoration stellar beside the gate.
- **A launch can stay on the Ambrosia splash past the Open Pilot wait
  (wave 30, 1 of 39 runs: "Open Pilot panel did not appear"), and two
  more runs flaked ("open panel closed unexpectedly", "exited after Enter
  Ship"; `run`'s retry ran both):** rerun the first by hand.
- **`move.mjs` (wave 30) turns the Kit Ring Lancer to a heading from its
  nose spoke in two or three window shots (to within 4 degrees: it reads
  in 10-degree sprite steps), even over a moon decoration; `Up@120` then
  coasts it at about 1.65 px a frame (49 px/s).** Decoration "rulers" (moon
  sprites at known positions, off the ship's path) give the ship's world
  position in any recording frame (`tools/navsel.mjs`).
- **An Ammo take with a matching 0-round launcher took nothing (wave 30
  `pd_ammo_1`):** the dialog listed "Ammo: 5" with the button lit, the
  click at (510, 325) changed nothing and printed nothing, and the pulled
  pilot still had 0 rounds. The rig needs a different launcher setup (an
  outfit-installed launcher? ammo the player can buy?) before the Ammo
  odds can be read.

- **The R7 refusal detector (`tools/freshrefuse.sh`, wave 30):** a priced
  offer lights the popup's red Lower Price button (159 red pixels in x
  360-470, y 296-306 of a window shot), a refusal none; use it to hunt a
  fresh refusal by runs (one first Offer a run, about 1 minute each).

- **A mission ship with ShipStart -2 sits EXACTLY on nav default 2 (wave
  29):** dx 170.0 / 189.9 / 209.9 / 230.0, dy 0.2-0.4 from a player on nav
  default 1, so a port at (0, 0) and a marker at (d, 0) put a target at a
  chosen distance, off screen too (the Kit Blast rig). Land, accept
  (Return = Yes), take off (Return = Leave): the player sits at rest on the
  port.
- **A window shot can miss a fresh status line (wave 28's gate_near, read
  in wave 29):** "Hypergate jump cancelled." was on screen in the
  recording after every cancel but missing in three of the six shots
  taken 1.2 s after the click. Read status lines from the recording (frames
  after the event's stamp) before calling a line absent.
- **The Kit Ring Lancer (497) is INERTIAL (wave 29 `bribe_stay`):** Down
  does not brake it; two hand-steered approaches to a port 300 px away
  overshot by hundreds of px, and `tools/steerland.mjs` locked onto the
  wrong planet with two on screen. To land at a second port, start the
  pilot ON it instead. Clicking a stellar in the play area selects it.
- **`j` near the planets does nothing (wave 29, as wave 28's
  `rank_picky`):** after `\` the first `j` about 400 px from the ports did
  nothing; 2.5 s of thrust further out it jumped.
- **A decoration stellar (spöb flags 0) is a clean start point (wave 29):**
  Enter Ship puts the player on it, `l` never selects it, it is not drawn
  under the ship (only a 2 x 2 radar dot), so `l` reaches only the stellar
  under test.
- **Write a run's time from its directory name, not from memory (wave
  29):** the first NOTES lines carried guessed times 20 minutes off (runs
  take about two minutes, not four); `ls -d */2026*` gives them.

- **A ship explosion's reach is a SQUARE (wave 28):** read a hit or a
  miss by max(|dx|, |dy|) from the wreck, not by distance (a 100 t wreck hit
  at 72 px and missed at 62). The `w28_death_at*` scenarios use the board
  loop's `fire.atPx` as a kill distance, but the loop fires at its FIRST
  stop inside it (asked 82, fired at 62) and then sweeps 70 presses at
  nothing (about 4 minutes a run): read the real distance with
  `tools/killdist.sh`, and lower `sweep.presses` for such runs.
- **`l` far from a hypergate selects nothing (wave 28 `gate_far`):** start
  gate-request tests on the gate or within about 250 px of it.
- **A withdrawn planet bribe poisons the rest of the visit (wave 28
  `prefuse_2m`):** after "No deal, cheapskate." every later Offer Bribe was
  refused or insulted, so only the FIRST offer of a flight is a reading of
  the refusal odds; repeat by runs, not by hails.
- **`j` right after takeoff, or after a landing, does nothing (wave 28
  `rank_picky`):** a ship next to the planet cannot jump, and a landing
  clears the hyperspace destination (re-pick it on the map).
- **One open_pilot died on "This pilot file appears to reference
  information that is from a plug-in ... not currently loaded" (wave 28
  `death_far300`, then fine on the rerun), one launch on "no EV Nova window
  within 30 s" (`gate_deny`, the retry ran), and one run flaked at Enter
  Ship (`death_far1000`, retried by `run`):** three flakes in sixteen runs;
  rerun.
- **A run's `run-*.json` lands a moment before its `result.json` (wave
  28):** a waiter that saw the first and not the second timed out once;
  wait on `result.json` (`tools/waitfile.mjs`).

- **An unexplored gate destination's ring hides under the arrowhead (wave
  27; wave 25 misread it):** it is a small (about 8 px) #424242 ring, darker than the
  lane and covered by the cyan head, and wave 25's click landed 54 px
  short of it. Compute where a destination sits from the sÿst
  coordinates (about 1.78 window px a map unit at the gate map's default
  zoom, the current system at (354, 264)) and click there; read the
  colour with a box histogram (`tools/pix.mjs`), not by eye.
- **Two kit systems at one map position read as one dot (wave 27):** Kit
  Map Permit first sat on wave 26's Kit Board Heavy Quick (-760,-1800),
  and its "<Unknown>" info and dark ring were the other system's. Run the
  kit comment's position check before using a new map row.
- **A live AI 4 hulk is not always on the radar at Enter Ship (wave 27):**
  `loops/board.mjs` failed "target not found" in 2 of 13 plunder runs
  (pd_500, pd_100: nothing but the port on the radar). A rerun found it.
- **The plunder blast is exact and repeatable (wave 27):** six repeats
  landed on the same bar pixel, so one tripped run per mass is a
  reading. Click Cargo first (the likeliest trip); a run whose three
  takes all pass is a lost reading (1 of 13 here).
- **`w20_fuel_m20` (record -20) is hostile to every Kit Assist ship (wave
  27 repeated wave 20's run by mistake):** -20 is below their govt's
  CrimeTol 10, so they answer Beg For Mercy refusals, not fuel asks. Use
  records from -1 to -9 for mood readings.
- **Tools copied from an older wave's evidence keep that wave's scenario
  and inbox (wave 27):** `bribe.sh` / `fuelrun.sh` started
  `w23_space_interactive.json` (inbox `w23.jsonl`) while `ask.mjs` wrote
  `w27.jsonl`; sed every `w2N_space_interactive` to the current wave's
  before the first run.
- **`bribe.sh` with fewer warships than its count (wave 27 `bribe_200m`):**
  a Tab past the last ship gives No Target and the next `y` hails the
  nav-target planet again, which answers the repeated offer as an insult
  ("We don't take kindly to insults."). Count the ships first.
- **A stock pilot started AT a Nil'kemorya stellar is dead before the
  first shot (wave 26):** with the game-made base's records (-5, CrimeTol
  1: hostile) the stellar's wëap 199 (Strength 4000) killed the Shuttle
  within 4 s of Enter Ship, and the title screen read "novaref-scenario
  has been killed" (three runs, first blamed on `exploreAll` and on a
  stellar listed in two systems). Start a stock pilot next to hostile
  space, not in it.
- **gövt Flags 0x0008 through an ATTRIBUTES InherentGovt (1xxx) does not
  stop the player's shots (wave 26 `fleetpass`):** the bolt disabled the
  escort that carried it. Use the ship's own (fleet / düde) govt.
- **Kit "slow escorts" (Speed / Accel 40) did not trail their lead (wave
  26 `fleetslow`):** the three hulls arrived and sat stacked.
- **A derelict placed by system traffic can sit about 3,000 px out**
  (wave 26 `pd_ptr`): `loops/board.mjs` dead-reckoned toward a radar arrow
  for 15 legs and the run timed out. Use the live AI 4 hulks (wave 8's
  kind; the player disables them), which have always been near.
- **The player's shield / armor bars are 148 px (x 673-820, rows 201 /
  219 of a window shot):** `tools/bars.mjs` and `droptime.sh` (wave-26
  evidence) read them; give the boarder 100 shield so a point is 1.5 px.
- **A Disable Gun bolt misses a moving target (wave 26 `coastfast`):** the
  turret does not lead; use the Kit Pulse Beam (instant) on anything
  faster than about 50 px/s. A trader met near its port is already slowing
  to land (`coastfast2` caught it at about 10 px/s).
- **`analysis/radar_blips.mjs` prints `t` as frame / 30:** on a 10 fps
  recording read the time as frame / 10. The fleet's ships show on the
  radar as GREY dots here (neutral and hostile alike in these runs), and
  the back-to-centre arrow is a static grey blip of about 28 px with its
  head at x -46..-49: filter both out.
- **A mission ship with ShipBehav 0 calls the fleet before the player
  does anything (wave 26 `farm3`):** an R19 rig that wants the call at a
  chosen moment must not use an attacking ship of the fleet's side.

- **A plunder take can trip the self-destruct whatever the item (wave
  25):** Cargo about 5 times in 6. Take the item you need to read first,
  and plan one board per reading.
- **`tools/takes.mjs` (wave 25) counts any white in the status line as
  text:** a planet behind the status line read as "+TEXT" twice; check
  the flagged shots by eye.
- **A Disable Gun shot at a fleet parked on the player hits an ESCORT
  first** (wave 25 `fleetlead`): the bolt meets the first hull on its
  line, and the whole fleet turns hostile. `tools/fireapproach.mjs` waits
  for a clear line, but the fleet parks about 20 px out and leaves faster
  than 2-second shots can catch; a rig that holds the lead apart (a slow
  lead, or escorts that trail far behind) is needed.
- **The lead's target is dropped between visits** (wave 25 `fleetlead2`):
  read the target panel's name before every shot (`fireapproach.mjs` now
  re-Tabs).
- **A `pgrep -f` waiter matched its own pattern again** (wave 25: three
  waiters spun for 10 minutes after the plunder runs had ended). Wait on a
  file (the run's `result.json`, a `finished` line in a log), not on
  `pgrep`.
- **Start ON a wormhole to read its lines, but MOVE before the first
  `l`** (wave 25): the first `l` acts at once (too far / too fast /
  transit), unlike a hypergate's first `l`, which is the clearance.
- **Mission ships on Kit Reinf Far M's port do not stay there** (wave 25
  `farm`): 8 s after take-off the Kit RV Guard S50 was already off the
  radar.

- **A usable kit hypergate (wave 24):** clone stock spöb 1400 and set govt
  -1, MinStatus -32767, Flags2 0x1000 (stock gates are MinStatus 32767,
  which is what "Hypergate usage denied." answers). `l` targets it
  ("cleared for hypergate entry"), the second `l` opens the gate map. The
  map opens zoomed in: its `-` button (window 537,541) zooms out. Done with
  no pick lifts off at the gate; after a transit the far gate is off
  screen, so start a separate pilot on each gate rather than flying back.
- **The Kit Lancer's heading cannot be read off its sprite** (wave 24: a
  "turn east, thrust" took it away from the port). Use the Kit Ring
  Lancer (pointer sprite) for anything that steers; `tools/steerland.mjs`
  lands after a jump with it in about 8 steps.
- **One Kit Disable Gun hit disables a 3000 / 3000 kit hull; a second
  kills it (wave 24).** Fire ONE shot and read the panel ("Disabled")
  before another.
- **A taken plunder can destroy the hulk** ("Oops! You tripped this
  ship's security self-destruct mechanism.", wave 24): take the plunder
  last, after every reading that needs the hulk.
- **A fleet that parked on the port at the player is gone from the
  turret within about 1 s of moving off (wave 24):** fire while it is
  parked or approaching, and re-Tab (`tools/tablead.mjs`) on each visit:
  the previous visit's target does not carry over.
- **`open_pilot` failed once more** ("panel still open; cancelled", wave
  24 `leaver_fail1`); rerun.

- **`l` on a wormhole goes THROUGH it (wave 23):** a pilot started on a
  wormhole is in the next system after the first `l` ("Passing through a
  wormhole into ..."). Start next to one, not on it, to look at it.
- **WRONG, corrected in wave 25: "Hiring is gated by the spöb TechLevel
  (wave 23)".** A SpecialTech match IS offered for hire, and an empty pool
  keeps Hire Escort live (a popup answers); the greyed button in wave 23's
  TechLevel-9000 runs was the six-escort cap. Kit hulls carry HireRandom 0
  (`shipBase`) unless a block sets it.
- **A map click selects a destination; `j` must be a TAP after the map is
  closed (wave 23):** `down:j wait 1500 up:j` right after closing the map
  did not jump once; `m wait 1200` then `j wait 3000` did, every time. In
  the map, Tab cycles the adjacent systems.
- **`bracketsIn` missed yellow brackets around a yellow disc (wave 23
  `tabcol.mjs`):** read the target panel's name (crop 650,334 170 x 16) or
  a disc colour instead of the brackets when the target sits among discs.
- **A click on a moving fleet ship does not target it** (the ship had
  moved in the ~1 s between shot and click); Tab and read the panel name.
- **The Kit Ring Lancer is CYAN**: a cyan kit disc and the player's ring
  share a colour (126 px ring vs 384 px disc); filter by pixel count.
- **Disabling a neutral ship turns its govt's other warships on the
  player (wave 23):** their hits push an inertialess hull off a boarding
  approach. Board in a system with no other ships of that govt.
- **The bash tool refuses a label named `fc`** (a shell builtin); pick
  another label.

- **`ctrl@120` does not press Control (wave 22):** the bay counter did
  not move; `down:ctrl wait 150 up:ctrl` launches one fighter per press.
- **Nine hired escorts load from a pilot file** (wave 22 `f1c_9`): the
  original flies all nine.
- **An AI 1 / AI 2 victim hit from 700+ px never calls the fleet (wave
  22)**: every reinforcement rig with a trader victim must hit it from the
  screen (wave 21's "slow hulls never call" was this). `tools/hitat.mjs`
  (wave-22 evidence) targets, reads the brackets / white radar blip, steers
  the Kit Ring Lancer toward or away from the victim and fires at a set
  distance.
- **The targeted ship's white radar blip blinks** (absent in every other
  shot, wave 22): a driver must not read one missing blip as "gone".
- **The radar scale (wave 22):** about 29 px a radar px in a kit system
  whose only stellar is at the centre (nine bracket / blip pairs), about 33
  in Kit Reinf Far C (a marker 1,000 px off the port at 30.5 radar px).
- **Traffic in a system whose only port is 3,000 px out hangs 500-1,000
  px from the CENTRE** for 5+ minutes and never visits the port (wave 22
  `farc2`; wave 21 saw the same at 6,000).
- **The Kit Ring Lancer moves about 1 px a ms under thrust**; a tap under
  about 300 ms barely moves it (the Down brake eats it). Legs of 500-1,500
  ms work.
- **gövt Flags vs Flags2 (wave 22):** 0x0008 is "player's shots won't hit"
  in Flags but "no distress messages" in Flags2; the first Kit Quiet Attr
  set the wrong word. Read the Bible's flag list header before using a bit.
- **`j` beside a planet does nothing;** fly a few hundred px off first. A
  jump back into a system arrives off the port's radar (no blip, no arrow
  in one shot): landing after a jump needs a steering driver.
- **A planet's bribe dialog stays up after a Lower Price COUNTER**
  (wave 22 `bribe_plain_20m`, `_1m_rec`): a script that closes the channel
  after one Lower Price leaves it open, and its later clicks press Offer
  Bribe ("We don't take kindly to insults."). `tools/bribe2.sh` presses
  Lower Price twice.
- **AI 1 freighters of a CrimeTol-10 govt stay neutral at record -50**
  (no Beg For Mercy) while its AI 3 warships are hostile: bribe rigs need
  warships.
- **`open_pilot` failed once more** ("panel still open; cancelled", wave 22
  `fuel_rich`); rerun.

- **A port with trade tiers lists stock cargo jobs on its BBS (wave
  21):** Kit Live Port (PORT_FLAGS) listed a stock "Delivery to Earth"
  FIRST, above the kit's DispWeight-30000 jobs, and the first Accept took
  it. Read the selected job's title in a shot before pressing Accept. A
  0x43 port has no Trade Center button at all.
- **The BBS stays open after an accept unless it empties (wave 21)**: a
  driver that expects the board to close after Accept (wave 10's one-job
  case) must shoot it; reopening it shows the landing's frozen list.
- **The radar's reach depends on the system (wave 21):** about 1,600 px
  (18.6 px per radar px) in the kit systems whose only stellar is 6,000 px
  out, about 57 px per radar px in Kit Self Defence (markers at 5,000 /
  -9,000 px), 31.6 in Kit Range. Calibrate it per system from a stellar's
  blip while flying a known leg. With nothing targeted, an arrow at the
  radar's edge points back toward the system's centre when the player is
  far from it; it is NOT a target arrow.
- **Far beam pulses miss (wave 21, again):** two Kit Pulse Beam pulses at
  an AI 4 victim about 1,700 and 3,400 px away left it at 100%. Fly to
  within the screen before the hit.
- **A mission ship of düde 441 (the AI 4 S50 guard, gövt 311) never
  appeared** at ShipStart -1 (offer 940, two builds); other düdes at
  ShipStart -1 work. Untested why; avoid it as a mission ship.
- **AI 1 traffic does not gather at a far port (wave 21):** in a system
  whose only stellar is 6,000 px from the centre the AI 1 and AI 4 traffic
  stayed thousands of px from it for minutes. Rigs that need the victim
  beside a far port need another way to put it there.
- **The novaref `open_pilot` can fail once ("panel still open;
  cancelled", wave 21 `odds150a`):** the run cleans up; just run it again.

- **An anchored hull (Speed 0) is inert to the AI (wave 20):** an anchored
  victim never called reinforcements (four hits, then two victims, the beam
  and the Disable Gun), as wave 17's anchored shooter never fired. Rigs
  that need the victim's AI (calls, flight, fighting back) need Speed > 0;
  Speed 20 / Accel 50 keeps a ship nearly in place and its AI running.
- **An AI 1 victim jumps out about 10 s after the first hit (wave 20),**
  even at Speed 20 (the jump does not use its top speed), and a fleet
  called by a victim that has left never came. **Correction (wave 21):** the
  slow AI 1 S50 never called at all (no distress line, no fleet, even when
  it stayed 60-90 s), so that run shows no cancelled call. Use an AI 4 victim (it
  stays and fights; it does NOT chase the player far from its port) for
  anything that waits more than a few seconds.
- **`r` targets nothing in this install (wave 20):** after Tab had
  targeted the victim `r` left it targeted, and from "No Target" `r`
  selected nothing (the pulses fired at nothing). Use Tab and read the
  panel (`tools/pulse2.mjs` re-Tabs until the panel's name row is lit).
- **Repeated beam pulses at a far victim stop landing (wave 20,
  `odds400`):** the first Kit Pulse Beam pulse hit a victim about 1,300 px
  out; every later one left the shield at 90% and the panel at "No
  Target" after the press. The one-hit design (each run one point) avoids
  it; the hit is the frame the panel's "Shield:" digits change
  (`analysis/panel_hits.mjs --rect 648,424,90,16`).
- **A live interactive run blocks the next one silently (wave 20):** a
  hand-driven run left without `{"done":true}` keeps the lock, and the next
  `run` waits on it (`--lock-wait`); a driver that deletes the inbox first
  must not do it while another run's loop reads it. Append
  `{"done":true}` to the inbox to end it.
- **A waiter loop must not `pgrep -f` its own pattern (wave 20):** `until !
  pgrep -f "onehit.sh"` matched the waiter's own shell command and never
  ended; anchor the pattern (`pgrep -f "^bash onehit.sh"`).
- **The take-off line gives the date (wave 20):** every take-off advances
  the date one day (as wave 19) and the status line says "Taking off from
  ... on June 24th, 1177 NC." / "Blasting off from ..." : read the day off
  the recording without pulling the pilot.
- **A hail sheet needs the record above -CrimeTol (wave 20):** at record
  -20 in a CrimeTol-10 govt's system every AI 4 warship was "Status:
  Hostile" and answered "No way." / "In your dreams, pal." / "You wish.":
  no fuel sale to read.

- **`b` boards the TARGET only, from about 12 px (wave 19):** with no
  target a press does nothing at all; Tab to the hulk first (a disabled one
  has grey brackets: find it with `analysis/brackets.mjs --colour grey`,
  not `pointer.mjs`, which takes the first magenta pointer hull it sees
  when several are on screen). The slow Kit Ring Crawler (818) walked to
  4-8 px with dead-reckoned turns (87.1 deg/s) and thrust (about 46 px/s)
  and boarded at the first or second press, four hulks out of four.
- **Check the spaceport shot before ending a run whose pilot you need
  (wave 19):** in the first A14 take "Cleared to land" at about 170 px was
  followed by an `l` that did not land; the run ended in flight and the
  pulled pilot was the one of the previous take-off (the boarding's records
  were lost; redone).
- **A landing and take-off advances the date one day (wave 19):** the
  pulled pilot went June 23 -> 25 over two take-offs. Anything once a day
  (reinforcement fleets) is re-armed by a relaunch.
- **After a jump the traffic can be out of a turret's reach (wave 19):**
  the Kit Reinf Slow traders were 1,000+ px from the arrival point (the
  Disable Gun reaches 720 px) and fled; a landing and take-off placed them
  beside the port again.
- **`tools/radar.mjs` misses dim blips and sees the radar's target arrow
  (wave 19):** grey blips (116-128) of far ships are sometimes dropped, and
  the off-radar target arrow (a short line) blinks, so it shows up as a
  fixed cluster of "blips" in every other sample. Look at a zoomed radar
  crop before reading blips as ships.
- **The Enter Ship flake can hit twice in one run (wave 19,
  `reinf_weak`: `-retry2`)**; a third would fail the run (`--retries`).
- **A stock BBS job took the Accept again (wave 19, the first
  `ally_disab` take):** "Delivery to Earth" (4 t) above the kit's ränk
  job; the kit job was accepted on a second BBS visit.
- **AI 4 traffic stays (wave 17), which makes it the rig for many hails
  (wave 19):** six neutral AI 4 warships per run, Tab'd in a fixed order
  (`tools/fuelship.sh`, `tools/fuelsheet.sh`).

- **`loops/board.mjs` can lock onto a stray radar blip (wave 18):** with
  the target off screen at the start it took a dim grey blip at the radar's
  top edge (`start: {on: false, blips: [(-20, -88)]}`) and walked toward a
  fixed "2,978 px" (measured null) for ten legs: wave 17's "stalled about
  3,000 px from marker 2102" was this, not the marker's distance. Start a
  board run with the target ON SCREEN (a marker within about 300 px), and
  even then the sweep's last answer can be "not close enough" at 22 px
  from a 24 px hulk (the square range is about half the sprite).
- **The kit's mïsn ids run out at 1127 (wave 18):** use the free ids
  919-959 between the stock missions (128-918) and the kit's 960 (dësc
  4791-4831 for their offer text).
- **The target panel clears when the target turns hostile, so a second
  Space fires untargeted (wave 18, as wave 14):** after the first Kit
  Disable Gun hit the panel read "No Target"; re-target from a Tab census
  (find "Disabled" / the lowered shield) before every further shot.
- **A neutral AI 3 warship of traffic leaves within a minute or two (wave
  18):** hail it the moment Tab finds it; "Unable to send hail - target
  ship is entering hyperspace." means it is already leaving.
- **A stock BBS job can still sit above a kit job (wave 18)**, DispWeight
  30000 notwithstanding: "Delivery to Earth" took the first Accept at Kit
  Self Defence Port. Shoot the BBS before Accept and redo if needed.
- **Starting a run with `&` from a tool shell (wave 18)** is fine with
  `disown`; queue runs behind the lock with `--lock-wait` long enough for
  the runs ahead (`tools/run.sh` takes `LW=`).

- **The targeted ship's radar blip is white (wave 17)**, every other ship
  grey: Tab to a ship off screen and read its blip from `tools/radar.mjs`
  (the `W` blips) to place it.
- **The target is cleared when the target turns hostile (wave 17):** a beam
  on a neutral leaves "No Target" in the panel at once although the ship is
  still there (wave 16's 0x4000 "lost at once" was this). Tab again.
- **Anchored 0x0004 hulls may never fire first (wave 17):** the kit's
  anchored AI 3 Kit Shooter (gövt 362, a 1-damage turret) stayed silent
  beside a Kit Lancer and a Strength-1 hull; wave 13's Kit Disabler (same
  govt, a 1200-damage bolt) fired at once. Check for the first bolt (a shield
  bar drop) before reading anything as self-defence.
- **The board loop cannot reach Kit Range's marker 2102 (wave 17):** it
  stalled about 3,000 px out; rescue rigs need a marker within a screen or
  two of the port.
- **A stopped census loop can leave its next Tab burst queued (wave 17):**
  TaskStop on a `sleep; census` loop killed `ask.mjs` after it had appended
  its keys, so the run still pressed 20 Tabs before `{"done":true}`.

- **Mission ships never send distress calls (wave 16).** Rigs that need
  calls must attack ordinary TRAFFIC (a mission raider at the port among
  traffic traders works); seven mission victims stayed silent.
- **A status line lasts 8 s (wave 16).** `region_lit.mjs` merges
  back-to-back messages into one long stretch (wave 14's "21-25 s");
  `evidence/20261124-w16/tools/sl_changes.mjs` segments the line where its
  lit pattern changes. Ships crossing the line split a segment too: read
  each segment's text.
- **The hail dialog reads a ship's disposition at any range (wave 16):**
  "Status: Hostile" and Beg For Mercy for a hostile ship, no status line and
  Request Assistance for a neutral one; close it with Close Channel
  (window 309,389). An empty BBS answers "There are no missions available
  here." with an Okay dialog that swallows the next Return.
- **Tab cycles every ship in the system, on screen or not (wave 16)**: 30
  Tabs in one keys string, with the target panel's name cut from the
  recording 6 frames after each press (`tools/tab_names.sh`), is a census
  of a stock system.
- **Start `waitready` only after the run has cleared the old outbox (wave
  16):** a waiter started before `run.sh ... fresh-inbox` removed the
  outbox read the PREVIOUS run's "ready" line, and its steps went to an
  inbox that was then deleted (nothing ran; the run was redone).
- **A planet under the player hides ships:** three mission ships placed at
  the port sat under the player's sprite for 15 s after take-off (looked
  cloaked); place ships under test on a marker a little away from the port.


- **Place kit systems apart (wave 15).** The A14 spread treats a system
  that sits at the same map position as a linked system as linked too:
  wave 15's 1510 / 1511 shared positions with 2085 / 2082, and one kill
  changed the records of 2081-2085 as well. Give every rig system its own
  map position.
- **New kit id ranges (wave 15):** every spöb id 2000-2175 was taken, so
  wave 15 opened sÿst / spöb 1500-1599 and shïp 416-699 (README "Id
  limits"). They load and land normally.
- **A düde's hull odds come out uneven (wave 15).** Four equal-odds hulls
  in one düde gave four purple shuttles of six and no azure; three red
  cloakers of five in another system. Count per colour before reading
  anything per hull.
- **A pilot is written only when the player LEAVES a spaceport (again,
  wave 15):** after a jump the arrival point is far from the port, the
  `l l l` landing fails ("You're too far away"), and the pulled pilot is
  the one from the previous take-off. Read records after a landing you
  have seen succeed.
- **Hand-driven runs cannot run loop scripts** (`tab_to`, `board`): the
  interactive step refuses nested scripts. Tab and strip the target
  panel's name (crop 200x22 at 632,332) instead.
- **Shuttles hold their traffic slots (wave 15)**: a system whose traffic
  includes Flags3-0x0002 shuttles fills with them in a few minutes; watch
  traders in a system without shuttles.

- **Count the kills from the pilot (wave 14).** In the A14 spread run a
  press of Space while the panel read "No Target" (a Tab had cycled past
  the last ship) still fired and killed a second trader; the combat
  rating (+4 per kit kill) in the pulled pilot told. Check the panel
  before each shot and read the rating.
- **A contraband pilot that starts in a customs system is scanned before
  it can land (wave 14)**, within the first seconds after Enter Ship, so
  it cannot accept a mission first; with CrimeTol 10 the SmugPenalty then
